title: Partner:in für Social Media & Budgetierung (m/w/d) mit Unternehmensbeteiligung
description:
Dein Schwerpunkt: Marke, Social Media und Community. Dein Einstieg: als Teil des Unternehmens.

Du budgetierst selbst seit Jahren, steckst voller Ideen und hast Lust, eine bestehende Marke unternehmerisch weiterzuentwickeln? Bei BeginnerBudget kannst du deine Erfahrung einbringen, das Gesicht der Marke werden und dich am Unternehmen beteiligen.

Wir suchen eine Person, die gemeinsam mit uns in die nächste Phase von BeginnerBudget geht und dabei die operative Verantwortung für unseren Markenauftritt übernimmt. Die Unternehmensbeteiligung ist ein fester Bestandteil der angestrebten Zusammenarbeit. Wie wir deinen Einstieg, die Beteiligung und deine Vergütung gestalten, besprechen wir persönlich.

Über BeginnerBudget

Bei BeginnerBudget dreht sich alles um Budgetierung und die passenden Produkte dafür. Hinter der Marke steht aktuell ein fünfköpfiges Team.

Wir als Gründer möchten uns aus dem operativen Tagesgeschäft stärker zurückziehen und den nächsten Entwicklungsschritt gemeinsam mit dir gestalten. Du bekommst den Raum, die Marke mit eigenen Ideen zu prägen und Entscheidungen zu treffen. Wir unterstützen dich im Hintergrund mit unserer Erfahrung und bei der Umsetzung.

Deine Rolle

Du wirst das Gesicht von BeginnerBudget und übernimmst die Führung unserer Kommunikation nach außen. Social Media ist dabei dein wichtigster Aufgabenbereich:

  • Du entwickelst unsere Social-Media-Präsenz weiter, planst Inhalte und setzt sie selbst um.

  • Du stehst vor der Kamera und machst Budgetierung verständlich, persönlich und alltagsnah.

  • Du bist im Austausch mit unserer Community, hörst zu und bringst ihre Bedürfnisse in die Weiterentwicklung der Marke ein.

  • Du entwickelst eigene Ideen für Produkte, Inhalte und Aktionen.

  • Du gestaltest den Markenauftritt und entscheidest mit unternehmerischem Blick, was BeginnerBudget voranbringt.

Du erhältst weitreichende Entscheidungsfreiheit. Wenn du mit der Zeit weitere Bereiche des Unternehmens übernehmen möchtest, arbeiten wir dich Schritt für Schritt ein.

Das bringst du mit

  • Eigene Budgetierungserfahrung: Du beschäftigst dich seit mehreren Jahren damit und kennst die Herausforderungen aus deinem Alltag.

  • Freude an Social Media: Du kannst Inhalte entwickeln und umsetzen und fühlst dich vor der Kamera wohl.

  • Unternehmerischen Antrieb: Du möchtest Verantwortung übernehmen, eigene Entscheidungen treffen und etwas langfristig aufbauen.

  • Nähe zur Community: Du kannst zuhören, verständlich erklären und mit Menschen ins Gespräch kommen.

  • Zeit und Verbindlichkeit: Du kannst dich mindestens in Teilzeit einbringen und BeginnerBudget kontinuierlich voranbringen.

Das bringen wir ein

Du steigst bei BeginnerBudget in eine bestehende Marke mit einem eingespielten, fünfköpfigen Team ein. Unser Team übernimmt die weiteren operativen Bereiche: Grafikdesign und gestalterische Umsetzung, das Management unseres Shopify-Shops, der angebundenen Systeme und Marktplätze sowie den Kundensupport. Auch Produktentwicklung, Beschaffung, die Zusammenarbeit mit Lieferanten, Werbung und die Automatisierung interner Prozesse decken wir ab.

Deine Ideen für neue Produkte entwickeln wir gemeinsam weiter und kümmern uns um die Umsetzung.

So kannst du dich beim Einstieg auf Marke, Content und Community konzentrieren und zugleich auf die Erfahrung des Teams zurückgreifen.

Du bekommst echten Gestaltungsspielraum, eine Unternehmensbeteiligung und die Möglichkeit, langfristig immer mehr Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Die Zusammenarbeit ist remote auf selbstständiger Basis vorgesehen.

Lass uns kennenlernen

Erzähl uns, wie du selbst budgetierst, warum du BeginnerBudget mitgestalten möchtest und welche Erfahrungen du mit Social Media mitbringst. Verlinke gerne eigene Kanäle oder Beispiele deiner Inhalte.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich und deine Ideen kennenzulernen.

title: (Senior) Customer Success Manager:in SaaS Energiewirtschaft (w/m/d) - Remote
description:
Was Dich erwartet

Als Teil unseres Customer Success Teams stehst Du in direktem Kontakt mit unseren Kunden und Software-Nutzern aus dem Bereich der kaufmännischen Betriebsführung von Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen. Du begleitest eigenständig neue Kunden durch einen strukturieren Einrichtungsprozess der Software opti.node und stellst so sicher, dass sie den größtmöglichen Nutzen aus der Anwendung ziehen können. Die Anforderungen unserer Kunden sind oftmals anspruchsvoll und nicht selten innovativ - in diesen Fällen bist du nicht auf dich alleine gestellt, sondern hast hoch qualifizierte Kolleg:innen aus allen Bereichen, mit denen offene Fragen und neue Herausforderungen besprochen und gelöst werden können.

node.energy ermöglicht mit klugen Software-as-a-Service-Lösungen professionellen Betreibern von Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen neue Geschäftsmodelle ganz einfach umzusetzen und damit profitabel zu bleiben. Hierfür führt opti.node alle Daten für die kaufmännische Betriebsführung von Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen zusammen und automatisiert anspruchsvolle Verwaltungsaufgaben und energiewirtschaftliche Geschäftsprozesse. Bereits heute vertrauen Betreiber von mehr als 14.000 Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen, die mehr als ein Drittel des deutschen Grünstroms erzeugen, auf opti.node.

Wir suchen dich als (Senior) Customer Success Manager:in (w/m/d) in Voll- oder Teilzeit zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Frankfurt am Main, Freiburg oder remote. Wir sind sehr gespannt, auf deine Bewerbung. Einfach klicken und abschicken!

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du organisierst das perfekte Onboarding für unsere neuen Kunden und begleitest sie durch den Prozess in unserer Software

  • Du betreust unsere Kunden aus dem Bereich der kaufmännischen Betriebsführung für Wind- und Solarparks und hast hierbei keine Berührungsängste mit rechtlich-regulatorischen Themen

  • Du erklärst Kunden, wie sie opti.node optimal nutzen können und hörst dabei genau hin, um weitere Anforderungen und Wünsche zu erkennen

  • Du hältst auch nach dem erfolgreichen Onboarding regelmäßig Kontakt zu Kunden, um neue Funktionen in opti.node zu erläutern und weitere Anknüpfungspunkte zur Zusammenarbeit zu besprechen

  • Du bist das Gesicht zu unseren Kunden, kennst und löst ihre individuellen Herausforderungen und führst sie so zum Erfolg

  • Du arbeitest eng mit dem Produktmanagement, den Product Ownern und dem Sales-Team zusammen, um Anforderungen von Kunden zu bewerten und neue Funktionen zu spezifizieren

Was Du mitbringen solltest

  • Du bringst einen energiewirtschaftlichen Studienhintergrund oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung mit und hast Kenntnisse in mindestens einem der folgenden Themenfelder:

  1. Erfahrung in Direktvermarktung, Energiehandel, Energiedienstleistungen o.ä.

  2. Energiewirtschaftliche Abgaben & Privilegierungen oder Meldepflichten

  3. Kenntnisse in energiewirtschaftlichen Prozessen und Abläufen zwischen verschiedenen Marktakteuren wie Netzbetreibern, Messstellenbetreibern, Lieferanten etc.

  • Du hast bereits Erfahrung im Customer Success gesammelt, hast Freude an der Interaktion mit B2B-Kunden und kannst Dich in andere hineinversetzen

  • Du hast Freude am Lösen komplexer Aufgaben, arbeitest Dich gerne tief ein und willst (technische) Prozesse verstehen und hinterfragen

  • Du arbeitest gerne mit digitalen Tools (Hubspot, Confluence, Miro, Teams und unserer eigenen Software) und bist für Excel immer zu haben

  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf C2 Niveau (unsere Unternehmenssprache) und besitzt gute Englischkenntnisse

Was Du sonst noch bekommst

  • Job mit Sinn: Wir treiben gemeinsam die grüne Energiewende voran

  • Nachhaltige und flexible Arbeitsbedingungen: Unbefristeter Arbeitsertrag, ein ordentliches Gehalt, 30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr, Remote-First-Kultur mit Büros in Frankfurt a. M. und Freiburg - von wo aus du arbeitest, entscheidest du

  • Strukturierte Einarbeitung: Du bekommst eine strukturierte Einarbeitung, begleitet durch eine:n Mentor:in und eine:n Kolleg:in als Social Buddy für deine soziale Integration bei node.energy

  • Mitgestaltungsmöglichkeiten: Du wirkst aktiv an der stetigen Entwicklung unseres Unternehmens mit und das ohne starre Prozesse, hierarchische Strukturen oder veraltete Technologien

  • Weiterbildung: Jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget und regelmäßige Feedbackgespräche zur Förderung deiner individuellen Entwicklung

  • Persönliche Treffen: Monatliche Teamtage und jährige Teamevents vor Ort zur persönlichen Zusammenarbeit und Vernetzung - diese sind aber freiwillig

  • Workation: Nach der Probezeit hast du die Möglichkeit, im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Bestimmungen temporär an einem Ort innerhalb der EU zu arbeiten

  • Eine Vielzahl weiterer Benefits: Bahncard, Bezuschussung des Job-Tickets, Bikeleasing, Urban Sports Club/Hansefit, nilo.health Zugang und betriebliche Altersvorsorge

title: Financial Controller (w/m/d)
description:
Tangany mit Sitz in München ist ein innovatives Technologieunternehmen mit einer marktführenden B2B-Lösung für die Verwahrung digitaler Vermögenswerte (z. B. Kryptowährungen, Stablecoins und anderen tokenisierten Vermögenswerten) in Blockchain-Netzwerken. Unsere Lösung wird bereits von mehr als 50 institutionellen Kunden eingesetzt. Als lizenziertes Finanzinstitut wird die Tangany GmbH von der BaFin reguliert.

Für unser anhaltendes Wachstum suchen wir einen Financial Controller (w/m/d) zur Verstärkung unseres Teams.

Deine Rolle

Du verantwortest das Controlling und die Finanzsteuerung und berichtest an das Management Board.

Das Team ist klein. Deine Expertise und dein Beitrag wirken sich unmittelbar aus: Du arbeitest mit unserer Accountant und unserer Steuerkanzlei z.B. an Themen wie Finanzbuchhaltung, Lohn und Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung; die formale Verantwortung für das Rechnungswesen liegt bei der Geschäftsleitung, Zahlungen geben wir im Vier-Augen-Prinzip frei. In diesem Rahmen bist du die Person, die weiß, wo die Zahlen stehen, warum sie dort stehen und wie sich Ergebnis, Kosten, Liquidität und Eigenmittel entwickeln werden.

Der Kern der Rolle hat zwei Seiten: die regulatorische Pflicht und eine Steuerung, mit der wir jede Finanzfrage jederzeit in wenigen Minuten beantworten können. Business Cases und Investor Reporting kommen dazu und wachsen mit dir.

Heute arbeiten wir vor allem mit DATEV Unternehmen Online und Tableau. Die Steuerung darauf baust du zu großen Teilen neu auf, gern AI-gestützt: Unser AI-Dev-Team setzt mit dir Live-Reporting, Abstimmungen und ein Finanz-Cockpit um.

Aufgaben

  • Den Jahresabschluss nach HGB und RechKredV erstellen, ergänzt um die RechZahlV-Posten für unser Zahlungsgeschäft, und die Prüfung gemeinsam mit unserer Steuerkanzlei und Abschlussprüfer durchführen.

  • Das aufsichtsrechtliche Meldewesen führen und Finanzinformationen nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben unter Begleitung des Compliance-Teams bereitstellen.

  • Regulatorische Planzahlen, etwa die Eigenmittelanforderung, aus der Bilanzplanung ableiten und in Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsleitung laufend überwachen.

  • Cashflow- und Runway-Planung führen und Finanzierungsbedarf früh sichtbar machen.

  • Liquiditäts- und Kontrahentenrisiken in das unternehmensweite Risikocontrolling einbringen und laufend überwachen.

  • Business Cases und Rentabilitätsrechnungen erstellen und Investor-Updates vorbereiten.

  • Eine Kostenstellenstruktur aufbauen, Budgets je Kostenstelle mit den Verantwortlichen festlegen, Kosten, Budgets und KPIs laufend überwachen sowie Live-Reporting und Ad-hoc-Auswertungen für Geschäftsleitung und Budgetverantwortliche bereitstellen und Plan-Ist-Abweichungen analysieren.

  • Aus der Praxiserfahrung heraus Input liefern, um Finanzprozesse, Tools und das interne Kontrollsystem gemeinsam mit unserem AI-Dev-Team auszubauen.

Wen wir suchen

  • Du bist Controller:in (idealerweise aus einem regulierten Institut) und hast Jahresabschluss und Meldewesen selbst verantwortet.

  • Abweichungen erkennst du früh: Wenn sich Eigenmittel, Liquidität oder Kosten in die falsche Richtung bewegen, liegt deine Analyse mit Optionen auf dem Tisch, solange noch Zeit zum Handeln ist.

  • Deine Forecasts halten auch Monate später, und wo sie abweichen, kannst du erklären, warum.

  • Meldefristen und Prüfungsanforderungen baust du so in die Abläufe ein, dass vor dem Stichtag keine Ad-hoc Aktion nötig ist.

  • Prüfer und Risikocontrolling nehmen deine Zahlen als Ausgangspunkt.

  • Stellt die Geschäftsleitung eine Finanzfrage, kannst du schnell und problemlos Antworten geben, weil deine Daten und Auswertungen genau dafür gebaut sind.

  • Du entscheidest auch mit unvollständigen Informationen, sagst klar, wenn etwas nicht geht, und stellst einen Prozess um, sobald er nicht mehr passt.

Qualifikation

Must-Haves

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium oder Ausbildung in Finanzen, Controlling oder einem verwandten Feld.

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung im Controlling oder Rechnungswesen, idealerweise in einem regulierten Institut (nach KWG, ZAG oder MiCAR) oder in der Prüfung entsprechender Institute.

  • Eigenständig erstellte Jahresabschlüsse nach HGB, sowie Erfahrung mit Liquiditäts- und Kontrahentenrisiken sowie Risikotragfähigkeit.

  • Aufbau von Kostenstellenrechnung und Management-Reporting, sicherer Umgang mit DATEV, Excel und Google Sheets inklusive Finanzmodellen und deren Visualisierung, idealerweise mit einem BI-Tool wie Tableau.

  • Offenheit: Reporting mit AI-Werkzeugen neu aufsetzen.

  • Fließend Deutsch und Englisch (C1 oder höher).

Nice-to-Haves

  • Erfahrung mit MiCAR, etwa der Eigenmittelberechnung.

  • FP&A, Business Cases oder Investor-Reporting in einem wachsenden Unternehmen.

  • Erfahrung im aufsichtsrechtlichen Meldewesen nach KWG oder ZAG.

  • Interesse an Krypto und Tokenisierung.

Benefits

Flexibilität & Work-Life-Balance:

  • 30 Tage Urlaub, dazu jeweils ein halber Tag frei an Heiligabend und Silvester, und bei Bedarf zusätzlicher unbezahlter Urlaub, um die Akkus wieder aufzuladen.

  • Zusätzlicher bezahlter Urlaub für frischgebackene Eltern.

  • Die Freiheit, von zu Hause oder in unserem schönen Büro mitten in München zu arbeiten.

  • Möglichkeit einer Workation, um auch auf Reisen zu arbeiten.

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Du arbeitest, wenn du am produktivsten bist.

Deine Entwicklung:

  • Es startet mit dem ersten Tag: Mit unserem auf deine Bedürfnisse zugeschnittenen Onboarding erhältst du einen strukturierten Einarbeitungsplan und Feedbackgespräche während der Probezeit (und natürlich auch danach).

  • Wir wachsen und möchten, dass du mit uns wächst! Werde zum Blockchain-Experten, tausche dich mit unserem hochmotivierten Team aus und bilde dich in individuellen Trainings weiter.

  • Regelmäßige Feedback-Gespräche: Zweimal im Jahr evaluieren wir gemeinsam mit deinen Karriereweg und leiten die nächsten Schritte in die richtige Richtung ein.

Entlohnung und Zusatzleistungen

  • Ein attraktives, marktkonformes Jahresgehalt.

  • Spaß bei der Arbeit: eine Runde mit Kolleg:innen an unserer Tischtennisplatte, ein Feierabendgetränk auf unserer großartigen Dachterrasse und unsere Team-Events.

Motivierte Mitarbeitende sind der Schlüssel zum Erfolg. Deshalb bieten wir dir über Hrmony flexible, digitale Benefits, die dich im Alltag unterstützen. Du erhältst ein monatliches Budget, das du nach deinen Bedürfnissen aufteilst:

  • Essenszuschuss: für Lebensmittel, Restaurants oder Lieferdienste

  • Mobilitätsbudget: z. B. für das Deutschlandticket

  • Sachbezüge: flexibel nutzbar für Streaming, Fitness, Shopping und mehr

Werde Teil unseres Teams und revolutioniere gemeinsam mit uns den traditionellen Finanzmarkt. Nutze die Chance und gestalte die Zukunft der Branche aktiv mit. Bewirb dich jetzt und sei Teil unserer innovativen Reise, um Blockchain-Technologie für jeden zugänglich zu machen.

title: Head of Operations
description:
Über Fahrengold

Wir bei Fahrengold entwickeln, konstruieren und vermarkten hochwertige Designgaragen und innovative Präsentationslösungen für exklusive Fahrzeuge. Dabei verbinden wir anspruchsvolles Design, technische Innovation und höchste Qualitätsstandards.

An unserem Hauptstandort in Berlin-Marzahn befinden sich unsere Verwaltung sowie die Endmontage und Vorbereitung der Auslieferung unserer Produkte. Mit einem internationalen Kunden- und Partnernetzwerk treiben wir die Weiterentwicklung und Skalierung unseres Unternehmens voran.

Ihre neue Herausforderung

Für die Position des Head of Operations (w/m/d) suchen wir eine erfahrene, unternehmerisch denkende Führungspersönlichkeit, die unsere operativen Strukturen weiterentwickelt, internationale Produktionskapazitäten aufbaut und unsere Prozesse nachhaltig optimiert.

Sie übernehmen eine zentrale Rolle bei der Weiterentwicklung unseres Unternehmens und gestalten die operative Skalierung von Fahrengold aktiv mit.


Ihr Beitrag zu unserer Erfolgsgeschichte

  • Operative Gesamtverantwortung: Steuerung und Weiterentwicklung der Bereiche Produktentwicklung, Supply Chain, Produktion, Auslieferung und After-Sales-Service.

  • Internationale Produktionsstrukturen: Strategische Planung, Aufbau und Skalierung internationaler Produktionsstandorte und Fertigungslinien unter Berücksichtigung von Wirtschaftlichkeit, Qualität und Effizienz.

  • Prozessoptimierung und Digitalisierung: Analyse und kontinuierliche Verbesserung bestehender Wertschöpfungsprozesse sowie Einführung effizienter, digital gestützter Systeme und Abläufe.

  • Produktions- und Qualitätsmanagement: Sicherstellung der Produktionsziele, Liefertermine und Qualitätsstandards sowie Entwicklung und Überwachung relevanter KPIs.

  • Führung und Personalentwicklung: Aktive Führung, Förderung und Weiterentwicklung der Mitarbeitenden im Bereich Operations.

  • Lieferantenmanagement: Auswahl, Verhandlung und Steuerung nationaler und internationaler Lieferanten, Produktionspartner und Dienstleister.

title: TUM Project Study: Earned LinkedIn Media for Enterprise
description:
About us

Mediacharge GmbH is a Munich-based, internationally oriented marketing agency with ten years of experience in cutting-edge marketing for international enterprises. Operating in 14 languages, we combine first-tier strategic consulting with hands-on operational excellence, measured against business results.

Project description (TUM Project)

This project study explores what turns an enterprise’s own people into LinkedIn voices that measurably drive Sales, Recruiting or Employer Brand. Using Mediacharge and its enterprise clients as the case environment, it examines how earned media, meaning content published by real people rather than paid brand channels, creates business impact.

The project combines a business strategy perspective - objectives, the right people and measurable outcomes - with a content and platform perspective, focusing on talent profiles, content types, success patterns and the time it takes to build an effective voice.

Objectives of the project study

  • to classify enterprise objectives for earned LinkedIn media (Sales, Recruiting, Employer Brand),

  • to identify which talent profiles and content types work best for each objective,

  • to derive success patterns, including what it takes and how long it takes to see results,

  • to develop one strategy blueprint per objective and an impact model to measure business effect.

Main task and methodology

Students explore the topic through research, interviews and real enterprise cases (month 1), classify goals, talent profiles and success patterns (month 2), and build strategy blueprints, a final report and a pitch to Mediacharge leadership (month 3). Recommended methods include desk research, expert interviews, enterprise case analysis, benchmarking and impact modelling.

Student requirements

Students are fascinated by marketing at international enterprise scale, work analytically and build things that hold up in practice. Strong results open the door to a next conversation with Mediacharge.

Project scope and application

Preferred scope: 3 months in three phases: Explore, Analyse, Build

Number of students: 3–5

Supervision: A Mediacharge supervisor with direct input from enterprise practice; final pitch to leadership

Client access: Mediacharge enterprise clients, on request and case by case

Research budget: €2,000, released for a defined purpose agreed with the supervisor

title: Founding Recruiter (m/f/x)
description:
01 · Why this role exists

Invest in Values. Produce in Freedom. Boost Europe.

Behind every megawatt hour our clients save, there are people who make it happen. RIZM helps Europe's largest industrial companies – together around 2% of Europe's total energy demand – make their energy decisions with AI. Our agent RIZMO works as a digital colleague. But the most important colleagues are the ones we haven't found yet.

That's your job. We're about 15 people today and growing fast. There is no recruiting playbook yet, no big HR department and no "that's how we've always done it". You'll write the playbook. Not as application admin, but as the person who shapes who RIZM becomes.

02 · Hi, we're Diana and Josh – we'll be working together

I'm Diana, 20, I study civil engineering in Münster and I currently run recruiting at RIZM on my own, 20 hours a week. That's not enough for what's ahead of us, which is why we're looking for you. We'll build this together, side by side in our Münster office. Josh, our co-founder & CBO, comes from statistics and risk management and will be your sparring partner whenever you need one – for tricky candidates, for offers and for figuring out who we need next. Got questions before you apply? Just message me on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/diana-pashaian-1637133b2/

03 · What you'll do

  • Build the team of tomorrow: Design our recruiting from scratch – roles, workflows, tools – and later bring more recruiters and sourcers on board yourself.

  • Find the right people: Track down engineers, energy experts and product people via LinkedIn, Juicebox, universities, communities and your own network.

  • Win people over: Lead first conversations, tell our story convincingly and make sure every candidate feels well looked after – even when it's a no.

  • Make it smart: Automate sequences, screening and reporting with AI instead of maintaining spreadsheets.

  • Steer by numbers: Always know where the funnel gets stuck – and turn the right dials.

  • Get us seen: Shape how RIZM is perceived as an employer – careers page, job ads, events, university partnerships.

04 · What you bring

  • Experience: You've worked in recruiting or talent acquisition, ideally in startups or tech, and you know how to approach technical profiles.

  • People sense: You spot potential even when it's not on the CV, and you talk to engineers as equals.

  • Tech affinity: You try out new tools, build your own workflows and enjoy making things faster.

  • Builder drive: You don't want to step into ready-made structures – you want to create them, independently, reliably and fast.

  • Background: A degree in psychology, business, HR, social sciences or similar – or a path that prepared you just as well.

  • Languages: Fluent German and English, written and spoken.

05 · What you get

  • Performance counts: Uncapped variable pay plus equity – good work is visible here and rewarded directly.

  • Real ownership: You're the first recruiter. What you build stays.

  • A network that moves you forward: Sparring, mentoring and learning with the networks of our investors Point 9 and Earlybird.

  • Once a year, we get out: A team workation with everyone, including conversations with inspiring guests like Robert Habeck, Kitty Mayo or James Vincent.

  • Stay fit: Urban Sports Club membership.

  • Münster office: You sit right next to our engineering team – the people you'll hire most – and you hear first-hand what makes a great engineer at RIZM. Recruiting thrives on short distances – the best ideas come up at the same table.

06 · How to apply

A cover letter is required. Keep it short and answer two questions: Why are you exactly the right fit for RIZM? And what is your biggest achievement in HR or recruiting so far?

title: TYPO3 Developer
description:
TYPO3 Developer
(Mensch)

Andere zählen Schafe. Du zählst TYPO3-Major-Versionen, die du schon migriert hast. Und hast Lust, die Websites großer, internationaler Unternehmen technisch zu verantworten?

Zur Übersicht

Der ultimative TYPO3-Check

Du bist bei uns richtig, wenn du…

  • … bei „Wir brauchen nur ein kleines Feld mehr im Backend“ im Kopf schon TCA, Datenbank-Migration und die drei Fluid-Templates aufklappst, die es wirklich braucht.

  • … für dein wichtigstes Werkzeug hältst. Direkt nach dem Cache-Leeren.

  • … beim Satz „Das ging in TYPO3 v7 aber noch“ freundlich lächelst und den Extension Scanner startest.

  • … sofort merkst, wenn dir die KI eine TypoScript-Lösung aus dem Jahr 2014 andreht. Und sie trotzdem jeden Tag nutzt, weil sie dich schneller macht.

  • … und dein Gewissen dir verbietet, freitags um 16 Uhr ein Major-Update auf Production zu schieben. Auch nicht „nur schnell“.

… dann gilt für uns nur noch eins: composer require netfed/du

Worum geht es?

Du verantwortest die TYPO3-Technik großer Corporate-Websites. Von der Aufwandsschätzung über Konzeption und Neuaufbau bis zu Weiterentwicklung, Support und Updates. Du berätst Kolleg:innen und Kunden und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Projekte auf einem sauberen technischen Fundament stehen.

Warum diese Rolle bei uns anders ist?

Wir arbeiten für namhafte Konzerne und große Mittelständler, bei denen die Website ein strategisches Aushängeschild ist. Du baust hier nicht Website Nummer 47 nach Schema F. Du triffst die technischen Entscheidungen und verantwortest die Architektur. Dabei vertrauen wir voll auf deine Erfahrung. Dazu kommen eine eigene, von uns betriebene Cloud-Hosting-Umgebung und eine gelebte DevOps-Kultur, die sich am Stand der Technik orientiert.

Und was ist mit KI?

Gehört bei uns zum Alltag. Nicht als Pilotprojekt, sondern als Werkzeug. title: Senior Fraud & Risk Analyst (f/m/x)
description:
Your Mission

This is a company built for growth.

When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone. We move fast, cut the noise, and focus on what actually matters, because in our industry, speed wins.

With 50M+ platform downloads, we’re rapidly scaling one of the most exciting innovations in mobile gaming: a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps players discover, and engage with games they enjoy - creating lasting value for both players and gaming studios.

As a Senior Fraud Analyst, you'll join our Fraud Analytics team as a close partner to our Fraud Analytics Team Lead - someone who can operate independently, mentor other team members, and help shape the fraud and risk agenda as the team and company scale.

You'll work cross-functionally with different teams, dig into fraud patterns across our platform, and build the processes we don't have yet. It's a highly visible, high-ownership role in a fast-growing company.

What You'll Own:

  • Strategic partnership: Partner directly with the Fraud Analytics Team Lead on strategy, ideation, and day-to-day problem solving - acting as a sounding board, ready to step in and keep things moving when needed.
  • Reporting uplift: Drive the evolution of fraud and risk reporting, turning raw data into sharp, decision-ready insights.
  • Fraud trend analysis: Hunt down patterns across our user base, shape the detection logic and rules that keep us ahead of bad actors, monitor how those rules perform, and optimise them over time.
  • Process ownership: Own the design of fraud and risk processes end-to-end, spotting gaps and building what doesn't exist yet.
  • Experimentation: Test, learn, and iterate - running A/B tests to continuously sharpen our fraud prevention strategies.
  • Strategic thinking: Think beyond the day-to-day, helping define where fraud and risk management goes next as the team scales.
  • Mentorship & collaboration: Mentor teammates and partner cross-functionally with Tech, Data, Product, Support, and Finance - becoming a go-to person others rely on.

What You Bring

  • Fraud & risk experience: 5+ years in fraud, risk management, or a closely related financial risk function; direct fraud experience is a strong plus, ideally in gaming or another B2C/app-based industry.
  • Data & AI fluency: Comfort working with data - SQL, databases, and hands-on experience using AI tools for analysis and prompting.
  • Analytical mindset: Strong analytical skills and genuine comfort with numbers, paired with the ability to turn analysis into clear, actionable reporting.
  • Strategic contribution: Experience contributing to or developing risk/fraud strategy, not just executing existing processes — including running A/B tests to validate ideas.
  • Collaboration & mentorship: Experience mentoring or supporting colleagues, and working cross-functionally across different stakeholder perspectives.
  • Education: A relevant Bachelor's or Master's degree (Business, Finance, Accounting, Data/Mathematics, Engineering, or similar).
  • Language: Fluent English, written and spoken.

Nice to have:

  • Background in policy design or risk governance frameworks.
  • Relevant certifications such as CFE, CFCS, CAMS, CRISC, CFA, and/or FRM.
  • Working knowledge of relevant regulatory frameworks - e.g. GDPR, PSD2/SCA, AML/KYC principles, and PCI-DSS basics where payment data is processed.

How We Win

  • Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
  • Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
  • See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
  • Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
  • Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.

Please note: this is not a remote only position, we offer you a flexible hybrid model here in Hamburg, Germany - working from home on Mondays & Fridays, coming to the office on Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday!

Own a piece of the product, not a ticket queue

ilert is the alerting, on-call and incident response platform that engineering teams worldwide rely on when things break. That covers alerting, on-call scheduling, call routing, status pages, and an AI SRE that investigates incidents alongside the people responding to them.

We're bootstrapped, profitable, and small (~15 engineers). Your work reaches customers fast, and you have a real say in what gets built.

We're looking for a Product Engineer to own one area of that product. We'll give you a domain, not a spec. You figure out what customers need, build it across the stack, ship it, and check whether it made a difference.

We build with AI every day. But AI is leverage on top of engineering, not a substitute for it. We're looking for a solid engineer first, someone who uses AI to move faster, not to skip understanding the code.

Tasks

  • Own a product domain end-to-end. Depending on where you'll have the most impact, that could be alerting, on-call and call routing, status pages, integrations, or our AI SRE. You propose what to build, build it, and measure whether it worked.
  • Ship across the stack. Java and Rust on the backend, React and TypeScript on the frontend. We work in 2-week bets that end in a production deploy.
  • Talk to customers. Join customer calls, read support conversations, dig into usage data, and turn what you learn into product improvements.
  • Make the scope calls. Decide what to cut, what ships first, and what to validate before building it. We trust you with these trade-offs.
  • Own it in production. You're responsible for what you ship, including when it breaks. Reliability is literally our product.

What you bring

  • 2+ years of software engineering in a team codebase. That means code review, tests, production incidents, and code you didn't write alone. Side projects are great, but they don't replace this.
  • You've shipped features end-to-end and cared whether people actually used them.
  • Comfortable across the stack. Strong on one side, and willing and able to work on the other.
  • Solid fundamentals. Data modeling, debugging, testing, and thinking through failure modes. You can read unfamiliar code and reason about it before you reach for a prompt.
  • Real AI fluency. You use AI coding tools every day, you know where they help and where they mislead, and you can defend a design decision without "the AI suggested it."
  • Product instinct. You have opinions about what to build, not just how.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity. A domain and a problem are enough for you to get going.
  • Fluent English (our working language).
  • Able to be in our Cologne office 3 days a week.

Bonus

  • Experience at a B2B SaaS or developer-tools company
  • Exposure to incident management, DevOps, SRE or on-call, or just real curiosity about it. The domain is learnable; we care more about how you build.
  • Hands-on with Java, Rust, React or TypeScript
  • Something you built that other people actually use (open source, a side project, an internal tool)
  • German language skills

Benefits

  • 🧭 Real Ownership: You decide what to build in your domain, not just how to build it.
  • ⚡ Ship Fast, See Impact: 2-week cycles with production deploys. Your work reaches customers in weeks, not quarters.
  • 🤖 AI in Production: Build on and next to an AI SRE that investigates real incidents for real customers. Human-AI collaboration in production, not a demo.
  • 🏡 Hybrid Freedom: Our office in Cologne Rheinauhafen with a roof terrace (3 days/week), plus work from home on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
  • 🌴 Focus > Meetings: We protect maker time, write things down async (Notion, Loom), and keep meetings rare.
  • 🎯 Direct Line to the Founders: You report to the CTO and work directly with the CEO on what to build.
  • 💪 Independent and Stable: Bootstrapped and profitable. We build for customers, not for the next funding round.

How to apply

No cover letter needed. Send your CV along with:

  1. One link to something you shipped and are proud of (a product, a feature, a repo or a write-up), plus a sentence on what your part in it was.
  2. A few lines on which part of ilert you'd want to own first, and why.

If you're the kind of engineer who has opinions about what to build, not just how to build it, we want to talk to you.

title: Staff Data Scientist, Pricing
description:
Help Us Build The Future of Travel

At Airalo, we're making it easier for people to stay connected wherever they travel. As the world's first eSIM store, we help millions of travelers access affordable mobile data in 200+ countries and regions around the world.

Today, we're a team of 400+ people across 60+ countries, building a product used by travelers every day. We've grown quickly, but we've worked hard to keep what matters: trust, ownership, and the freedom for people to do great work without unnecessary layers or bureaucracy.

We're fully remote by design, genuinely global, and united by a shared mission to make travel simpler for everyone.

We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Pricing to build the analytical and machine learning capability that pricing runs on, from demand modelling through to the systems that recommend price.

You won't be starting from zero. We've invested in the foundational data and infrastructure that pricing decisions depend on. What's missing is the capability on top: models the business trusts, experiments that settle pricing questions with evidence, and economics defined once so they hold consistently across Commercial, Product and the customer experience.

The arc of the role runs from measurement to prediction to prescription - understanding how demand responds to price, forecasting how it will respond, and ultimately building the models that recommend the price itself.


What You'll Do:

  • Build and own the demand and elasticity modelling capability, quantifying how price affects volume across destination, duration, data tier, and customer segment.

  • Develop machine learning models for demand forecasting and willingness-to-pay, and take them from exploration through to production with the monitoring and retraining that keeps them honest.

  • Move us from predictive to prescriptive by building the optimisation layer that turns forecasts and elasticities into recommended prices under margin, competitive and partner constraints.

  • Design and analyse pricing experiments with statistical rigour, and apply causal methods where clean randomisation isn't possible.

  • Define pricing within our data ecosystem, owning the governed definitions of price, cost and package economics that reporting, analysis and product surfaces all read from.

  • Partner with Commercial and Finance to connect pricing decisions to margin and revenue, and to size opportunities before we commit.

  • Set the analytical standard for pricing at Airalo, from what counts as evidence through to how a model or recommendation gets validated before it influences live pricing.


    • What You'll Bring:

  • 7+ years in data science, quantitative economics, or applied research, including pricing, monetisation, or marketplace economics work that demonstrably changed decisions.

  • Experience with dynamic or algorithmic pricing systems in production.

  • An advanced degree in Econometrics, Statistics, Operations Research or similar, or equivalent applied depth in demand estimation and the identification problems that make naive price-quantity regressions wrong.

  • Hands-on machine learning experience across the full lifecycle, from feature engineering and model selection through to deployment

  • Familiarity with optimisation and decision-science methods that turn predictions into recommended actions, whether through constrained optimisation, bandits, or reinforcement learning approaches.

  • Proven experimentation expertise, having designed and defended experiments with a clear view on decision frameworks and common failure modes.

  • Experience building analytical capability where none existed before, turning raw data and a business question into something a commercial team uses repeatedly.

  • Strong data modelling instincts, thinking in reusable definitions and single sources of truth rather than standalone analyses.

  • The ability to move comfortably between financial, product and operational data and connect the analysis to a financial outcome.

  • Genuine partnership instincts, translating between analytical rigour and commercial reality so that Commercial and Product come to you early rather than after the decision.

  • Fluency in the Python ML stack alongside strong SQL, with the engineering hygiene to hand over code that others can run and maintain.

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to make a methodological argument to people who won't check your standard errors.

  • A self-starter mindset that thrives in ambiguity and brings structure without waiting for permission.

  • Comfort using AI tools to augment analytical work, with a point of view on where they help and where they don't


    • Nice to have:

  • Experience in marketplace, telecom, travel, or subscription/usage-based businesses.

  • Bayesian or hierarchical modelling for sparse segments and long-tail SKUs.

  • Competitive price response modelling, or working with scraped competitor pricing data.

  • Familiarity with dbt, LightDash, or similar semantic/BI layers.

  • Experience designing semantic or metric layers consumed by both analytics and production systems.

  • Experience working in cross-functional teams spanning commercial, finance and product disciplines.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

Why we're hiring

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

 

About the role

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

  • Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

  • Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

  • Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

  • Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

  • Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

  • Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

 

What this role isn't

  • An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

  • A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

  • A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

  • A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

  • A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

 

What success looks like

In your first 90 days:

  • The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

  • Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

  • You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

  • Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

  • At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

  • We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

  • You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

  • The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

  • Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

  • Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

 

About you

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

  • You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

  • You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

  • You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

  • You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

  • You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

 

How you will grow

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

 

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

  • 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

  • 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

  • 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

  • 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

  • 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

 

The environment

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

How we build (worth reading before the role)

How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.

We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.

We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

 

About the role

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.

Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.

That's also what makes it exciting.

You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.

Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.

Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product".

Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.

 

What matters most

We need all of these at once:

  • Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.

  • Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea.

  • Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked.

  • Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see.

  • Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features.

  • Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's.

And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it.

  • Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution.

  • Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense.

  • Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built.

  • Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst.

  • Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck.

 

About you

You'll likely thrive here if:

  • You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention.

  • You've worked on the commercial side as well as the product side: a P&L, a supplier or partner relationship, pricing, or a whole service line.

  • You're comfortable enough with data and code to unblock yourself.

Nice-to-haves:

  • You were a software engineer before you moved into product.

  • You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces.

  • You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off.

This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned.

 

How we work

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you.

Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first.

We're office-first, near Farringdon. We do a lot of our best thinking together and being in the same room helps, though we're pragmatic about heads-down work when you need it.

At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.

The opportunity

You’ll be the keeper of the player experience on our hybrid casual RPG. Combat, heroes, art, and features all come together in the levels you build, and you decide whether that adds up to something players want to come back to.

You’ll join a small, AI-native game team on its way to launch. You’ll own the level design area completely: you set the roadmap, make the calls, and ship. A dedicated level editor and an AI-powered level generation pipeline will be ready on day one, so you spend your time on what matters: making every level fun.

What you’ll do

  • Build. Design, build, and tune levels directly in Unity, covering layouts, encounters, pacing and difficulty.
  • Scale. Triple our level content by combining our AI pipeline with your own design judgment.
  • Balance. Model how health, damage, and stat changes affect the numbers before anything ships.
  • Polish. Bring existing levels to final quality and give them the feel and juice that make players stay.
  • Own. Set the level design roadmap, make design calls, and question whether each choice fits the game.
  • Specify. Write clear, detailed specs that developers can implement as written.
  • Learn from players. Use playtests and player data to see what works and iterate quickly.
  • AI. Use AI every day to generate layouts, prototype encounters, simulate balancing, and automate level work.

Requirements

  • Years of level design experience, with shipped levels on a hybrid casual, RPG or combat-based game.
  • Hands-on balancing skills: you’re comfortable with stats, health and damage maths, and spreadsheets.
  • Fluency in Unity: you build and iterate levels in the engine yourself.
  • A strong sense of game feel: you know when a level is fun, and you can explain why.
  • AI is already part of how you work every day. You've used it to automate, speed up, or rethink.
  • The autonomy to build your own roadmap and make design decisions.
  • A data-driven approach to level tuning.
  • Feature design experience alongside level design.

For this role, you’ll also bring

  • Extreme ownership. You drive outcomes. When something breaks, you fix it instead of explaining why it broke.
  • Proactive. You don’t wait for instructions or perfect conditions. You spot what needs doing and do it.
  • Pragmatism and simplicity. You look for the simplest solution that works, use whatever tools are available, and ship.
  • Sharp thinking. You learn fast, reason from facts, and structure your ideas clearly.
  • Hungry and motivated. You’re ambitious, high-energy, and grounded.

Why Homa

  • Exceptional growth. We hire people of outstanding potential, then put them where they can grow fastest.
  • Real ownership. You own the player experience of a game, and you’ll see your levels move the metrics.
  • The right tools from day one. A dedicated level editor and an AI level pipeline, so you focus on design.
  • A high talent bar. Our teams are small and ambiti us, and the people around you will push you to grow.
  • AI at the core. You’ll have access to the best AI tools, and you’ll help shape how level design works in an AI-first company.

Benefits

At Homa, we prioritize talent, energy, and determination over traditional credentials. We’re building a global community of brilliant, driven people who think boldly, act with pragmatism, move fast, and push boundaries. We believe true innovation comes from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and curiosity without limits. Our culture is grounded in four core values:

  • Humility: We recognise that we are always learning, we can always improve and grow.
  • Curiosity: We continuously seek the “why” behind the “what” - we explore with purpose and practicality.
  • Focus: Our curiosity takes us deeper, not wider - we obsess over the details and let pragmatism guide our attention.
  • Ambition: We strive for the best - we don’t settle for “good enough,” - we use common sense to reach higher.

Benefits

Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here’s what you can expect:

  • 🏥 Comprehensive Benefits: Depending on your location, you’ll enjoy a range of perks such as insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym memberships, and more.

  • 🌍 Coworking Access: You will have access to WeWork spaces throughout Europe, along with all their perks and professional office environments.

  • ✈️ Team Gatherings: We value time together beyond the screen. Join us for occasional team gatherings, off-site retreats (Workations as we name them) to connect, recharge, and celebrate.
  • 📈 Performance Reviews: We’re committed to your growth. Every six months, we reflect on your progress, recognize your achievements, and align on clear development goals.
  • 💻 Equipment Support: From day one, we’ll provide everything you need to do your best work, including a home office setup allowance if you're working remotely.

Where We Hire

Our HQ in Paris is a vibrant hub of creativity, collaboration, and connection. From rooftop lunches and coffee chats to after-work apéros and community events, we’ve designed a space people genuinely enjoy - all within a cozy WeWork filled with good energy (and snacks).

We also have incredible team members across Europe - from Spain and Turkey to Germany, North Macedonia, Poland, the UK, and more. To keep collaboration smooth, we primarily hire within European time zones (UTC to UTC+3). If you're based there - or planning to be - we’d love to hear from you!

title: CENTRALE LYON - Doctorat Modélisation prédictive de matériaux polymères recyclés par inférence statistique et apprentissage machine hybride.
description:
Contexte

Le projet MIAM, soutenu par l’Institut Carnot Ingénierie@Lyon, propose une thèse de doctorat de 36 mois au sein du Laboratoire de Tribologie et Dynamique des Systèmes (LTDS UMR CNRS 5513, Ecole Centrale de Lyon, Ecully, France). Ce travail de recherche s’inscrit dans une collaboration étroite entre les équipes DySCo du LTDS et les laboratoires partenaires comme le LAMCOS (INSA de Lyon) et du Centre Technique Industriel (CTI) de la Plasturgie et des Composites français (IPC). L’objectif scientifique est de lever les verrous liés à la variabilité des matières plastiques recyclées en développant des stratégies d’apprentissage machine et d’inférence statistique capables de garantir une qualité de 1 production stable malgré l’hétérogénéité des gisements de matériaux.

Le cœur des travaux portera sur le développement d’une structure d’apprentissage originale permettant de fusionner des données expérimentales réelles avec des données synthétiques issues de simulations numériques. Le candidat devra concevoir des modèles prédictifs robustes, souvent qualifiés de jumeaux numériques, pour assurer un pilotage des procédés en temps réel. Cette approche vise à réduire drastiquement les délais de mise en œuvre de nouveaux matériaux innovants tout en maintenant une fidélité physique stricte, assurant ainsi que les modèles ne soient pas de simples corrélations statistiques mais reflètent la réalité mécanique.

Cas d’étude

Le cas d’application principal retenu pour cette recherche est le développement d’un capteur virtuel appliqué à la rhéologie au sein des lignes de transformation de l’IPC. En instrumentant les étapes de mélange et d’injection, le doctorant cherchera à prédire les propriétés finales de la matière, telles que la viscosité et le comportement des granulés, en fonction des réglages machines. Ce cas offre un terrain d’étude idéal pour tester la résilience des algorithmes face à des conditions de production changeantes.


Profil recherché

Le profil recherché pour cette thèse est celui d’un candidat possédant une double compétence affirmée en intelligence artificielle et en modélisation physique des matériaux. Une maîtrise des outils de programmation et une sensibilité aux problématiques industrielles sont indispensables pour mener à bien les missions de ce projet. Les travaux se dérouleront principalement à l’École Centrale de Lyon, avec des échanges réguliers entre les sites d’Écully, de Villeurbanne et d’Oyonnax, et bénéficieront d’un environnement scientifique de haut niveau dédié à l’innovation dans le domaine des matériaux et des procédés.

Type de contrat

Le contrat sera un CDD de type contrat doctoral ’avec activité (diffusion d’informations scientifiques et/ou expertise)’ géré par Centrale Lyon. La rémunération sera d’approximativement 2035€ net par mois sur 36 mois.

title: Product Line Manager
description:
About Wallee Group AG

Wallee Group is a leader in advanced payment solutions, dedicated to providing robust, scalable, and secure systems across multiple domains. We enhance customer experiences through innovative payment and finance technology that empowers businesses to grow efficiently. With operations spanning several countries, we thrive on collaboration and agility, utilizing the Scrum framework to drive our international teams. At Wallee, we stay at the forefront of market trends, continuously innovating to deliver premier services to our global customers.

The Role

The Product Line Manager owns the full lifecycle of a product line - from introduction through to controlled end-of-life. The role combines strategic portfolio and roadmap management with subject matter expertise in specific verticals, bringing market, product, and supplier perspectives into one consistent strategy.

In Wallee's payment technology context, this specifically includes managing hardware/firmware generations (e.g., terminal models, certification versions like the EMV L2 kernel) and forward-looking planning for successor products.

The Impact You’ll Make

  • Drive Full Lifecycle & Strategy: Own the product journey from concept to decommissioning—defining launch criteria, target segments, success metrics, and forward-looking successor products before hardware/firmware generation changes.

  • Optimize the Portfolio: Maintain a structured view of all variants (terminal types, SoftPOS vs. hardware POS) using frameworks like the BCG matrix to prioritize investment and avoid overlap/cannibalization.

  • Build Capacity-Synced Roadmaps: Translate strategic goals and vertical needs into prioritized, time-boxed feature roadmaps (e.g., quarterly or PI planning in SAFe), balancing "run the business" compliance updates against "grow the business" initiatives.

  • Champion Vertical Expertise & Research: Act as the "translator" between vertical requirements (e.g., retail, hospitality, events) and engineering's technical language while running ongoing trend scanning (PCI/EMV updates), competitor analysis, and customer feedback synthesis.

  • Lead Go-to-Market & Sales Enablement: Define launch plans (positioning, pricing, training, documentation), coordinate alignment across Sales, Marketing, and Support, and assist Sales with technical expertise on complex, regulated deals.

  • Manage Suppliers & Ecosystems: Onboard and manage external partners (terminal manufacturers, component suppliers, certification labs), overseeing SLAs, operational forecasting, defect escalations, contract negotiations, and risk mitigation (such as dual-sourcing).

What Success Looks Like

  • Strategic Portfolio Health: A clear, non-overlapping product line where investments are prioritized effectively and End-of-Sale (EOS) / End-of-Life (EOL) migration paths are seamlessly executed.

  • Uncompromising Compliance: Continuous alignment with certification and regulatory standards (PCI, EMV, ep2) across the entire portfolio, eliminating compliance risk.

  • Reliable Supplier Alignment: High-performing partner relationships with well-managed SLAs, aligned roadmaps, and secure supply chains.

  • Market-Driven Innovation: Roadmaps and GTM materials that accurately reflect vertical user journeys, market trends, and validated customer needs.

  • Cross-Functional Readiness: Seamless coordination with internal teams so all departments are aligned and fully enabled from day one of product launches.

What You Bring to the Table

  • Product Experience: Proven experience in product management, ideally with portfolio or product line ownership in fintech, payments, or hardware-enabled software.

  • Domain Knowledge: Understanding or familiarity with payment certification and compliance topics (PCI, EMV, ep2) is a strong plus.

  • Vertical & Market Expertise: Experience or strong interest in specific industry verticals, coupled with a track record in market research and competitor analysis.

  • Strategic & Analytical Mindset: Strong problem-solving skills with a solution- and customer-oriented approach.

  • Stakeholder & Supplier Management: Exceptional communication and negotiation skills, comfortable managing both internal stakeholders and external supplier relationships.

  • Languages: Fluent in English and German.

Why Join Wallee?

  • Modern Workspace: A beautiful office in the heart of Winterthur - comfortable, bright, and collaboration-ready.

  • True Flexibility: Flexible daily hours and a 4-week "Work from Anywhere" policy every year.

  • Innovation First: We work with the latest tech stacks in a flat hierarchy where your voice actually matters.

  • Growth & Culture: Competitive compensation, aligned with experience, seniority, and expertise, personal development budgets, and a social calendar filled with events.

  • The Perks: Fresh fruits, snacks, and high-quality coffee to keep you fueled.

Don’t tick every box? Neither do most great hires. If the role feels right, reach out, we’d love to see if we’re a match.
