title: Senior Technical Support Engineer
description:
Who We Are; What We Do; Where We’re Going
 
Magnet Forensics is a global leader in the development of digital investigative software that acquires, analyzes, and shares evidence from computers, smartphones, tablets, and IoT-related devices. We are continually innovating so our customers can deploy advanced and effective tools to protect their companies, communities, and countries.
 
Serving thousands of customers globally, our solutions are playing a crucial role in modernizing digital investigations, helping investigators fight crime, protect assets, and guard national security.
 
With employees based around the world, Magnet Forensics has been expanding our global presence. As a part of Magnet Forensics, you can expect to make a difference in the world, no matter what role you play. You’ll be supported through learning and development, not to mention an incredible team with unbelievable talent and integrity.
 
If you think you would be the right person to join our team working towards this goal, we would love to hear from you! 

Role Overview

The Senior Technical Support Engineer is a technical escalation point for complex, high-impact, and sensitive customer issues. This role leads systemic problem management, develops technical capability across the Support team, and partners with Engineering and Product Management to reduce recurring issues, improve product quality, and strengthen support effectiveness. 

This is a senior individual contributor role with technical leadership responsibilities and no direct reports. This position reports directly to the Manager, Customer Success and receives functional direction from the Director, Technical Support. 


What You’ll Do
  • Own resolution of escalated, high-severity, or cross-system customer issues, providing clear and timely customer communication while balancing speed, technical quality, and customer impact. 
  • Lead root-cause and trend analysis for complex or recurring issues, quantify customer and support impact, and partner with Engineering to implement and validate corrective actions that reduce repeat cases.
  • Provide senior technical leadership during customer-impacting incidents and contribute to post-incident reviews, including timelines, root-cause findings, corrective actions, and recommendations.
  • Provide technical guidance and coaching to Technical Support Engineers during complex investigations, escalations, and incident response.
  • Represent customer impact in defect triage and product feedback forums by providing clear evidence, use cases, severity context, and recommended priorities.
  • Define and improve support playbooks, escalation paths, and diagnostic standards.
  • Create and maintain reusable technical guidance, diagnostic procedures, and knowledge articles, and apply that content to new-hire onboarding and ongoing team development.
    •  

    What We’re Looking For
  • Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of experience investigating complex technical issues in enterprise software support, systems engineering, digital forensics, or a related technical environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to explain complex technical issues clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including customers experiencing high-impact or sensitive issues.
  • Strong incident management, root cause analysis, and cross-functional leadership skills.
  • Demonstrated experience coaching technical support professionals and developing or improving diagnostic practices, escalation standards, or support procedures.

    • What Success Looks Like
  • High-impact and sensitive customer issues are resolved in a timely manner, with clear communication and strong technical quality.
  • Recurring issues are identified and addressed through validated corrective actions, reducing repeat cases and customer impact.
  • Technical Support Engineers apply stronger diagnostic practices, escalation standards, and technical guidance during complex investigations.
  • Customer impact is translated into actionable product feedback that contributes to improved product quality and support effectiveness.

    • Preferred Qualifications
  • Advanced experience with Magnet Forensics products or comparable digital forensics platforms. Successful candidates may be required to complete relevant Magnet certifications after hire. 
  • Professional fluency in written and spoken Arabic to support Arabic-speaking customers.
  • Industry-recognized AI, Cloud, or networking certifications and introductory programming experience.
  • Experience with Salesforce Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, and Knowledge.

    • Working Conditions
  • This role follows a Sunday-to-Thursday work week, with standard working hours of 9 am to 5 pm Arabia Standard Time. Corresponding UK working hours vary between GMT and BST due to seasonal clock changes.
  • This is a remote role based in the United Kingdom.
  • The position involves extended periods of computer-based work.
  • Occasional work outside standard hours may be required to address critical customer issues.
  • Occasional travel may be required for customer engagements, training, or team meetings. 

    • Compensation & Benefits

    The Compensation range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. Please note that the actual compensation may vary depending on location and job-related factors such as qualifications, experience, knowledge and skills. If you are applying for this role outside of the primary location and you are selected for an interview, the Talent Acquisition Partner can share more information with you.    

    Position Type: New Position 


    Magnet is proud to offer benefits such as: 
     
    - Generous time off policies 
    - Competitive compensation 
    - Volunteer opportunities  
    - Reward and recognition programs   
    - Employee committees & resource groups  
    - Healthcare and retirement benefits 
     
    Indicators of Success
     
    We’re looking for someone who checks off most, but not all, of the boxes listed in “skills and experiences”.  It’s more important to us to find candidates who can display indicators of success through skills they have developed and experiences they have been a part of, than to find folks who have “been there, done that”.  We want to be part of your development journey, and we’ll learn as much from you as you learn from us. 
     
    How We Work
     
    At Magnet Forensics, we take a hybrid-flexible approach to support your productivity and work-life balance. If you’re within a comfortable travel distance to one of our offices, you’ll occasionally join us in person. How often you’ll come in depends on your department and team needs, typically ranging from weekly to monthly. These in-person moments help us build stronger connections, spark new ideas, and celebrate our successes together. Most days, you can choose what works best for you, while staying in tune with your team’s goals.
     
    We’re excited to welcome you to our team and look forward to achieving great things together - both in the office and wherever you work best!
     
    The Most Important Thing
     
    We’re looking for candidates that can provide examples of how they have demonstrated Magnet CODE in their previous experiences:
     
    CARE – We care about each other and our mission to make a difference in the world.
    OWN – We are accountable for our results – while never forgetting to act with integrity, empathy, and respect.
    DEDICATE – We put our heart and soul into meeting the needs of our customers and helping them serve the people they protect.
    EVOLVE – We are constantly innovating and exploring new ways to work together to make an impact with our work.
     
    Here at Magnet Forensics, we are committed to continuous learning and are focused on building a diverse and inclusive workforce. This commitment will be reflected in our hiring processes and embedded in our values and how we treat one another. If you’re interested in this role, but do not meet all of the qualifications listed above, we encourage you to apply anyways.

Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team - from Finance to HR - to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.
 
Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally. Industry leaders like Unilever, Uber, Anthropic, Snowflake or Siemens, use Pigment daily to make more informed decisions and confidently navigate any scenario.
 
With a team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, we've raised nearly $400M from top-tier investors and were named a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software.
 
At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

You’ll join Pigment’s Reporting & Collaboration community, working as a senior hands-on Frontend Engineer on some of the most complex parts of the product.

This community is responsible for how users access, configure and interact with their data. That creates significant frontend challenges around large-scale datasets, filtering, visualisation, complex configuration and increasingly AI-powered experiences.


On the engineering part:
  • Spend approximately 80% of your time as a hands-on engineer, designing, building and shipping production features.
  • Work on complex, data-heavy frontend problems where performance, usability and scale all matter.
  • Build sophisticated interfaces for displaying, filtering and interacting with large datasets.
  • Work with React, TypeScript and JavaScript, while contributing to the wider technical decisions behind the product.
  • Partner closely with Product Managers, Product Designers and Engineers to take features from problem definition through to production.
  • Make pragmatic engineering decisions based on the needs of the product and its users, rather than pursuing technical complexity for its own sake.
  • Contribute to areas across Reporting & Collaboration depending on business needs and your interests, including data extraction and filtering, visualisation, complex configuration and emerging AI experiences.
  • Use modern engineering tooling, with Pigment teams working across GCP, CircleCI and AI development tools such as Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot.

    • This is not a traditional Engineering Manager role where you step away from the code. You will remain a senior individual contributor and be expected to ship.

     


    On the people management part, here is what it entails:

    At Pigment, people management and technical leadership are deliberately separated.

    Tech Leads lead the technical direction of individual teams. Engineering Managers focus on developing engineers as people while remaining hands-on engineers themselves.

  • Spend approximately 20% of your time on people management.
  • Gradually take on direct reports after establishing yourself as an IC during your probation period.
  • Coach engineers across different teams within the Reporting & Collaboration community.
  • Support engineers with career progression, development, feedback and performance.
  • Run regular 1:1s and help engineers understand what they need to do to progress.
  • Set clear expectations and provide actionable feedback.
  • Handle difficult performance conversations when necessary and follow through with clear development plans.
  • Partner with Tech Leads to understand how your reports are performing technically without taking ownership of the Tech Lead's responsibilities.
  • Help create an environment where strong engineers can continue to develop while doing their best work.

    • Engineering Managers typically support engineers across multiple teams within their community rather than "owning" a single engineering team.

     


    Who you are

    We’re looking for someone who is both a strong senior Frontend Engineer and an experienced people manager.

  • Significant professional software-engineering experience, with the technical depth expected of a senior engineer.
  • Strong recent hands-on frontend engineering experience.
  • Production experience with React, TypeScript and/or JavaScript.
  • Previous formal people-management experience. Ideally, you have already managed engineers rather than looking for your first management opportunity.
  • Experience owning areas such as coaching, career development, feedback and performance management, not simply mentoring engineers or leading projects.
  • Experience building complex product interfaces, ideally within B2B SaaS, enterprise software, analytics, data platforms or another sophisticated data-heavy product.
  • Experience solving frontend problems involving areas such as large datasets, visualisation, filtering, configuration, performance or complex workflows.
  • A strong product mindset. You care about what you're building, who is using it and whether it genuinely solves their problem.
  • Strong collaboration skills across Engineering, Product and Design.
  • The ability and desire to remain deeply hands-on in the code while managing people.
  • The autonomy expected of a senior IC: once you understand the problem, you can work with the team to move it forward without needing constant direction.
  • Fluent English. French is not required.

    • What you will get
  • Competitive salary
  • Equity
  • The best health insurance with Alan Blue is entirely free for you and your family 💙
  • Trust and flexible working hours
  • Brand new offices in the heart of Paris, London, New York, and, Toronto
  • Remote-friendly environment

title: Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling
description:
Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling

Hybrid in London or remote in the UK

We’re looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team.

You'll shape how iwoca models credit risk – setting the technical direction on multi-quarter projects, and lifting the bar for the team as you go.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and Customer Lifetime Value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.

The team is around twelve data scientists. Some work on auto-space models that decide within five minutes from data candidates authorise us to pull. Others work on manual-space models that pick up when a credit analyst adds digital footprint and income data, which lands a decision within 24 hours.

The role

You'll own credit and CLtV modelling projects end to end, from spotting where the modelling stack is holding the business back through to landing the change. The work spans keeping production models healthy, incremental development, and research that reshapes how the models work. AI has lowered the cost of prototyping enough that ideas which used to sit below the priority line are now viable, so the R&D share of the role is growing.

Live examples of the work:

  • Causal estimation of offer terms. Modelling how amount, duration, and price shape customer outcomes.

  • Unifying auto and manual models. The two families were built without forced technical alignment. Finding a principled way to unify them on a common cost function is open work.

  • IFRS accounting model. A multi-stage credit model where information propagates back from later-stage recovery predictions to sharpen upfront loss estimates.

  • Generalising credit and CLtV. Whether a more general framing could replace both separate models is an open research question.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns.

  • Production ML. You have built and shipped supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, monitoring.

  • Research mindset. You proactively explore new ways to add value. R&D time is when you expect to find the next step change.

  • Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere. You've influenced technical direction beyond your own projects.

  • Project leadership. You've owned modelling projects end to end, from spotting the opportunity through framing, method choice, shipping, and landing the commercial impact. You move fast, iterate, and update on new evidence rather than chase perfection.

  • AI fluency. You use AI as a primary tool. You prototype with it, automate with it, and take on R&D that would not otherwise be viable. You use judgement on where it helps and where it doesn't.

Bonus:

  • Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling.

  • Non-linear methods. You have shipped gradient boosting or neural networks on tabular data in production.

  • Bayesian methods. You have used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work.

  • Time series modelling. You have modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered.

  • Python. The stack the team uses.

The salary

We expect to pay from £90,000 – £120,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

title: Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling
description:
Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling

Hybrid in London or remote in the UK

We’re looking for a Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team.

You'll work on the credit models that sit at the core of iwoca's lending business – the models that decide who we lend to, on what terms, and how far the product can grow.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and customer lifetime value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.

The team is around twelve data scientists, who combined create models to efficiently drive fully automated and human-in-the-loop decision making. This forms the core analytical team that interface with and support smaller analytic functions in other parts of the business.

The role

You'll run credit and CLtV modelling projects alongside the rest of the team. The work spans keeping production models healthy, incremental development, and research that reshapes how the models work. AI has lowered the cost of prototyping enough that ideas which used to sit below the priority line are now viable, so the R&D share of the role is growing.

Live examples of the work:

  • Causal estimation of offer terms. Modelling how amount, duration, and price shape customer outcomes.

  • Unifying auto and manual models. The two families were built without forced technical alignment. Finding a principled way to unify them on a common cost function is open work.

  • IFRS accounting model. A multi-stage credit model where information propagates back from later-stage recovery predictions to sharpen upfront loss estimates.

  • Generalising credit and CLtV. Whether a more general framing could replace both separate models is an open research question.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns.

  • Research mindset. You're actively exploring new ways to add value. R&D time is when you expect to find the next step change.

  • Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere.

  • Analytical ownership. You take ambiguous problems end to end, from framing to a landed decision. You like to move fast, iterate, and update on new evidence rather than chase perfection.

  • AI fluency. You use AI as a primary tool. You prototype with it, automate with it, and take on R&D that would not otherwise be viable. You use judgement on where it helps and where it doesn't.

Bonus:

  • Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling.

  • Production ML. You have built and shipped supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, monitoring.

  • Non-linear methods. You can think in terms of the cost function and inductive biases of your models

  • Bayesian methods. You have used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work.

  • Time series modelling. You have modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered.

  • Python. The stack the team uses.

The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 – £90,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

title: Stage IA/ML Engineer 100% R&D - agentic AI
description:
INTERNSHIP 

Agentic AI for Semi-Automating the Data Science Workflow 

Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. 

Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models. 

Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices. 

Key Figures 

  • 20 years of experience in data science 

  • 500+ data scientists, all consultants 

  • 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 

  • 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) 

  • $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 

  • 1,000+ data science projects 

Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. 

A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. 

Internship Objective: From a Business Question to a Trusted Recommendation 

LLM-based agents have made rapid progress in the past two years: they can now write, run and tune machine learning code with little human help. Yet real data science projects rarely start from a clean, well-defined task. They start from a business question and imperfect data, and the early choices (what to predict, how to measure success, how to validate) decide whether the result can be trusted. Automating these steps calls for assistants that know when to ask, when to stop, and how to back every claim with evidence. 

The Innovation Department is building remit, a harness that semi-automates the data science workflow. At each step of a project (framing, data design, exploratory analysis, modeling, evaluation), AI agents draft the output, automatic checks catch common mistakes such as data leakage, and a data scientist reviews and accepts the result before moving on. Ultimately, a business user brings a question and a dataset, and the system frames the problem, prepares and explores the data, compares models against a simple baseline, and returns a clear recommendation in which every figure can be traced back to the data. 

The work builds on recent research in agentic data science [1]. Agents now earn medals on many of the Kaggle competitions in MLE-bench [2], yet they tend to guess silently rather than ask when a task is ambiguous [3]. Meanwhile, tabular foundation models such as TabICLv2 [4] give strong predictive models without any tuning. 

The intern will work with senior data scientists and AI builders to build and refine remit. This internship offers an opportunity to engage with cutting-edge AI research and production engineering. 

Key Responsibilities 

The intern will: 

  • Review the latest research on agentic data science and on the evaluation of AI agents, building on the team's recent review. 

  • Design and implement remit's agents, starting with problem framing and data design, together with the automatic checks that catch mistakes such as data leakage. 

  • Help define how the system works with business users: when to ask a clarifying question, when to stop rather than guess, and how to explain results in plain language. 

  • Extend the system toward modeling and evaluation, building on trusted tools (scikit-learn, AutoML, tabular foundation models) rather than free-form generated code. 

  • Build a benchmark of realistic business cases, run experiments to measure quality, reliability and cost, and take part in a pilot with business users. 

  • Help integrate the system with the Databricks stack (Unity Catalog, MLflow) and support the safe and governed operation of the agents. 

Profile 

  • Currently in the final year of a Master's or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming. 

  • Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research-and-build problem and to explain results to non-specialists. 

  • Familiarity with large language models and agentic techniques (prompting, tool calling, structured outputs, evaluation). 

  • Strong Python skills and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). 

  • Fluency in English. 

  • Nice to have: experience with an agent framework, solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing), and exposure to Databricks, MLflow or cloud data platforms. 

Benefits 

  • Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact. 

  • Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetrics' Innovation Department. 

  • Skill Development: Gain expertise in LLM agents, the evaluation of AI systems, and production tooling on Databricks (Unity Catalog, MLflow). 

  • Career Growth: Opportunity to transition into a full-time Data Scientist role in AI at Ekimetrics, or into a PhD program, upon successful completion of the internship. 

  • Scientific Contribution: Opportunity to co-author and publish scientific papers in reputable AI and data science conferences and journals. 

  • Networking: Collaborate with Ekimetrics' industrial and academic partners, enhancing your professional network in the AI research community. 

  • Ethical and Sustainable AI: Learn to develop AI solutions that align with ethical, governed, and sustainable best practices, a core commitment of Ekimetrics. 

Duration: 6 months, Paris 

References 

[1] LLM-Based Data Science Agents: A Survey of Capabilities, Challenges, and Future Directions (2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04023 

[2] MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering (2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07095 

[3] Ambig-DS: A Benchmark for Task-Framing Ambiguity in Data-Science Agents (2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09698 

[4] TabICLv2: A Better, Faster, Scalable, and Open Tabular Foundation Model (2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11139

Chez Ekimetrics, vos idées comptent vraiment et vous appartiennent: à vous de leur donner vie. Nous cultivons un esprit entrepreneurial qui vous encourage à repousser les limites pour créer un impact significatif.

title: Stage 2027 AI/ML Engineer 100% R&D - Tabular foundation models
description:
Latent Reasoning for Tabular Foundation Models: Performance Enhancement and Interpretability 

 

 

Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. 

Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models. 

Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices. 

Key Figures 

  • 20 years of experience in data science 

  • 500+ data scientists, all consultants 

  • 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 

  • 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) 

  • $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 

  • 1,000+ data science projects 

Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. 

A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. 

 

Internship Objective: From Latent Reasoning to Better and More Understandable Tabular Models 

 

Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) such as TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT are transformers pre-trained on large collections of mostly synthetic datasets. They learn in context: the training data and the points to predict are given as input, and predictions come out of a single forward pass, with no dataset-specific training or tuning. They now rival gradient boosting on many benchmarks [3], which is changing how tabular modeling is practiced. 

In large language models, a growing line of research lets the model “reason” in its latent space rather than through generated tokens, using extra depth-wise computation, reused continuous hidden states or internal iterations. This latent reasoning can improve performance without longer text outputs [1, 2]. Our hypothesis is that a similar mechanism can improve TFMs: spending more latent compute at inference on hard or ambiguous cases could help them make better use of the in-context examples. Almost all existing work on latent reasoning targets natural language, and its transfer to tabular models, whose architecture, pre-training data and output differ profoundly, remains largely unexplored. 

Mechanistic interpretability is starting to open the black box, both for latent-reasoning language models and for TFMs themselves [4]. It lets us ask not only whether latent reasoning improves a TFM, but also what the model actually computes during these extra steps, and whether that computation is faithful and useful. The internship therefore has two goals: designing and evaluating latent reasoning mechanisms for TFMs, and using interpretability methods to analyze what they learn. 

The intern will work with senior researchers and data scientists. This internship offers an opportunity to contribute to an emerging research topic at the intersection of tabular modeling, latent reasoning and interpretability. 

Key Responsibilities 

The intern will: 

  • Review the literature on latent reasoning (NLP) and tabular foundation models, building on recent surveys. 

  • Identify and adapt latent reasoning mechanisms to TFM architectures (e.g. iterative depth-wise computation, hidden-state reuse). 

  • Implement them on open-source TFMs and measure their effect on accuracy, calibration and robustness against strong baselines (gradient boosting, standard TFMs) at comparable compute. 

  • Apply interpretability methods (representation analysis, probing, activation patching) to characterize the computation performed during latent reasoning. 

  • Build an evaluation protocol on diverse tabular datasets, including realistic business cases. 

  • Document the results and contribute to scientific publications. 

Profile 

  • Currently in the final year of a Master’s or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming. 

  • Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines. 

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research problem. 

  • Knowledge of transformers and language models; familiarity with latent reasoning or recurrent-depth models is a plus. 

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills, and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). 

  • Fluency in English is a plus. 

  • Nice to have: experience in interpretability, knowledge of TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT, and solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing). 

Benefits 

  • Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact. 

  • Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetrics' Innovation Department. 

  • Skill Development: Gain expertise in LLM agents, the evaluation of AI systems, and production tooling on Databricks (Unity Catalog, MLflow). 

  • Career Growth: Opportunity to transition into a full-time Data Scientist role in AI at Ekimetrics, or into a PhD program, upon successful completion of the internship. 

  • Scientific Contribution: Opportunity to co-author and publish scientific papers in reputable AI and data science conferences and journals. 

  • Networking: Collaborate with Ekimetrics' industrial and academic partners, enhancing your professional network in the AI research community. 

  • Ethical and Sustainable AI: Learn to develop AI solutions that align with ethical, governed, and sustainable best practices, a core commitment of Ekimetrics. 

Duration: 6 months, Paris 

References 

[1] Zhu, R.-J. et al. (2025). A Survey on Latent Reasoning. arXiv:2507.06203. 

[2] Chen, X. et al. (2025). Reasoning Beyond Language: A Comprehensive Survey on Latent Chain-of-Thought Reasoning. arXiv:2505.16782. 

[3] Tabular Foundation Models: A Systematic Survey. [authors, year, link to complete] 

[4] Biloš, M. et al. (2026). A Mechanistic Study of Tabular Foundation Models. [link to complete]

Nous sommes convaincus que notre succès réside dans nos équipes passionnées et dévouées, engagées à bâtir une entreprise où chacun peut évoluer et construire sa carrière. Home page
Customer Stories
Nos valeurs

AGICAP recherche un(e) Ingénieur GRC pour faire partie de notre équipe Organizational Security. Si tu souhaites jouer un rôle central dans la protection des données et renforcer la sécurité de l’information dans un environnement dynamique et en constante évolution, ce poste est fait pour toi !
 
Notre département Sécurité est actuellement composé de 3 équipes :
- Platform Security : En charge de la sécurité technique
- Product Security : En charge de tous les sujets sécurité qui tournent autour de notre produit

En tant que Ingénieur GRC, tu participes à la sécurité des systèmes d’information d’Agicap. Tu participes à la définition et est garant de la mise en œuvre des politiques et procédures de sécurité pour protéger nos données, infrastructures et ressources.

title: Product ML Engineer
description:
About us

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.

Role Summary

We're looking for a Product ML Engineer to join one of our product experience teams — SMB, Scaler or Enterprise — and own the ML side of short, high-impact projects.

You'll work on focused ML problems with a clear product outcome, sometimes fine-tuning one of our models, sometimes integrating the best externally available model, but always choosing the fastest and most effective path to customer value.

You'll bring the technical depth of an Applied Scientist while operating with the pace and pragmatism of a product engineer. You'll own the journey from framing the problem through to shipping, measuring and iterating on the feature in production.

This is not a research role. Your time horizon is weeks rather than quarters, and success is measured by what reaches users and the impact it creates.

About the role

  • Embed directly within a product team. Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes.

  • Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production.

  • Make the build vs. buy decision. Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself versus integrating an external model, API or existing library.

  • Move from idea to production quickly. Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact.

  • Work closely with the ML team. Leverage shared infrastructure, evaluation tooling and expertise while remaining embedded in the product team's priorities and cadence.

  • Stay close to users. Get rapid feedback from customers, monitor how people use what you've shipped and use those insights to drive the next iteration.

  • Balance technical depth with pragmatism. Know when deeper modelling work is necessary and when an existing solution is already good enough to ship.

  • Write production code. Work directly in the product team's codebase rather than operating primarily through research notebooks and experiments.

  • Own quality in production. Build sound evaluations, monitor performance and investigate failures once the feature is live.

About You

  • You've shipped ML into production. You have 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping ML-powered products, with strong experience in PyTorch or equivalent frameworks such as TensorFlow or JAX.

  • You have applied-science depth. You can fine-tune vision or diffusion models, design meaningful evaluations and debug training runs when necessary.

  • You're a pragmatic builder. You care about solving the customer's problem rather than proving that your own model is the best approach. You'll happily use an external model, API or existing library when that's the fastest route to value.

  • You're product-minded. You measure success through shipped features, user behaviour and business outcomes rather than papers or benchmarks alone.

  • You're comfortable in production codebases. You can move between experimentation and production engineering, writing maintainable code that lives inside a real product.

  • You have strong ownership. You're comfortable taking an ambiguous ML problem, deciding what matters, choosing an approach and driving it through to production.

  • You iterate quickly. You enjoy short feedback loops and would rather ship something useful, learn from users and improve it than spend months optimising something that hasn't reached production.

  • You're curious and collaborative. You can both explain your expertise and learn from the deep technical expertise around you. You value knowledge sharing and humility.

  • You're fluent in English. French isn't required.

Nice to have: experience shipping generative image models or diffusion models into production; experience evaluating third-party AI APIs against internal alternatives; experience working in a fast-growing startup or directly within a product team.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary + meaningful equity

  • Hybrid working from our Paris headquarters

  • Visa sponsorship and relocation support up to €10,000

  • MacBook Pro and full home office setup

  • 30 days annual leave

  • Private healthcare

  • Regular company off-sites and team retreats

  • International English-speaking team

  • Language lessons in English and French

  1. Screening with an ML Researcher / Engineer

  2. Home technical assignment and review with the team

  3. Culture fit interview and meet the team

  4. Reference check and offer

title: Post-doctorante ou Post-doctorant en Evaluation de la vulnérabilité d’un réseau d’accès Télécom de type PON (Passive Optical Network) vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS (Distributed Acoustic Sensor) - CDD de 12 mois
description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 5 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons notre futur(e) post-doctorant(e) en évaluation de la vulnérabilité d’un réseau d’accès Télécom de type PON (Passive Optical Network) vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS (Distributed Acoustic Sensor) pour rejoindre le département Communications et Electronique (COMELEC).

Cette étude se situe dans le cadre du projet « Ecoute Acoustique Terrestre » (EAT) RAPID (Régime d’Appui Pour l’Innovation Duale), fruit d’un partenariat entre la société Febus Optics et Télécom Paris.

 La mesure de vibrations acoustiques distribuées par fibre optique (DAS, Distributed Acoustic Sensing) est une technologie récente, dont les applications ne cessent de se diversifier. On peut citer par exemple la détection d’intrusion en surveillance périmétrique, les mesures sismiques, le diagnostic de puits (pétrole, géothermie), etc. La bande passante de la mesure, de sub-Hertz à la centaine de kiloHertz, permet également d’envisager la captation de la bande audio, et donc de réaliser des mesures audios sur une fibre optique. Il est ainsi possible d’utiliser le réseau optique télécom d’un bâtiment pour réaliser des écoutes, en utilisant un système DAS modifié, intégrant des artéfacts matériels particuliers (enroulement, antennes, connecteurs) au voisinage de la zone d’écoute et un traitement du signal spécifique pour obtenir des performances suffisantes.

Le cadre de ce Postdoc est d’évaluer la vulnérabilité d’un réseau télécom vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS. Le branchement sur un réseau optique Telecom local en fonctionnement nécessite de s’adapter à son architecture, notamment en termes de plan de longueur d’onde.

L’audit des systèmes de télécommunication afin d’en évaluer la vulnérabilité constitue un enjeu majeur du réseau télécom. Un exemple de configuration d’un réseau d’accès est décrit dans la figure ci-après. Depuis le réseau Backbone, à partir du ‘Central Office’, les signaux télécoms sont acheminés chez les abonnés via le PON (Passive Optical Network). À l’intérieur des bâtiments, un réseau FTTX (Fiber To The X=H home, X=R room, X=O office, etc) ou un réseau local LAN (Local Area Network) optique servent respectivement à acheminer le signal optique jusqu’au terminal final ou à communiquer entre deux terminaux locaux via une liaison optique. Le PON comprend une fibre nourricière (Feeder Fiber) puis, au moins, un coupleur 1×N. Le codage de l’information est alors un mélange de multiplexage en longueur d’onde grossier (C-WDM) et de multiplexage temporel (TDM). Chaque voie de sortie du coupleur 1×N est envoyée vers des groupes de 1 à n abonnés à travers, au moins, un filtre qui sélectionne la longueur d’onde qui leur est allouée. Le signal après ce filtre est alors monochromatique et codé TDM. Le dernier coupleur 1×n répartie le signal chez les n abonnés. Ce PON comprend donc, entre autres, des coupleurs passifs qui divisent les signaux vers différents abonnés mais aussi des connecteurs, soudures, etc.

L’objectif de ce Postdoc est de faire un état des lieux des différents types de réseau mis en place et d’en évaluer les conséquences sur la capacité de mesures DAS :

·         Description des différents types de réseaux locaux existants,

·         Etats des lieux des différents types de transmission : CWDM, TDM, …

·         Quels sont les différents points d’accès pour une mesure DAS ?

·         Comment discriminer les différentes fibres interrogées après un coupleur ? Influence des points réflecteurs,

·         Etude des différentes marges de puissance pour une mesure DAS,

·         Potentielle présence de nœuds d’insertion et limite de la transparence optique,

·         Sensibilité des mesures DAS en fonction des différents types de fibre et de leur environnement,

·         Influence du réflecteur final sur la capacité d’écoute.

Le caractère innovant sera la définition des conditions du réseau et des configurations et des performances DAS permettant un audit cyber sur des infrastructures déjà déployées.

Au-delà d’une synthèse des configurations que l’on peut trouver sur le terrain, il s’agira de mener des tests, soit sur un réseau réel auxquels un accès nous sera donné, soit sur un réseau modèle implémenté pour l’étude. Ces travaux permettront d’identifier le type de modules d’interfaçage nécessaires, et de les spécifier, puis de les concevoir et de les fabriquer.

Vos principales missions seront :

  • Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine des capteurs à fibre optique distribués

  • Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

  • Participer à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris


Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat en génie électrique, en communications optiques, en photonique, en capteurs optiques ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez d’une solide expertise théorique et pratique en photonique et en traitement du signal numérique, ainsi que de bonnes compétences en programmation. Une connaissance des algorithmes de traitement du signal appliqués aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique, notamment dans le cadre de la détection cohérente, constitue un atout. Vous maîtrisez l’anglais, et la pratique du français est souhaitée.

Vous manifestez un intérêt marqué pour la recherche appliquée et êtes capable d’évoluer dans un environnement multiculturel. Enfin, vous faites preuve d’un bon esprit d’équipe, de qualités relationnelles, rédactionnelles et pédagogiques, ainsi que d’une excellente capacité d’analyse et de synthèse.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant que post-doctorant, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au Centre SPIN.

Le centre « Sciences des Processus Industriels et Naturels » (SPIN) est un centre de recherche, d’enseignement et de transfert technologique reconnu pour son expertise en Génie des Procédés appliqué aux solides divisés. Il est au service de l’innovation pour les entreprises industrielles confrontées à la transition numérique et environnementale. La personne recrutée sera intégrée dans le département « Procédés de Transformation des Solides et Instrumentation » (PTSI) et dans le Laboratoire Georges Friedel UMR CNRS 5307.

Le projet proposé ici consistera à développer de capteurs de gaz à partir de matériaux fonctionnels. L’étude des interactions solide/gaz sera menée en parallèle des caractérisations électriques sous atmosphère gazeuse complexe (bancs de test avec génération contrôlée de polluants).

Cette étude sera menée en collaboration avec des chercheurs de IMT Mines Albi qui ont en charge la synthèse des matériaux sensibles et de IMT Atlantique pour l’intégration ultérieure du capteur dans des vêtements.

Dans le cadre du développement de capteurs, les matériaux sensibles seront déposés sur des supports préalablement équipés d’électrodes. Cette phase devra être optimisée afin de pouvoir effectuer des caractérisations reproductibles. La stabilité, la sensibilité à différents gaz et la sélectivité à un gaz donné seront étudiées. Pour cela, des tests sous gaz cibles seront réalisés et analysés, en atmosphère simple dans un premier temps jusqu’à des tests sous atmosphères plus représentatives d’un environnement réel. Ensuite, des études d’adsorption seront réalisées, un équipement de chimisorption sera utilisé afin d’étudier l’interaction solide (matériau sensible) / gaz et permettra d’apporter une compréhension sur les mécanismes de détection, de capture ou de traitement.

title: Lead Software Engineer
description:
Building the intelligence behind Solskin

Are you a driven person who wants to make buildings come alive?

We are Zurich Soft Robotics (ZSR), a Zurich-based startup developing Solskin – a climate-adaptive solar facade. Solskin is not just a PV system or a shading system; it’s an intelligent skin that uses weather and building data, occupant feedback, and AI algorithms to decide how the facade moves, so buildings stay comfortable, avoid overheating, and use energy as efficiently as possible. Solskin is already running on several buildings across Switzerland, with many more to follow.

In this role, you own the software that makes that happen. You write the code that runs Solskin, keep it reliable in the field, and constantly improve it. You will also architect and lead our future sensor-to-data platform. Your focus is where software meets hardware, and the control and AI on top of it. You don't need to be a front-end specialist.

What you will do

This is a hands-on leadership position: you code every day.

Own the full stack: You maintain and develop the whole software stack, from cloud and data management to user-facing applications, and from low-level embedded firmware to high-level AI controllers learning from users. You keep it reliable and keep making it better.

Be the link between the teams: You build the software that runs on real buildings and support the hardware team. You also build the internal tools used by sales and the business team.

Lead what comes next: With the CEO and CTO, you set the software direction and lead development of future products.

Our stack:

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, PyTorch

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript

  • Hardware: C/C++, STM32 microcontrollers, Beckhoff PLCs

  • Database: PostgreSQL (TimescaleDB)

  • DevOps & Cloud: Linux, Docker, AWS, Grafana

What we are looking for

Required:

  • Education: MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or similar.

  • Python: This is a must. You write clean Python that runs in production, on real systems.

  • Embedded & Hardware: Shipped C/C++ on microcontrollers running on physical hardware; comfortable working with sensors, actuators, and basic electronics.

  • Applied AI & Control: Understanding of modern control and ML/RL methods, with hands-on PyTorch experience applied to physical or dynamic systems.

  • Cloud & data: You are comfortable with PostgreSQL, Docker and AWS.

  • Leadership attitude: You take ownership, make decisions, and want to grow as a leader.

  • Languages: English. German is a big plus.

  • Hybrid setting: You will be expected to be on-site at least three days per week, and sometimes at customers’ locations, to work on real products.

  • Availability: 100%, as soon as possible.

  • Work-permit: You need the right to work in Switzerland for this position.

Preferred:

  • Startup experience: You have worked in a startup before and know what that means.

  • Building modeling and control: You have prior experience handling building data, modeling building dynamics, and developing building controllers; ideally with ML and RL tools.

  • Frontend: React and TypeScript.

Mindset:

  • Hands-on: You lead, and you still do the hard work yourself.

  • Fast: You are pragmatic and iterate quickly. Things break, and plans change, and that doesn't scare you.

  • Purpose: You care about climate and want to make buildings smarter.

Benefits

Impact: Your code runs on real buildings. You see the result of your work.

Ownership: A key role with a real say in our product and technology, and room to grow with the company.

Flexibility: Hybrid work and flexible hours. We like being in the Zurich office together, so plan for regular office days.

Team: A small, skilled, and down-to-earth team that helps each other out.

The reality: We are a startup. It is often messy; things rarely work the first time, and the workload is real. In return, you get a lot of freedom and responsibility from day one.

Sounds like you?

Send us your CV and a short document instead of a classic cover letter. It doesn’t need to be long, just enough for us to understand who you are and where you stand. Please cover these points:

  • About you: A short description of yourself.

  • Proud of: One thing you are really proud of, in a few sentences.

  • Startup: Why do you fit a startup?

  • Software meets hardware: Your experience where software and hardware come together.

  • Juggeling many hats: You’ll rarely finish one thing from A to Z without interruptions: different stacks, different people, different projects, and on-site surprises. Describe a time your work was like that, and how you handled it.

title: SAP Analytics Consultant
description:

  • Understanding of integration across CRM, S/4HANA, BW, HANA and reporting tools, with a focus on data quality, performance, security and governance

  • SAP Analytics certifications (BW, BW-IP, CDS Views, SLT, BO, Lumira, SAP cloud analytics) are an advantage

  • Fluent French is essential

What We Offer:

  • A long-term engagement through 2029, renewable annually

  • Meaningful work supporting the financial and budget processes of a public-sector organisation

  • A broad and modern SAP Analytics landscape covering BW/IP, HANA, CDS, SLT, BO/Lumira and cloud analytics

title: Growth & AI Marketing Operations Specialist
description:
About Papers

Papers AG is a Swiss cyber security engineering house and an incubator for our product portfolio. We build device-level alternatives to centralized cloud and trust. Our strategy is to grow our foundational decentralized network by building high-demand enterprise products directly on top of it.

Your portfolio includes:

  • Acurast: Decentralized confidential compute running on ordinary smartphones.

  • Obsidio: A continuous, AI-assisted pentesting subscription. Incubated by Papers, Obsidio is built directly on Acurast, leveraging the decentralized network as a unique compute moat to battle-test networks.

  • Hypergate: Enterprise mobile single sign-on for managed Android and iOS fleets.

As an engineering-driven team, we work with autonomy and purpose. Our culture is built on meritocracy, long-term thinking, and a commitment to quality over buzz, innovation is in our DNA. We aim to collaborate with people who love tech for its own sake and want to help shape the future by solving real-world challenges.

Your role

We are seeking a tech-savvy, execution-oriented Growth & AI Marketing Operations Specialist to serve as the engine powering our growth campaigns, content infrastructure, and data analytics pipeline.

Your main goal will be to communicate our stories across a portfolio of brands by bridging the gap between cutting-edge AI, data operations, and tactical growth marketing. You’ll be building automated content workflows, ensuring the highest quality across everything we generate, running multi-channel campaigns from start to finish, and maintaining rock-solid attribution tracking.

If you are obsessed with efficiency, operational speed, and using AI to scale output without ever sacrificing quality and if you thrive when given a blank slate to write your own playbook, this role is for you.

Success Metrics (First 90 Days)

  • 30 Days: Take full ownership of the existing marketing tech stack and establish baseline performance metrics.

  • 60 Days: Fully automate the core content generation pipeline and establish QA workflows.

  • 90 Days: Launch at least two multi-channel growth experiments and demonstrate a measurable reduction in CAC or an increase in content throughput.

Core Responsibilities

1. Storytelling That Converts

  • Making Complexity Clear: Take complex, often highly technical capabilities and features and turn them into clear, digestible stories without losing accuracy.

  • Audience-First Messaging: Understand who the campaigns speak to (developers, technical decision-makers, business stakeholders or end users) and frame each capability around what that audience cares about, at the right level of technical depth.

  • Spark Curiosity & Action: Craft narratives that get audiences interested and excited, and that move them to the desired conversion.

  • Product & Engineering Collaboration: Work closely with product and engineering teams to deeply understand what is being built, so every story is both compelling and technically correct.

2. Tactical Deployment & Agile Execution

  • Multi-Channel Campaign Launch: Execute and launch integrated campaigns across communities, social channels, search, newsletters, loyalty programs, influencers, paid ads and landing pages. Where needed, bring in and coordinate additional third parties to support execution, such as external PR firms and campaign support providers.

  • Marketing Automation: Maintain and scale lifecycle workflows, lead scoring mechanisms, drip sequences, and automated triggers to optimize lead conversion through the relevant funnel.

  • Rapid A/B & Multivariate Testing: Design, set up, and evaluate rapid growth experiments (copy variants, landing page layouts, audience segmentation, offer positioning) on a weekly sprint cycle.

3. AI Pipeline Operation & Content QA

description:

title: Production Planner
description:
At Harvey Performance Company, we're more than a team; we're a community. Our thriving, dynamic, and rapidly expanding organization values community, celebrates success, and fosters personal and professional growth opportunities.

Taken

The opportunity
Harvey Performance Company manufactures consumable precision cutting tools for industrial customers. We are seeking an experienced Production Planner to own production scheduling and material planning across our manufacturing operations.

This role is responsible for translating demand forecasts and customer orders into achievable production schedules, ensuring material and capacity availability through disciplined use of SAP/Epicor ERP and Material Requirements Planning (MRP), and driving on-time delivery in a fast-paced, high-volume parts production environment

In this role, you will be responsible for

  • Develop, publish, and maintain detailed production schedules across manufacturing cells/lines to meet customer demand, on-time delivery targets, and inventory objectives.
  • Own and execute Material Requirements Planning (MRP) within SAP/Epicor ERP, reviewing planned orders, exception messages, and net requirements to ensure timely material availability.
  • Maintain accuracy of SAP planning master data, including planning parameters, lead times, lot sizes, safety stock levels, BOMs, routings, etc.
  • Balance production capacity against demand forecasts and customer orders, adjusting schedules for a high-volume, high-mix precision manufacturing environment.
  • Partner with Purchasing/Supply Chain to resolve material shortages, expedite critical components, and manage supplier lead times.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering and Customer Service/Sales to resolve scheduling conflicts and support new product introductions.
  • Monitor work-in-process (WIP), backlog, and finished goods inventory; identify and drive inventory optimization opportunities.
  • Participate in and support the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process, providing planning input and capacity analysis.
  • Track and report key planning KPIs (on-time delivery, schedule adherence, machine/labor utilization, inventory turns) to operations leadership.
  • Identify, recommend, and implement continuous improvement initiatives to planning processes, systems, and data integrity (Lean/Six Sigma principles).
  • Support daily production meetings and escalating schedule risks proactively.

Vereisten

You’ll bring:

  • Minimum 5 years of production planning/scheduling experience in a high-volume parts manufacturing environment (required).
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience with SAP ERP (PP and MM modules) and Epicor for production planning and material management (required).
  • Highly competent in Material Requirements Planning (MRP) concepts, execution, and troubleshooting (required).
  • Experience in precision manufacturing, cutting tools, metalworking, or a related consumable parts industry is strongly preferred.
  • Strong analytical and Excel/data analysis skills; comfortable working with large datasets and planning reports.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and make sound decisions in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Qualification in supply chain management, Business, Industrial Engineering and advantage or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Advanced knowledge of MRP logic, demand planning, and capacity planning principles.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with a data-driven, root-cause approach.
  • Ability to read and interpret BOMs, routings, and production schedules.
  • Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

Benefits

What Harvey provides:
Do you want to get the very best out of yourself? So do we! That’s why, in addition to great colleagues and a cutting-edge high-tech environment, we offer

  • a competitive, market-based salary of €55.000,- to €65.000,-
  • a high degree of independence, responsibility, and opportunities to learn
  • an in-house fitness center
  • 26 vacation days
  • several fun company outings and parties each year
  • Occasional travel to other group/ divisional manufacturing sites

title: Business Developer B2B & Retail
description:
Bij de meeste salesbanen stopt je werk bij de afspraak. Bij MarketLeap begint het daar pas.

Ik ben Luc, mede-oprichter van MarketLeap. Wij zijn het externe salesteam van online gepositioneerde merken met een fysiek product. Onze klanten verkopen o.a. stoomreinigers, elektrische scooters, spark machines, pilates-reformers, stoelviltdoppen en autopoetsmiddelen. Wij zorgen dat die producten bij grote retailketens, groothandels en distributeurs terechtkomen, zowel nationaal als internationaal. Niet met alleen een lijst aan leads of een ingeplande afspraak, maar met een getekende deal en een product in het schap.

Onze merken vind je terug bij de Makro, Coolblue, Albert Heijn, Decathlon, Praxis, Karwei, Bouwmaat, Welkoop, Intratuin, MediaMarkt, Intersport, Sport2000, en we zitten aan tafel met grote internationale distribiteurs. Dat zijn dus niet alleen logo's op onze site, dat zijn concrete deals die ons team heeft gerealiseerd. We bestaan sinds 2023, hebben ruim 140 klanttrajecten gedraaid en zijn winstgevend. We zoeken per direct versterking van één a twee business developers voor ons team van zes business developers en twee founders in Utrecht.

Taken

Je bent de business developer van vijf tot zes merken tegelijk. Voor elk merk maak je een projectplan met heldere targets, zoek je de juiste afnemers, vindt je de beslissers, belt, mailt, plant de afspraak, voert het gesprek, maakt het voorstel en onderhandelt tot de handtekening. Daarna blijf jij het aanspreekpunt, want de herhaalorders zijn waar het geld zit, voor de klant en voor jou.

Zo ziet dit er in de praktijk uit. Zelf heb ik voor een van ons klanten een stoomreiniger bij Makro in het assortiment geplaatst, en de tweede,derde en vierde bestelling volgde. Een collega bouwde bij Decathlon een relatie op waar de orders sindsdien blijven doorlopen. In de eerste 30 dagen zorgde dit al voor tienduizenden euro's extra omzet voor onze klant.

Elke week bel je zo'n 80 tot 100 keer, ongeveer twee uur per dag. De rest van je tijd gaat naar het uitdenken van de strategie, klant management, voeren van warme gesprekken, voorstellen uitwerken, op afspraak gaan en het bijhouden van je pijplijn. Elke maandag stuur je de ondernemer achter het merk je weekplan en elke vrijdag je evaluatie. Het repeterende werk, zoals leadlijsten bouwen, research op een keten en de eerste opzet van een pitchdeck, hebben we in Claude Cowork geautomatiseerd met eigen skills. Jij werkt met HubSpot, Aircall, Apollo, Lusha, Notion en Claude, zodat je tijd gaat naar het voeren van gesprekken en closen van deals.

Hoe je start:

In je eerste maand krijg je één of twee eigen klanten. We doen niet aan een meeloopperiode van een kwartaal. Vanaf dag één heb je direct een klant waar jij verantwoordelijk voor bent. Zo leer je accountmanagement, sales en relatiebeheer op de enige manier die werkt, door het te doen. Je doet dat niet alleen. Week 1 zit je in het inwerkprogramma. Hierin neem je onze SOP's door, leer je de systemen kennen en kijk je mee bij een collega op een lopende deal. Daarna heb je een ervaren buddy die je eerste mails valideert en na je eerste gesprekken met je terugkijkt. Wekelijks krijg je salestraining en heb je een 1-op-1 met mij. Dagelijks kun je bij mij en de buddy terecht.

Vereisten

  • 2 tot 5 jaar werkervaring in een commerciële rol.
  • Je hebt al deals geclosed en kunt dit aantonen. Je hebt ook geleerd waarom een deal niet doorging en wist dit vervolgens snel te implementeren.
  • Je woont binnen een uur van Utrecht en bent drie dagen per week op kantoor.
  • Rijbewijs en een eigen auto zijn een must. Je gaat naar onze klanten en potentiële afnemers toe.
  • Vloeiend Nederlands, in spraak en op papier.
  • 40 uur per week beschikbaar, in loondienst.
  • Je neemt eigenaarschap over je pijplijn en je resultaten. Je krijgt energie van targets, deals en een product dat door jou uiteindelijk in het schap terug te vinden is.

Benefits

  • Basissalaris 3.200 tot 3.700 euro per maand, afhankelijk van ervaring.
  • De helft van de commissie die wij factureren over deals die jij sluit. Ook over elke herhaalorder, twee tot drie jaar lang. Geen plafond.
  • Extra bonussen bij grote wins.
  • Kilometervergoeding van €0,23,-per kilometer.
  • 25 vakantiedagen
  • Interne salestraining en dagelijks aan het werk met de nieuwste AI-tooling, ingericht voor dit werk.
  • Een hecht team van zes business developers en twee founders, 28 lopende klant trajecten, winstgevend en groeiend.
  • Hybride: drie dagen kantoor in Utrecht, twee dagen thuis.
  • Regelmatige leuke teamuitjes en sportieve activiteiten zoals padel.

Herken je jezelf hierin? Stuur je CV en drie regels over een deal waar je het meest trots op bent. Binnen twee werkdagen hoor je van mij. Daarna plannen we een belafspraak in van 20 a 30 minuten, gevolgd door een gesprek op kantoor in Utrecht met mij en een van de business developers. Bij een match vanuit beide kanten ontvang je een concreet aanbod. Van sollicitatie tot handtekening duurt zo'n twee weken en eventueel sneller als het kan.

Luc Broos, mede-oprichter MarketLeap

title: Senior CRM & Lifecycle Analyst (B2C) – Marketing Automation (all genders)

Du verbindest strategisches Denken, analytische Tiefe und operative Umsetzung: Du entwickelst Hypothesen, übersetzt sie in intelligente Segmente und automatisierte Journeys, analysierst die Ergebnisse und leitest daraus die nächsten Maßnahmen ab. Dabei hast du die Zusammenhänge und Abläufe der relevanten Systeme und Datenquellen im Blick.

Foodji ist dabei kein klassischer Onlineshop: Jeder Foodji hat individuelle Stocklevels und Produktkombinationen. Genau das macht CRM bei uns besonders spannend. Du entwickelst dynamische, hochgradig segmentierte Kampagnen und nutzt Daten, um die Kommunikation kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.

Deine Mission bei Foodji:

  • Aufbau einer skalierbaren CRM- und Lifecycle-Funktion im B2C-Bereich sowie Übernahme der strategischen und operativen Verantwortung.

  • Verantwortung für den vollständigen Kampagnen-Lifecycle: von Hypothese und Konzeption über Segmentierung, A/B-Tests und Kohorten bis zum Aufbau, zur Analyse und zur Iteration automatisierter Flows.

  • Entwicklung dynamischer Segmente und Journeys, die unterschiedliche Stocklevels, Produktkombinationen und Nutzerbedürfnisse berücksichtigen.

  • Eigenständige Analyse von Daten, Identifikation relevanter Hebel und Priorisierung von Maßnahmen nach ihrem erwarteten Impact.

  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Product, Tech und Analytics, um Daten und technische Möglichkeiten für relevante CRM-Maßnahmen zu nutzen.

  • Verständnis der Zusammenhänge zwischen CRM-Systemen, Datenquellen und technischen Abläufen sowie Mitgestaltung der CRM-Systemlandschaft.

  • Mitgestaltung der CRM-Systemlandschaft sowie sichere Anwendung von Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze oder vergleichbaren Marketing-Automation-Plattformen als Core User.

  • Hands-on-Umsetzung von Maßnahmen – von der Konzeption und dem Flow-Aufbau bis zur Auswertung und Optimierung.


DAS BRINGST DU MIT

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung in CRM, Lifecycle Marketing, Marketing Automation oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich.

  • Praktische Erfahrung mit dem vollständigen Kampagnen-Lifecycle – von Hypothese und Konzeption über komplexe Segmentierung, Kohorten und Flow-Aufbau bis zu Analyse und Iteration.

  • Starke analytische Arbeitsweise und ausgeprägte Daten-Affinität sowie Erfahrung mit A/B-Tests, Kohortenanalysen oder vergleichbaren Experimenten.

  • Erfahrung mit komplexen Segmenten und automatisierten Journeys in einem datengetriebenen CRM- oder Lifecycle-Umfeld.

  • Sehr gute Anwenderkenntnisse in Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze oder einer vergleichbaren CRM- beziehungsweise Marketing-Automation-Plattform.

  • Technisches Grundverständnis für die Zusammenhänge und Abläufe von CRM-Systemen, Marketing-Automation-Plattformen und relevanten Datenquellen.

  • Strategische und operative Arbeitsweise: Du identifizierst Hebel, setzt Prioritäten und setzt Maßnahmen selbstständig um.

  • Sichere Kommunikation auf Deutsch oder Englisch in Wort und Schrift.

Noch Fragen?

Wir freuen uns auf deine Nachricht und helfen dir gerne weiter!

DAS BIETEN WIR DIR

  • Office Foodji: Immer bestens versorgt bei uns im Office

  • bAV: Mit der Degura Pension Cloud sichern und bezuschussen wir jetzt schon deine Rente

  • Spendit Card: Wir stocken dein Gehalt auf! Mit Spendit stehen dir bis zu fünfzig Euro netto im Monat on top zur freien Verfügung

  • EGYM Wellpass: Mit uns bleibst du fit & wir bringen dich deutschlandweit in die angesagtesten Fitness- und Wellnessstudios

  • JobRad: Spring mit uns aufs Rad und lease dir dein Traumrad oder Pedelec

  • KITA/Kiga Kostenzuschuss: Wir bezuschussen deine Kosten für die Kinderbetreuung, damit deine Kinder immer bestens versorgt sind

  • Mitarbeiterrabatte: Du erhältst attraktive Promotions und Discounts verschiedener Brands

  • Food Tastings: Teste dich mit unserem Foodteam durch unsere Produkte und gestalte unser Sortiment von morgen

  • Development: Deine Weiterentwicklung liegt uns am Herzen und mit regelmäßigen Feedbackgesprächen und Trainings bieten wir dir spannende Perspektiven!

  • Flexwork: Arbeite 30 Tage im Jahr aus dem EU Ausland

  • Top Office Lage: Genieße eine erstklassige Arbeitsumgebung im Münchener Glockenbachviertel mit der Isar vor der Tür

  • Team Events: Wir sind ein Team - beim Skiday, Frühstück, Culture Week oder Office Party feiern wir gemeinsam!

ÜBER UNS

Hi, schön, dass du da bist! Wir sind Foodji - ein Team aus Food-Lovern & Tech-Nerds.

Unsere Mission ist es, frisches, gesundes und vor allem leckeres Essen überall dort anzubieten, wo Menschen den Großteil ihres Alltags verbringen – in Büros, ganz gleich, ob im Gewerbegebiet oder mitten in der Stadt, während langer Schichten im Krankenhaus oder in den Tiefen einer Produktionshalle, in der rund um die Uhr Menschen arbeiten. Überall bieten wir vollwertige Gerichte, Snacks und Getränke genau dort an, wo und wann du sie brauchst.

Proprietäre Technologien, selbstlernende Algorithmen und effiziente Lieferketten helfen uns dabei, das Paradox zwischen frischem Essen, Verfügbarkeit und Nachhaltigkeit aufzulösen. Mit unserer eigens entwickelten Technologieplattform optimieren wir die Mengenplanung und sagen Food Waste den Kampf an. Wir wollen einen positiven Effekt erzielen – auf die Umwelt, den Alltag unserer Kund:innen und unsere Communities. Deshalb spenden wir übrig gebliebene Gerichte an Foodsharing und andere soziale Initiativen direkt vor unserer Haustür.

Als Marktführer versorgen wir mit Foodji bereits täglich Tausende Menschen in ganz Deutschland. Zu unseren Kund:innen zählen unter anderem der Münchner Flughafen, Klarna, Enpal und Wingcopter. Und wir fangen gerade erst an: Allein in Deutschland gibt es mehr als 100.000 relevante Standorte für uns.

Trage auch du deinen Teil dazu bei und bewirb dich jetzt.
