description:
About Us

Base360.ai is the AI operating system for short-term rental businesses, helping property managers run their operations on autopilot.

Born out of The Flex, a short-term rental operator that scaled to an eight-figure business using its own software, Base360.ai is now launching as a standalone platform for short-term rental operators worldwide.

We bring reservations, guest communication, pricing, payments, cleaning, maintenance, and reporting into one platform—helping operators automate manual work, reduce costs, increase revenue, and scale their portfolios.

We're looking for an ambitious Senior Full-Stack Product Engineer who wants to turn real customer problems into intuitive, reliable software. You'll work closely with founders, designers, and operators to identify what matters, build solutions, and improve them based on how people use them.

If you enjoy owning the full journey from customer problem to shipped product—and you're excited by AI, automation, and short-term rentals—we want to meet you.

What You'll Build

As a Senior Full-Stack Product Engineer, you'll help shape and scale Base360.ai across the entire short-term rental lifecycle.

You'll build customer-facing features, operational dashboards, automation engines, AI-powered workflows, and integrations that help property managers grow without increasing their workload at the same rate.

Your work will connect what users see with the systems behind it—from a guest’s check-in experience to the workflows coordinating reservations, cleaning, payments, and owner reporting.

Your Mission

Understand Customer Problems

Work directly with property managers and internal teams to understand their workflows, identify friction, and decide which problems are worth solving.

Build Products End-to-End

Take features from idea and prototype through frontend, backend, integrations, testing, and deployment. Own the complete experience and how it performs in production.

Create Intuitive User Experiences

Work with designers to make complex short-term rental operations easy to manage. Build interfaces that help users complete tasks quickly and confidently.

Create Powerful Automations

Build event-driven workflows that eliminate repetitive work—from scheduling cleaning after a booking to sending check-in instructions and generating owner statements.

Develop AI-Powered Features

Use LLMs and AI agents to automate guest communication, triage maintenance requests, support pricing decisions, and help operators manage their portfolios more efficiently.

Connect the Ecosystem

Build reliable APIs and integrations with platforms including Airbnb, Hostaway, Stripe, Twilio, OpenAI, Google, and other partners across the short-term rental ecosystem.

Solve Real Operational Problems

Build solutions for:

  • Real-time reservation and availability synchronization

  • Dynamic pricing intelligence

  • Smart lock access and key management

  • Automated guest communication across channels

  • Guest check-in and upsell journeys

  • Operational forecasting

  • Cleaning and maintenance automation

  • Owner reporting and financial workflows

  • AI-powered monitoring and alerts

Measure and Improve

Use customer feedback, product usage, and operational results to evaluate what you ship. Improve features based on adoption, time saved, fewer errors, and better user outcomes.

Build for Scale

Make sound technical decisions that balance delivery speed, maintainability, security, and reliability as more operators and properties join the platform.

We care more about capability than specific technologies, but our current stack includes:

  • Python

  • React

  • TypeScript

  • Supabase

  • PostgreSQL

  • AWS

  • Serverless architecture

  • OpenAI APIs

  • Twilio

  • Stripe

  • Docker

  • GitHub Actions

You Might Be a Great Fit If You Have

  • Strong experience building and shipping production software

  • The ability to work across frontend and backend systems

  • Experience with React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, or similar technologies

  • Strong understanding of APIs, databases, integrations, and cloud architecture

  • A product mindset and curiosity about why users need a feature

  • Good judgment around usability, scope, and technical trade-offs

  • The ability to turn an ambiguous problem into a practical, working solution

  • Confidence working directly with customers, designers, and founders

  • The ability to work independently and own outcomes

  • Curiosity about AI, automation, and operational efficiency

  • A bias toward shipping, learning, and iterating

Bonus points for experience with:

  • Short-term rentals, hospitality technology, or property management systems

  • Multi-tenant SaaS platforms

  • Marketplace businesses and booking channel integrations

  • AI agents and workflow automation

  • Product analytics and experimentation

  • Event-driven architectures

  • Supabase

  • AWS serverless infrastructure

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

  • You've shipped features that property managers actively use

  • Core short-term rental workflows are automated through products you've built

  • Customers spend less time on manual administration and repetitive tasks

  • Complex workflows become easier to understand and complete

  • Integrations move reservations, availability, payments, and operational data reliably

  • AI-powered features become part of customers’ everyday operations

  • Customer feedback and usage data consistently inform your product decisions

  • Your work helps operators grow their portfolios, improve guest experiences, and operate more profitably

Why Join Us

Build Something Meaningful

Solve problems experienced daily by short-term rental operators, with direct access to The Flex’s operations to test ideas and see their impact.

Own the Product Outcome

Help decide what to build, how it should work, and how to measure its success. Take responsibility for features from the first conversation through ongoing improvement.

Small Team, Massive Opportunity

Work closely with the founders and directly influence the product and technical direction of Base360.ai.

Learn Faster

Solve real-world challenges across product, software, AI, automation, hospitality operations, and scale.

Performance-Based Rewards

Competitive compensation with substantial upside for exceptional performers.

Remote-First

Work from anywhere. We care about outcomes, not hours.

Born out of The Flex, a short-term rental operator that scaled to an eight-figure business using its own software, Base360.ai is now launching as a standalone platform for short-term rental operators worldwide.

We bring reservations, guest communication, pricing, payments, cleaning, maintenance, and reporting into one platform—helping operators automate manual work, reduce costs, increase revenue, and scale their portfolios.

We're looking for a highly ambitious Senior Software Engineer who wants to build systems that solve real problems at scale. You'll build, ship, automate, and deliver products that directly impact property managers, their teams, and their guests.

If you're excited by APIs, automation, AI agents, cloud infrastructure, and building products from the ground up, we want to meet you.

What You'll Build

As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll help architect and scale Base360.ai—the platform powering every aspect of a short-term rental business.

You'll build customer-facing products, automation engines, AI-powered workflows, integrations, and operational systems that help property managers grow without increasing their workload at the same rate.

Your work will span the entire short-term rental lifecycle: from listing distribution, pricing, and bookings to guest stays, property operations, and financial reporting.

Your Mission

Build the Core Platform

Design and develop scalable applications, services, and APIs that power reservations, availability, pricing, payments, guest experiences, and property operations.

Create Powerful Automations

Build event-driven workflows that eliminate repetitive work—from scheduling cleaning after a booking to sending check-in instructions and generating owner statements.

Develop AI-Powered Systems

Use LLMs and AI agents to automate guest communication, triage maintenance requests, support pricing decisions, and help operators manage their portfolios more efficiently.

Design API-First Architecture

Create robust APIs that connect internal services, booking channels, third-party providers, and customer systems.

Integrate the Ecosystem

Build and maintain integrations with platforms including Airbnb, Hostaway, Stripe, Twilio, OpenAI, Google, and other strategic partners across the short-term rental ecosystem.

Scale Infrastructure

Deploy and manage cloud-native infrastructure designed for reliability, performance, and global growth across multiple property management businesses.

Solve Complex Operational Problems

Build solutions for:

  • Real-time reservation and availability synchronization

  • Dynamic pricing intelligence

  • Smart lock access and key management

  • Automated guest communication across channels

  • Operational forecasting

  • Cleaning and maintenance automation

  • Owner reporting and financial workflows

  • AI-powered monitoring and alerts

Move Fast and Own Delivery

Own projects end-to-end—from understanding an operator’s problem to architecture, implementation, deployment, and ongoing improvement.

Bring senior engineering judgment to technical decisions, code reviews, and the reliability of the systems you build.

Tech Stack

We care more about capability than specific technologies, but our current stack includes:

  • Python

  • FastAPI

  • React

  • TypeScript

  • Supabase

  • PostgreSQL

  • AWS

  • Serverless architecture

  • OpenAI APIs

  • Twilio

  • Stripe

  • Docker

  • GitHub Actions

You Might Be a Great Fit If You Have

  • Strong experience building and owning production-grade software systems

  • Experience with FastAPI, Python, React, or similar frameworks

  • Strong understanding of APIs, distributed systems, and cloud architecture

  • Experience designing scalable backend systems and reliable data models

  • The ability to work independently and make sound technical decisions

  • Strong problem-solving skills and a product mindset

  • Curiosity about AI, automation, and operational efficiency

  • A bias toward action, shipping, and learning from real users

  • The ability to balance delivery speed with maintainability and reliability

Bonus points for experience with:

  • Short-term rentals, hospitality technology, or property management systems

  • Multi-tenant SaaS platforms

  • Marketplace businesses and booking channel integrations

  • AI agents and workflow automation

  • Event-driven architectures

  • Supabase

  • AWS serverless infrastructure

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

  • Core short-term rental workflows are automated through systems you've built

  • Property managers spend less time on manual administration

  • Reservations, availability, payments, and operational data move reliably between systems

  • New integrations are deployed and maintained reliably

  • AI-powered workflows become part of customers’ everyday operations

  • The platform supports more operators and properties while maintaining reliability and performance

  • Base360.ai helps customers grow their portfolios, improve guest experiences, and operate more profitably

Why Join Us

Build Something Meaningful

Solve problems experienced daily by short-term rental operators, with direct access to The Flex’s operations to test ideas and see their impact.

Extreme Ownership

Have the freedom and responsibility to make technical decisions and deliver systems that matter.

Small Team, Massive Opportunity

Learn Faster

Solve real-world challenges across software, AI, automation, hospitality operations, and scale.

Performance-Based Rewards

Competitive compensation with substantial upside for exceptional performers.

Remote-First

Work from anywhere. We care about outcomes, not hours.

  • You need detailed instructions for every task

description:
Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

About the role:

In this high-impact role, you will be instrumental in the development of next-generation verification features, deploying intelligent, production-ready solutions by leveraging state-of-the-art Orchestration technologies as well as Generative AI and Computer Vision technologies.
You will be expected to work closely and collaboratively with Product, DevOps, DataScientist, and Data teams to ensure successful, end-to-end delivery of these solutions, while constantly researching and integrating emerging technologies. A core part of your contribution will be safeguarding data integrity and ensuring compliance, and translating complex data insights into clear, actionable recommendations for stakeholders to support informed, data-driven decision-making across Checkout.com.

What you will be doing:
• Drive the design and development of innovative, complex and scalable applications for real-world identity verification challenges in a wider microservices using industry best practices.
• Take full ownership of new and existing features and service, managing the end-to-end lifecycle from initial conceptualization and design through to deployment and monitoring in a production environment.
• Actively collaborate with cross-functional teams (Engineering, Product, Risk) across the company to maximize the positive impact of data science initiatives.
• Champion a culture of technical excellence, cross-team learning, and knowledge sharing within the Data organization.
• Be part of, and collaborate with, cross-functional teams including product management, across a large engineering community.
• Write clean, maintainable, extendable and testable code on some of Checkout’s most impactful systems.
• Build, own and operate your systems to the highest levels of resilience and service.
• Mentor junior team members and assist in their technical development

What are we looking for:
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
• Over 5 years of experience as a Software Engineer working with complex, large-scale, and diversified applications and tech stacks.
• Proficiency in C# .NET, with a strong understanding of software development principles in either a backend or full stack environment.
• Great communication skills and ability to interact effectively with a wide range of stakeholders
• Experience working in agile environments and delivering high-quality code within tight deadlines
• Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team
• Someone who is AI proficient or AI curious, you will be hungry to embrace what the latest technology has to offer to enhance yours and your teams productivity
• Payments or financial knowledge is a plus, but not a necessity
• French language proficiency at a minimum B2 level

Bonus Points:
• Experience with Cloud and Infrastructure technologies like AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, prometheus...
• Experience with Databases like Postgresql, Mongo, Redis, ...
• Direct experience solving real-world business problems through innovative, data-driven approaches.
• Any experience in other programming languages not mentioned above.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

title: Ingénieur.e de recherche (H/F) - CDD 12 mois
description:
ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE :

École du ministère en charge de l'industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines- Télécom, 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l'avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses 4 missions - former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l'innovation - en un cercle vertueux et porteur d'innovation.

Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche la place IMT Mines Albi comme école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT, à savoir l’industrie du futur responsable, l’énergie, économie circulaire et société ainsi que l’ingénierie, santé et bien-être.

IMT Mines Albi s‘est dotée en 2023 et pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en 7 grandes actions, répondant ainsi aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT à laquelle elle appartient.

IMT Mines Albi, au travers du Centre Génie Industriel (CGI), développe des recherches à la frontière entre l’intelligence artificielle et le génie industriel, en collaboration avec des partenaires publics et industriels nationaux et internationaux.

Le Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) (https://cgi.imt-mines-albi.fr/) compte environ 70 personnes dont 25 doctorants. Le centre s’intéresse à l’accompagnement de la transition des écosystèmes en permettant de prendre des décisions responsables et durables, dans des environnements instables ou perturbés. Ceci est mis en pratique par la représentation, la modélisation et l’analyse des données de ces organisations afin de formaliser de la connaissance conduisant à la prise de décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs, incertains et/ou perturbés.

Le CGI est structuré selon des axes de recherche appliquée et des programmes scientifiques. Les axes de recherche appliquée sont :

  • Axe FLOWS : Flexible Logistics and Operations for sustainable WorldS dans lequel ce poste est rattaché.

  • Axe DiSCS : Digital Systems for Crisis management and Security ;

  • Axe TRACE : Territorial Resilience, Agility, and Circular Economy ;

  • Axe WHOPS : Well-being and Health through Organizational Processes and Services.

Les deux programmes scientifiques au cœur de ces axes de recherche sont :

  • HOPOPOP : Hybridization for Operations & Planning, Organizations & Performance, Optimization & Problem-solving ; 

  • AIME-DM : Automated Information Modeling and Extraction for Decision-Makers.

 

DESCRIPTION DU POSTE :

Dans le contexte de l’Education 4.0, les différents acteurs d’un établissement de formation universitaire (étudiants, personnels, intervenants extérieurs, etc.) ont des contraintes et des objectifs différents ce qui rend complexe la coordination et le pilotage de tels établissements (organisation et planification des enseignements, gestion des espaces collectifs, organisation des sessions d’examens…).

En complément, ces établissements doivent s’adapter tant sur la gestion de leurs sites (meilleure adéquation à de nouvelles formes pédagogiques) que sur les flux de personnes les utilisant pour une meilleure répartition des charges et une interopérabilité de tous les outils à disposition (par exemple, un gestionnaire d’emploi du temps). Dans ce cadre, le jumeau numérique organisationnel représente le système qui permet une simulation et une aide à la prise de décision par des échanges bidirectionnels entre l’organisation physique (personnes et systèmes dont les bâtiments) et sa réplique virtuelle dans un objectif de pilotage global des flux.

Le projet DIGIFAC’Santé s’inscrit dans ce contexte. Il porte sur la conception et le développement d'un jumeau numérique des sites d’une université, de la gestion des flux étudiants et personnels et de l’évolution pédagogique de ses formations.

Un jumeau numérique ne peut remplir son rôle qu'à la condition de représenter fidèlement les informations essentielles à la prise de décision, elles-mêmes issues de données collectées dans les différents services de l’Université et des applications logicielles actuelles. Or, ces applications présentent des niveaux d’hétérogénéité différents selon leurs fonctionnalités. La nature des opérations réalisées (emploi du temps, gestion des salles et du matériel, etc.) impose des contraintes fortes sur la disponibilité de ces données : leur collecte automatique et en temps réel n'est pas toujours techniquement envisageable, ce qui constitue un défi central pour l'alimentation du jumeau numérique.

L’étude à mener dans le cadre de ce projet vise à :

Modéliser le besoin informationnel. Il s'agit de concevoir un méta-modèle capable de représenter, de façon générique et formelle, les informations strictement nécessaires à l’alimentation du jumeau numérique universitaire. Ce méta-modèle doit permettre de cadrer la remontée d'information en définissant le juste besoin, c'est-à-dire en distinguant ce qui relève de l'information décisionnelle de ce qui constitue un artefact de collecte sans valeur ajoutée pour le pilotage.

Alimenter les modèles. Une fois le méta-modèle du besoin informationnel établi, la question de son instanciation à partir de données réelles des applications existantes se pose. Comment alimenter ces modèles à partir de données hétérogènes, partielles, et produites selon des rythmes et des modalités de collecte variables ? Ceci articule des enjeux d'intégration, de qualité et de cohérence de la donnée au regard des exigences du jumeau numérique.

Gérer l'absence de certaines données. Dans un contexte où certaines opérations ne permettent pas une collecte automatique et en temps réel, en raison de la nature même des processus mis en place (par exemple, construction de l’emploi du temps, suivi des cohortes d’étudiants), comment maintenir la cohérence et la complétude de la représentation portée par le jumeau numérique ? Ce lot interroge la capacité du système à pallier les lacunes de la remontée de données par des mécanismes d'inférence ou de déduction, permettant de reconstituer un état vraisemblable du système à partir d'informations partielles.

Proposer des aides au dimensionnement et au pilotage des sites universitaires. Il s’agit ici d’utiliser le jumeau numérique dans toutes ses fonctionnalités afin entres autres de s’assurer que les évolutions bâtimentaires envisagées permettent d’accueillir l’ensemble des flux actuel et projeté pour cet établissement, de permettre d’optimiser les flux entre les différents sites et de valider les choix d’évolution des pratiques pédagogiques et leur adéquation vis à vis des capacités disponibles (salles et équipements spécifiques, surfaces, personnels,etc.).

Compétences, connaissances et expériences souhaitables :

  • Modélisation des processus / d’organisation

  • Analyse systémique

  • Analyse de données

  • Ingénierie dirigée par les modèles

  • Aide à la décision

  • Simulation à évènements discrets et jumeau numérique

  • Fouille de processus (process mining),

  • Des connaissances en algorithmique, UML, Web sémantique seront très appréciées

Capacités et aptitudes :

  • Anglais écrit et parlé (Niveau B2 minimum exigé) ; cf. référentiel européen ; ex. :  785/990 minimum au TOEIC), attesté par une certification reconnue (TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS).

  • La maîtrise du français (C1 minimum) est exigée afin de faciliter les échanges avec les experts et les acteurs.

  • Capacité à travailler dans une équipe de recherche, autonomie, esprit d’initiative, organisation, curiosité intellectuelle…

  • Motivation pour contribuer à une application universitaire

 

PROFIL RECHERCHE :

Ingénieur.e recherche ou post-doctorant, en génie industriel et/ou supply chain management et/ou Génie Logiciel ou Master ou équivalent (niveau Bac+5).

 

AU-DELÀ DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT PROFESSIONNEL, POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE ? :

  • cadre de travail agréable dans un campus de 22 ha

  • 49 jours de congés par an

  • restauration administrative sur place

  • aide à la mobilité durable pour le transport domicile-travail

  • action sociale (protection sociale complémentaire et aide aux familles)

 

INFORMATIONS COMPLÉMENTAIRES :

Le poste est basé à IMT Mines Albi, Centre Génie Industriel, Albi (France). Des déplacements sont à prévoir sur le site du partenaire du projet à Toulouse (Haute Garonne), France.

Head of DC Operations (H/F)

Région parisienne

Votre mission

Dans un environnement où la disponibilité et la fiabilité des infrastructures sont essentielles, Isatalent recherche un(e) Head of DC Operations pour piloter les opérations de ses data centers en région parisienne.

Rattaché(e) à la direction, vous êtes garant(e) de la performance opérationnelle, de la continuité de service et de la fiabilité des infrastructures. Vous encadrez les responsables de site et travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d'expertise centrales, les clients et les partenaires de maintenance.

Dans un contexte de croissance de l'entreprise et d'exigences opérationnelles, vous jouez un rôle clé dans l'harmonisation des pratiques, la structuration du pilotage des activités et l'accompagnement du changement auprès des équipes.

Votre objectif : construire une vision opérationnelle consolidée, maîtriser les risques et fédérer les équipes autour d'exigences communes de performance, de sécurité et de qualité de service.

Vos responsabilités

Piloter la stratégie et la performance des opérations multisites

  • Élaborer une feuille de route opérationnelle à court et moyen terme, en définissant les priorités, les plans d'action et les ressources humaines et financières nécessaires.

  • Définir et harmoniser les méthodes de pilotage des activités opérationnelles sur l'ensemble des sites.

  • Consolider et faire évoluer les KPI et tableaux de bord portant notamment sur la disponibilité des infrastructures, la maintenance, la communication client et le respect des procédures.

  • Analyser les résultats, identifier les écarts de performance et piloter les actions correctives.

  • Produire un reporting structuré à destination de la direction et éclairer les décisions stratégiques.

Manager les responsables de site et accompagner la transformation

  • Encadrer et accompagner les responsables de site dans le pilotage de leurs activités et le développement de leurs compétences.

  • Apporter une expertise opérationnelle et technique permettant de challenger les choix, les priorités et les plans d'action.

  • Favoriser l'autonomie, la responsabilisation et la coopération des équipes.

  • Organiser l'allocation des ressources et le suivi des plans de charge.

  • Accompagner la réorganisation du périmètre, harmoniser les pratiques et contribuer à l'intégration de nouveaux sites.

  • Travailler en transversalité avec le responsable du pôle Expertise et les autres fonctions de l'entreprise.

Garantir la fiabilité des infrastructures et maîtriser les risques

  • Garantir la disponibilité, la résilience et la continuité d'exploitation des infrastructures critiques.

  • Superviser la maintenance préventive, corrective et réglementaire, ainsi que les travaux, extensions, rétrofits et changements réalisés en environnement exploité.

  • Reprendre et consolider la cartographie des risques opérationnels et techniques, notamment les points uniques de défaillance (SPOF) et les obsolescences critiques.

  • Hiérarchiser les risques, définir les plans de traitement, en évaluer les impacts financiers et humains et identifier les investissements nécessaires.

  • Piloter les incidents majeurs, les escalades, les analyses de causes et le suivi des actions correctives et préventives.

  • Garantir le respect des exigences de sécurité, de conformité et de continuité de service.

Développer la relation client et le partenariat avec les mainteneurs

  • Garantir le respect des engagements contractuels, des SLA et des standards de qualité attendus par les clients.

description:

Avec 900 000 clients en janvier 2026 (x3 en 2025), Pennylane évolue dans un contexte d'hyper croissance.

L'équipe commerciale joue un rôle primordial dans la recherche et la signature de nouveaux contrats.

Dans ce contexte, l’équipe AE Small Business gère des prospects provenant essentiellement du site web, ayant commencé le funnel self-signup, mais n’ayant pas réussi/terminé la souscription.
A partir d'informations qualitatives, leur objectif est de les signer (en partie en direct par appel) pour générer du MRR. Le volume actuel géré est de 2 500 leads par mois.

Contexte 2026

L’équipe Account Executive Small Business grandit vite et se structure.

Il va y avoir une augmentation du volume à gérer, des process à mettre en place, en parallèle d’un besoin de coaching important (équipe presque entièrement renouvelée, avec des profils relativement juniors sur la partie closing).

L'équipe grandit vite et atteint désormais 10 personnes. Pour continuer à scaler sans sacrifier la qualité du management et du coaching, nous avons besoin d'un·e Team Lead AE Small Business qui prendra en charge 5 SBS en direct, permettant à Thomas de se concentrer sur les 5 autres membres, la stratégie, et la coordination globale de l'équipe.

Comment vas-tu contribuer au projet ?

En tant que Team Lead Account Executive Small Business, tu assureras un rôle de management d'une équipe d’AE full-cycle sur le segment des petites entreprises (0-5 salariés). Tu seras garant·e de la performance de ton pod de 5 AEs, de leur montée en compétences et de l'atteinte des objectifs MRR collectifs.

Quelles seront tes missions au quotidien ?

Management d'équipe

  • Piloter et développer un pod de 5 AE Small

  • Pilotage de la performance

    • Suivre les KPIs clés : volume d’activité, MRR signé, taux de conversion, nombre de deals closés, vitesse de traitement des leads - et garantir leur atteinte

    • Remonter les insights terrain et proposer des actions correctives

    • Participer à l'effort de vente en prenant part aux appels avec l'équipe

  • Structuration & amélioration continue

    • Contribuer à l'amélioration continue du contacting et du discours commercial

    • Tester de nouvelles approches et partager les bonnes pratiques avec l'ensemble de l'équipe

    • Aider à la mise en place et au respect de la sales policy

    • Collaborer avec les équipes SDR, Marketing, Ops & Data pour fluidifier la transmission des leads (leur qualité, conversion), et optimiser le fonctionnement du département

  • Être un relais terrain

    • Faire remonter les feedbacks produit et commerciaux aux équipes internes

    • Être l'interface entre son pod et les équipes transverses (Care, Onboarding, Ops)

  • Expérience commerciale confirmée :

    • 3+ ans de closing B2B (ou B2C),

    • Idéalement dans un contexte de volume élevé, cycle court et full-cycle

  • Track record MRR/closing : Capacité prouvée à atteindre et dépasser des objectifs de revenus récurrents

  • Expérience en management : 1+ an de management d'équipe ou expérience TL/mentor (idéalement 3-5 personnes) — une forte expérience opérationnelle et de mentoring peut compenser une expérience sans management

  • Data-driven : À l'aise avec les outils CRM (Salesforce), analytics (Metabase) et la gestion par les KPIs

Compétences relationnelles

  • Coach : Capacité à analyser la performance, construire et suivre des plans d’actions/coaching

  • Excellence commerciale : Aisance téléphonique, écoute active, capacité à closer rapidement dans un contexte "low touch"

  • Esprit collaboratif : Capacité à travailler avec des équipes transverses

  • Adaptabilité : À l'aise dans un environnement scale-up en forte croissance

Qualités personnelles

  • Orientation résultats : Ambition et envie de dépasser les objectifs individuels et collectifs

  • Pédagogie : Envie de former, de transmettre et de faire grandir son équipe

  • Proactivité : Force de proposition sur les process, le discours, la performance

  • Résilience : Capacité à gérer le rythme élevé (volume de leads, pression MRR) tout en maintenant l'énergie de son pod

title: Senior Revenue Ops
description:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

⭐️ The Senior Revenue Operations job

Our Business Strategy & Operations team runs the most critical, strategic, and data-driven projects at Alan. It sits at the intersection of Sales, Product, and Finance, and covers four core areas: sales strategy and planning, sales effectiveness, sales enablement, and business segment leadership.

You'll be joining the Sales Effectiveness team, whose mission is to make our sales organization run at its best across France, Belgium, Spain, and Canada. This team is a key lever on one of the company's most watched metrics: our customer acquisition cost.

Why is this role interesting?

  • High-impact scope: You'll work across the full sales organization, from Account Executives to BDRs, Account Management, and Customer Success Managers.

  • Real ownership: You'll own initiatives end to end, from strategy and design to execution and adoption, not just delivery.

  • Builder's playground: You'll have access to a modern stack, combining low-code tools, AI (Dust, Claude), Salesforce, and SQL, to ship things fast and at scale.

  • Tangible results: Recent examples from our roadmap include fully automating slide deck generation for Sales (saving 1,000+ hours per year) and building an AI-powered outbound machine reaching a 15% discovery rate.

What will you do with us?

Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.

  • Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

  • Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

  • Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

  • Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

  • Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

  • Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

  • Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

It is also most of what a protein costs to make, which makes procurement one of the biggest levers on gross margin in the business.

So far scientists have bought what they need, decisions get made in hours, and nothing blocks an experiment. That was the right trade while we were proving the thing works. But we are multiplying lab throughput several times over, and at that volume procurement becomes a discipline: real terms with the suppliers we already buy from heavily, qualified second sources where we currently have one, inventory that is planned rather than remembered. Nobody has taken that on yet.

You would be our first dedicated supply chain hire, and it is hands-on — you do the sourcing and the negotiating yourself. What You'll Do

  • Own procurement end to end. Every input to the lab, from gene synthesis down to gloves. Requests, POs, receiving, vendor onboarding, the lot.

  • Negotiate. Build the supplier relationships across our DNA, reagent, biosensor and catalog-protein vendors, put volume commitments and pricing agreements in place, and go get the margin back.

  • Drive down the cost of a protein. Go category by category and take cost out of each. A few francs per protein, multiplied across the volumes we are heading toward, is a seven-figure line.

  • Stay ahead of the science. When R&D says they are adding a new assay next quarter, you should already be sourcing the reagents for it.

  • Set inventory policy, and make the numbers true. Reorder points and safety stock, so we never stall a customer experiment on a stockout and never have six figures of reagents quietly expiring in a freezer. You decide what should be on the shelves and how much of it.

  • Plan supply for the lab expansion. Model what several-fold throughput actually needs — volumes, lead times, storage, cash tied up in stock — and have it in place before the capacity comes online, not after.

  • Own landed cost. Shipping, customs, import duties, VAT recoverability, cold chain. We import a lot of biology into Switzerland and both the cost and the failure modes matter.

Every franc you take out of the cost of a protein, and every week you take out of a lead time, shows up directly in what we can offer customers and in whether AI-designed biology is cheap enough to be worth doing at scale. description:
Sécheron Hasler Group is a global leader in railway and industrial electrification systems, offering cutting-edge solutions to enhance transportation and decarbonize industrial processes. With a rich heritage of over a century and a commitment to innovation, Sécheron Hasler Group is growing worldwide.

For the Electrical Safety Solutions (ESS) Business Unit, we are looking for an experienced marketing professional with a strong interest in technical products and industrial markets. The Senior Product Marketing & Exhibitions Specialist will translate ESS business priorities and product value propositions into clear marketing communications, sales tools, product training and customer-facing materials. The candidate will work closely with the Business Development Manager, Product Line Managers, Sales and the Sécheron Hasler Group Marketing Team.

Global objectives:

  • Drive the execution of the ESS marketing plan and business growth priorities, in cooperation with the Business Development Manager, Product Line Managers and Sales.
  • Develop and maintain marketing and sales materials for existing and new products and applications.
  • Develop product marketing communication using various communication channels to promote ESS and its respective products.
  • Work with the Sécheron Hasler Group Marketing Team for trade shows/fairs and manage the required preparation and coordination with the respective Business Unit teams.
  • Provide marketing inputs and product communication materials to support Product Line Managers and Sales.

Key responsibilities:

  • Develop and deliver marketing communication plans based on ESS business priorities agreed with the Business Development Manager.
  • Contribute to product launch plans defined with the Business Development Manager and Product Line Managers; coordinate the preparation and delivery of marketing materials, training and communication activities
  • Develop marketing and sales materials, including commercial brochures, PowerPoint presentations, promotional videos and animations for products and applications, and website content.
  • Collect and structure market and competitor information; prepare customer-oriented product messages, competitive comparisons and sales enablement materials in collaboration with the Business Development Manager and Product Line Managers.
  • Develop product training materials with Product Line Managers and support training for the worldwide Sales network.
  • Maintain product documentation for intranet and corporate purposes.
  • Coordinate annual exhibition and trade show preparation within ESS, based on priorities agreed with the Business Development Manager and Sales, and in alignment with the Sécheron Hasler Group Marketing Team.
  • Develop marketing concepts, communication campaigns, exhibition experiences, templates and customer engagement initiatives aligned with ESS business priorities.
  • Contribute to the annual ESS strategy review by preparing marketing performance indicators, communication plans and supporting materials.
  • Support the continuous improvement of ESS sales enablement tools and materials, helping ensure that Sales teams have up-to-date product messaging, training and communication.

Requirements

  • Further education in industrial product marketing
  • Degree in marketing, communications, business or a technical field; equivalent professional experience will also be considered.
  • Ability to understand electronic products and translate technical information into clear customer-facing content.
  • Solid experience in marketing communications, product marketing or sales enablement in an international industrial B2B environment.
  • Experience creating marketing materials for technical products and collaborating with Sales, Product Management or Engineering teams.
  • Experience coordinating projects and stakeholders across different countries or functions.
  • Experience in product marketing, marketing communications or sales enablement for technical products.
  • Good knowledge of at least one of the following industry sectors: high voltage, railway traction systems, power transmission & distribution, renewable energy and e-mobility.
  • Interest and ability to understand DC and AC power systems and corresponding product needs.
  • Excellent project management, organizational and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills.
  • Ability to translate technical information into clear marketing messages and customer benefits.
  • Proven ability to think creatively, identify and resolve problems.
  • Experienced to work under pressure and meet deadlines.
  • Proficiency in MS-Office programs.

Benefits

We foster flat hierarchies and direct communication, enabling quick decisions and strong collaboration across all levels. You’ll be trusted with real responsibility and encouraged to take initiative, with plenty of opportunities to grow both personally and professionally.

title: Senior Cryogenic Engineer
RF Engineer (GNSS)
description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As an RF Engineer (GNSS) in the Hardware (Electronics) team, you will own the radionavigation architecture of our products. Our systems need high-precision navigation and robust connectivity in contested, complex environments, and you will be the expert responsible for the RF subsystems, from antenna design to integration and compliance. You will design custom GNSS antennas and receiver modules, extend them towards CRPAs for GNSS-denied operations, and see each design through simulation, lab validation and flight tests. Based in Lausanne, Switzerland.

Responsibilities

  • Antenna Design: Design custom GNSS antennas and receiver modules for our products, and extend the work towards CRPAs (Controlled Reception Pattern Antennas) for GNSS-denied environments.

  • Antenna Integration: Integrate all antennas (GNSS, radio link) into the drones, validating through simulation (gain diagrams) and real-life lab and flight testing.

  • GNSS Test Bench: Develop, maintain and configure the GNSS test bench to simulate satellite constellations and interference scenarios.

  • RF Measurement: Run hands-on characterization with network and spectrum analyzers, and simulate new antenna iterations with EM software.

  • Electromagnetic Compatibility: Lead EMC troubleshooting and pre-compliance testing, identifying and removing blockers early.

  • PCB Collaboration: Work with PCB designers to review routing, shielding and RF layout.

  • Architecture Ownership: Review and own the RF architecture across product lines, including link budgets and system-level RF performance.

  • Mentoring: Act as the team's RF subject matter expert, coaching junior engineers on RF layout principles and EMC mitigation.

Candidate Requirements

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, RF Engineering, Telecommunications or a related field.

  • Experience: Proven track record taking complex wireless devices from concept to mass production, including clearing strict EMC compliance hurdles. Background in aerospace, commercial drones or GNSS products is a strong advantage.

  • GNSS: Solid grounding in GNSS, including hands-on use of a GNSS test bench to simulate edge-case environments, and an understanding of effects such as multipath.

  • Antenna Design: Experience designing custom antennas under tight mechanical and space constraints, with EM simulation tools.

  • RF & EMC: Strong command of RF fundamentals and measurement equipment (network and spectrum analyzers); comfortable working in an anechoic chamber.

  • Mindset: Analytical, meticulous, structured and resilient; a hands-on problem-solver who works autonomously and collaborates well.

  • Communication & Influence: Excellent written and verbal communication, capable of leading diverse principals, from junior members to senior executives.

  • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI's mission, vision, and ambitious growth plans, ready to go the extra mile to ensure operational excellence.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As a Systems Engineer in the Warhead team at Harmattan AI, you will help structure and build complete development assurance and qualification frameworks for energetic effectors. Working alongside the effectors and platform teams, you will help develop the necessary protocols, requirements management, S3 assessment frameworks and qualification programs for the energetic systems and sub-systems in the final use case. The role requires an individual with a pragmatic and rigorous approach and an understanding of NATO doctrine and qualification regimes.

Responsibilities

  • Review system architectures and advise on compliance with military doctrine, with a focus on safety and mission objectives.

  • Define clear system and sub-system requirements, and maintain a traceable verification and validation matrix.

  • Work with product leads and engineers on design choices to ensure smooth integration and pragmatic delivery.

  • Develop qualification programs and master test plans for systems and sub-systems, from specification through to final reporting.

  • Run qualification readiness reviews and flag risks to qualification early.

  • Lead engagements with defense customers and test facilities on product qualification and testing, including regular travel to test sites.

  • Document system safety and suitability for service in line with NATO and customer requirements.

  • Coach wider teams on qualification processes and the safety of munition systems.

Candidate Requirements

  • Engineering degree in Systems, Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in systems engineering roles qualifying weapon systems such as missiles, drones or other effectors.

  • Pragmatic, structured approach to stakeholder management in fast-moving programs.

  • Experience managing qualification programs end to end, including handling test failures and non-conformances.

  • Safety assessment experience on munition systems.

  • Strong understanding of NATO doctrine, and experience working with defense customers and ministries of defense.

  • Comfort working with energetic systems such as warheads, fuzes and rocket motors.

  • Strong technical writing and reporting skills.

  • Fluency in English required.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Senior Documentation Specialist
description:
About this position

As the Senior Documentation Specialist, you ensure the effective management, quality, completeness, and inspection readiness of essential clinical trial documentation for assigned studies, programmes or documentation activities, including the sponsor TMF and oversight of CRO and laboratory TMFs. You acts as an experienced TMF specialist, working closely with Clinical Operations and cross-functional study teams to provide expert guidance on document processes, compliance, risk management and continuous improvement.

Your tasks:

  • Oversee documentation handling, filing and archival activities for assigned studies, programmes or documentation activities across relevant functional areas, ensuring that final documents are complete, accurate, traceable and maintained in the company document management system.

  • Perform complex quality-control reviews and provide technical oversight of QC activities completed by TMF colleagues and external partners, in accordance with applicable SOPs, the CDISC TMF Reference Model, study-specific TMF Plans and regulatory requirements.

  • Plan and conduct risk-based periodic oversight reviews of CRO and laboratory TMFs; identify quality or completeness issues, recommend remediation actions, monitor progress and escalate significant or recurring risks.

  • Lead TMF inspection-readiness activities for assigned studies and coordinate documentation support during audits and regulatory inspections; develop and coordinate documentation-related corrective and preventive actions, monitor implementation and verify effective closure.

  • Act as a TMF subject matter expert for study teams and external partners, providing practical guidance and escalating matters that require management direction or cross-functional decisions.

  • Analyse and communicate TMF quality and performance metrics, identify trends and recommend improvements to processes, systems, templates and ways of working.

  • Ensure assigned activities comply with company and CRO SOPs, ICH GCP, applicable regulations and relevant regulatory guidance.

  • Represent Clinical Documentation in study meetings, provide input on TMF status and quality, and follow up on agreed documentation actions, decisions and risks.

  • Prepare and deliver TMF guidance and training, and share expertise with study-team members and other TMF colleagues on compliant documentation practices.

Role requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in a scientific, health-related or other relevant discipline.

  • Minimum seven years of experience in TMF and documentation management within the pharmaceutical or CRO industry, including at least three years of experience in biotechnology or another fast-growing, dynamic environment.

  • Advanced knowledge of eTMF solutions, such as Veeva Vault Clinical, PhlexTMF or comparable platforms, together with strong working knowledge of ICH GCP, applicable regulations and the CDISC TMF Reference Model.

  • Demonstrated experience in TMF quality control, risk-based TMF reviews and CRO or vendor oversight.

  • Demonstrated experience leading TMF inspection-readiness activities and managing documentation-related findings and corrective and preventive actions.

  • Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, with the ability to provide clear guidance, influence without direct authority and build effective working relationships across functions.

  • Proactive and accountable approach, with sound judgement, analytical problem-solving skills and the ability to identify and implement pragmatic, GCP-compliant solutions.

  • Excellent attention to detail, organisation and time management, with the ability to prioritise and manage multiple activities in a dynamic environment.

  • Professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

Work permit

Candidate needs to hold a Swiss work permit or be an EU citizen eligible to work in Switzerland

Your path forward

If you meet most of these requirements and bring a strong dedication to technical documentation, we encourage you to apply. You will contribute directly to our mission of advancing new medicines for patients.

title: Content Creator, Personal Brand (50–100 %)
description:
Gute Geschichten brauchen jemanden, der sie entdeckt. Und umsetzt. ✨

Wir bauen die Marke, auf die unsere Eltern gewartet haben: Fortisana, einen wissenschaftlich fundierten All-in-One-Drink rund um Muskelerhalt und ein aktives Leben. Mit dir wollen wir die Menschen und Ideen dahinter sichtbar machen.

Hinter Fortisana stehen Piran, Leon und Max:

  • Piran hat KoRo mitgegründet und über neun Jahre zu einer der erfolgreichsten Lebensmittelmarken Deutschlands aufgebaut.

  • Leon ist Ernährungsberater und in der Welt der Nahrungsergänzung aufgewachsen. Seine Familie produziert seit über 25 Jahren Nahrungsergänzungsmittel in Deutschland.

  • Max hat bereits mehr als sechs Startups begleitet und zuletzt bei 1KOMMA5° gelernt, wie aus einer Vision ein operativ exzellentes Unternehmen wird.

Du arbeitest direkt mit Leon daran, seine persönliche Marke aufzubauen. Du machst aus seinem Wissen, seinen Ideen und seinem Alltag als Gründer Inhalte, die Menschen wirklich sehen wollen. Du findest die Geschichte, fragst nach und bringst sie vom ersten Gedanken bis zum veröffentlichten Video.

Lerne Leon kennen: Auf Instagram @leonbader99 (https://www.instagram.com/leonbader99/) bekommst du einen Eindruck von seinen Themen, seinem Stil und den Inhalten, die du mit ihm weiterentwickelst.

Was du bei uns machst

  • Du entwickelst eigene Formate. Gemeinsam mit Leon findest du Themen, starke Einstiege und Geschichten rund um Ernährung, Unternehmertum und den Aufbau von Fortisana.

  • Du setzt selbst um. Du planst Drehs, filmst Interviews und direkte Ansprachen an die Kamera und hältst spontane Momente hinter den Kulissen fest.

  • Du machst aus Material gute Videos. Du schneidest Kurzvideos mit Rhythmus, sauberem Ton und Untertiteln, die das Anschauen leicht machen.

  • Du denkst bis zur Veröffentlichung. Du schreibst Begleittexte, veröffentlichst Beiträge und gehst auf Fragen und Reaktionen der Community ein.

  • Du lernst aus den Ergebnissen. Du erkennst, welche Themen, Einstiege und Formate funktionieren, und entwickelst sie weiter.

Was du mitbringst

  • Du verstehst Social Media. Du kannst Geschichten erzählen und bei Menschen eine Reaktion auslösen. Dein Portfolio zeigt dein Können in Konzeption, Dreh und Schnitt. Eigene Projekte zählen genauso.

  • Du hast ein gutes Gespür. Für Ästhetik, Sprache und Details – und dafür, wann eine Geschichte echt wirkt.

  • Du bist neugierig und fragst nach. Du kannst Menschen vor der Kamera begleiten, gute Fragen stellen und aus einer ersten Idee mehr herausholen.

  • Du packst an. Du bringst eigene Ideen ein und übernimmst Verantwortung für ihre Umsetzung.

  • Du kommunizierst sicher. Ausgezeichnete Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sind Voraussetzung. Du formulierst in beiden Sprachen sicher, präzise und zielgruppengerecht.

  • Du denkst mit. Ernährung, Sport oder Unternehmertum interessieren dich. Du recherchierst sorgfältig und vermittelst Gesundheitsthemen verständlich und ohne übertriebene Versprechen.

  • Du bist beim Dreh dabei. Für diese Stelle kannst du regelmässig vor Ort in Zürich mit Leon drehen. Drehs in Zürich oder Berlin stimmen wir gemeinsam ab.

  • Du arbeitest AI-native und mit Qualitätsanspruch. Du testest eigenständig neue KI-Tools und kreative Ansätze und integrierst sie sinnvoll in deine Workflows. Dabei prüfst du die Ergebnisse kritisch und hältst unseren Qualitätsstandard bei Inhalt, Gestaltung und Genauigkeit hoch.

Was wir dir bieten

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit Leon. Kurze Wege, ehrliches Feedback und die Chance, eine persönliche Marke von Anfang an mitzugestalten.

  • Kreativen Freiraum. Deine Ideen sind gefragt. Du kannst Formate ausprobieren und einen Stil entwickeln, der wiedererkennbar ist.

  • Einblick in echten Markenaufbau. Du erlebst den Aufbau von Fortisana und lernst von Pirans KoRo-Erfahrung und Leons Wissen aus der Nahrungsergänzungsbranche.

  • Arbeit, die deine Handschrift trägt. Du entwickelst dich in Storytelling, Produktion und Schnitt weiter und baust ein sichtbares Portfolio auf.

Zwei Wege ins Team

Du kannst mit einem sechsmonatigen Vollzeitpraktikum einsteigen, mit der Möglichkeit einer Festanstellung nach erfolgreichem Abschluss. Wenn du bereits mehr Erfahrung mitbringst, ist auch eine Teilzeit- oder freiberufliche Zusammenarbeit mit einem Umfang von mindestens 50 % möglich.

Zeig uns deine Arbeit 🤎

Ein perfektes Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Uns interessiert, wie du denkst und was du selbst auf die Strasse gebracht hast.

Schick uns drei Arbeiten, auf die du stolz bist. Sag bei jeder Arbeit konkret, was von dir stammt: Idee, Skript, Dreh, Schnitt oder Veröffentlichung – und ob sie im Job, für einen Kunden oder als eigenes Projekt entstanden ist. Wenn vorhanden, ergänze Ergebnisse und was du daraus gelernt hast. Dazu brauchen wir deinen Standort, deinen möglichen Starttermin und ein kurzes Profil oder einen Lebenslauf.

Ein eingespieltes Team in einem wachsenden Jungunternehmen, ein wunderschönes Büro mitten in Bern und die Möglichkeit, hybrid zu arbeiten.

title: Quantum Hardware Assembly Technician
description:
About Us

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in!

As our Quantum Hardware Assembly Technician at QuantWare, you are the hands that turn a quantum chip into a working, measurable product. You package our chips into their housing and onto a PCB, and you will assemble and mount the new devices into their cryo fridge in the test facility. Your precision, discipline and reliability directly keep our production and measurement pipelines moving, and ensure our quantum hardware meets the highest quality standards.

This is a hands-on execution role. You carry out chip assembly and fridge loading according to technical drawings and documented work instructions (SOPs), to a consistent quality standard and pace, and you record your work in our production systems. You report to the Production Manager, who holds formal line-management responsibility (1:1s, performance reviews, absence and leave). You take your daily and weekly priorities from the Assembly Tech Lead, who sets the assembly schedule and is the technical authority on the floor; fridge loading is planned in close coordination with the measurement team.

What you'll be doing

Core Responsibilities

  • Assemble quantum chips into their packaging, working from technical drawings and work instructions to place and mount the chip in its housing and mount the chip in its housing with the PCB.

  • Make the electrical connections, wirebonding (manual and automatic) will be a significant part of the daily activities, as well as manual soldering.

  • Measure and test your work, performing the defined electrical and mechanical checks and recording the results, so issues are caught before a device moves on.

  • Finish and close the package, including sealing, inspection, laser engraving and preparing for transportation to the measurement location.

  • Load our cryogenic fridges with new chips to be measured, mounting packaged samples and QPUs, making the wiring, thermal and mechanical connections, and closing up the system with magnetic shields.

  • Safeguard quality, handling fragile, high-value parts with care and following handling and ESD procedures, because a single scratch, particle or ESD event can ruin a chip.

Supporting Responsibilities

  • Flag deviations early, stopping and raising it with the Assembly Tech Lead when something does not match the instruction or does not look right, rather than improvising a fix.

  • Help improve how we work, giving practical feedback on work instructions, fixtures and tools while our processes are still maturing.

  • Keep a safe, clean and organised workplace, applying 5S and HSE rules every day and making sure your bench, tooling and consumables are ready.

Your Profile

  • MBO-level technical education (level 3 or 4) or equivalent, for example in mechatronics, mechanical engineering, electronics, fine-mechanical or precision engineering, or lab or instrument technology.

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience assembling mechanical, electrical or mechatronic systems; relevant internships count.

  • Able to read work instructions with photos and technical drawings, and comfortable with basic digital tools and production systems.

  • Good with your hands at two scales: precision in assembly, handling of fine devices and connectors, and mechanical assembly such as bolting, cabling and fitting larger parts together.

  • Precise and patient, with a genuine liking for detailed hands-on work done well, every time, and a practical approach to solving problems.

  • Comfortable with structured, repeatable work, and disciplined about following instructions step by step and recording what you did.

  • Comfortable in an environment that is still being built, where not every process is finished yet and priorities can shift.

  • A team player in a young, driven team who communicates openly and speaks up when something isn't right.

  • Good command of technical English.

Bonus if you also bring:

  • Experience with wirebonding, die attach or other chip-packaging / microelectronics assembly.

  • Experience with measurements, diagnostics or troubleshooting.

  • Experience in a lab, ESD-controlled or 5S production environment.

  • Experience assembling, servicing or setting up complex equipment, instruments or machines.

  • Familiarity with cryogenics or vacuum systems.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway! Research shows women often self-select out if they don't meet every requirement. Here's our take: nobody ticks every box. This is a description of our ideal candidate, not a filter. If most resonates and you're keen to learn the gaps, apply. We hire for trajectory, not perfection.

What We Offer:

At QuantWare, you’ll be part of a high-performing team of world-class experts in an ambitious, fast-moving environment. From day one, you’ll have the trust, tools, and support to do your best work. Here’s what you can expect:

Competitive salary - A salary that reflects the impact and importance of the role (and of course 8% holiday allowance)

Pension that’s built to last - A generous and future-proof pension plan that includes partner and dependent coverage.

Flexibility built on trust - We focus on outcomes. Work flexibly, in a hybrid setup, with an open vacation policy that lets you manage your time

Personal growth - We invest in your L&D, with a budget available to each team member, dependent on their individual ambitions, development needs, and performance

A connected team - We make space to celebrate wins together, with team events, offsites, and spontaneous moments that bring us closer

Diversity & Inclusion at QuantWare

We’re an ambitious company, not only for our goals but also to become an even more diverse and inclusive team. We know great candidates don't always follow a straight path, and we value diverse experience, perspectives, and ways of thinking. We know this helps us make better decisions, drives more innovation, and strengthens our culture.

title: Senior Accountant
description:
Hi, I'm Serhii, I'm the Accounting Team Lead at WeTravel, and I'm hiring the Senior Accountant to take over the work I've done for the past three years.

I joined as a Junior Accountant, took on this scope early, and grew into leading the accounting

team. That path is real here: if you own your work and keep improving how it gets done, scope

follows. You'll report to me, and I'll be your day-to-day partner, reviewer and someone to think

problems through with.

How we work

We're a small team, so your work is visible and your ideas get used. We value autonomy: you get clear ownership, not a checklist and someone looking over your shoulder.

We care about the "how" as much as the "what." We write standard operating procedures (SOPs), build reusable workpapers, script repetitive NetSuite tasks and use AI tools daily to move faster. If you've ever rebuilt a reconciliation so the next month took half the time, you'll fit in. We're remote-first. Our finance team works mostly from home, split between Amsterdam and the US, so you'll collaborate across time zones. You and I will meet at our Amsterdam office for in-person days, such as working sessions, close kick-offs and planning. How often depends on what the work needs, and we keep it flexible. The office is open every day if you'd rather work from there. You'll need to live in the Netherlands, within reach of Amsterdam.

Our values:

• Be Respectful: we build an inclusive team that values different perspectives.

• Be Honest: we default to transparency, including when something in the numbers is wrong.

• Be Resourceful: we find a way forward even when the path isn't mapped out.

• Be the Solution: spotting a problem is the start; fixing it is the job.

What you'll own

You'll own these areas end to end, from monthly entries through audit support.

• Month-end close: you'll be the main preparer of the monthly close, owning accruals, prepaids

and balance sheet reconciliations, and reviewing the income statement for accuracy, correct

periods and department mapping before it goes to final review.

• Cash: bank, card and payment-platform accounts across multiple currencies and entities,

including Stripe, Airwallex, ING and Corpay.

• Intercompany: intercompany entries and loan agreements with interest between entities.

• Leases and fixed assets: lease accounting (right-of-use assets and liabilities), leasehold

improvements, fixed assets, intangibles and depreciation.

• Compensation: bonus and commission accruals, payroll journal entries and liabilities, pension

and 401(k).

• Expenses and AP: the full expense cycle, from vendor bills and card spend to prepaid

amortization, AP tie-outs and department mapping.

• VAT: preparing BV VAT returns for review.

• Audits: owning your areas in the annual financial audit and tax reviews.

• Process: documenting and improving what you own, from standard operating procedures

(SOPs) to automation.

• Reporting: presenting your areas to the finance team in a weekly review.

We care most about how you work, then what you know. Audit firm or in-house, scale-up or

corporate: your background matters less than what you've owned.

Why You Should or Shouldn't Apply

You should apply if you have:

• A track record of owning close areas end to end without needing someone to drive them.

• 3+ years in accounting, with hands-on month-end close experience.

• Multi-entity and multi-currency experience, including intercompany.

• Solid grounding in accrual accounting; US GAAP experience, or the willingness to get there

quickly alongside Dutch GAAP.

• Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills and experience with a mid-market ERP (NetSuite ideal).

• Fluent English, written and spoken.

• A bachelor's degree in accounting or finance, or equivalent experience.

Nice-to-haves

• NetSuite and Ramp experience.

• Dutch VAT or statutory reporting exposure.

• Examples of processes you've automated or documented, with or without AI tools.

• Interest in growing your scope and responsibilities over time.

You shouldn't apply if:

• You prefer a role where every process is fully documented and never changes.

• You need regular check-ins to keep month-end tasks moving.

• You'd rather flag a problem than dig in and propose a fix.

• You're uncomfortable explaining your numbers, or saying when you got something wrong.

Benefits

  • Generous "Time to Recharge" policy — enjoy unlimited paid time off to rest, recharge, and show up as your best self.

  • Work remotely for a maximum of 4 weeks per calendar year.

  • 2-week cross-functional onboarding program.

  • Monday and Thursday lunches and after-work social events.

  • Beautiful office in central Amsterdam – rooftop garden

  • Extensive paid family leave.

  • Cutting-edge equipment and tools to set you up for success.
