title: Senior Optical Systems Engineer
description:
About Quandela:

Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges.
Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

About this position: 

You will join the QPU Prototyping team, which develops and integrates the optical systems at the heart of Quandela's quantum processors, turning advanced R&D experiments into operational hardware. 

We are looking for a Senior Optical Systems Engineer to take ownership of a major optical development work package within our next-generation QPU programme. 

Your main challenge will be to maximise optical transmission and system performance, from experimental characterisation and precision alignment to qualification and integration. You'll tackle complex optical challenges, defining the right experimental approaches and driving solutions from investigation to validation. 

You will also coordinate technical activities involving several engineers and scientists, ensuring the delivery of critical milestones. 

This is a predominantly hands-on experimental role, combining deep technical expertise with project ownership.

Requirements

What you'll do: 

Develop and optimise optical systems 

  • Design, assemble, align and operate complex optical setups. 
  • Characterise optical transmission, identify losses and improve efficiency. 
  • Define measurement methods and improve stability and reproducibility. 
  • Troubleshoot experimental challenges and implement reliable solutions. 

Qualify and integrate optical subsystems 

  • Optimise research-developed optical subsystems for QPU integration. 
  • Define experimental tests, performance targets and qualification procedures. 
  • Collaborate with optics, electronics and system integration teams. 

Drive technical delivery 

  • Own technical deliverables within a major optical development project. 
  • Coordinate experimental activities across engineers and scientists. 
  • Plan tasks, milestones, equipment and laboratory resources. 
  • Anticipate technical risks, resolve blockers and guide contributors. 

The role combines approximately 80% hands-on experimental work and 20% technical coordination, with no initial requirement for formal people management. 
-

How you'll grow: 

First 3 months: Become familiar with Quandela's optical systems, experimental infrastructure and qualification objectives. 

Within 6 months: Take ownership of optical characterisation and optimisation activities, coordinating experimental work and technical milestones. 

Within 12 months: Lead the technical delivery of complex optical developments, with increasing autonomy over planning and resources. 

Longer term: Potential progression towards technical team leadership as the team grows. 

-

Requirements 

What we're looking for: 

We are looking for an experienced optical engineer or experimental scientist with strong hands-on expertise and the ability to drive complex technical projects. 

Relevant backgrounds include fibered optical systems, laser systems, experimental optics, and optical metrology. Academic and industrial experience are equally welcome. 

Must-have: 

  • PhD in Optics, Photonics, Physics or related fields. 
  • >5 years of experimental experience, including postdoctoral research. 
  • Hands-on expertise in complex optical systems, alignment and troubleshooting. 
  • Strong knowledge of linear optics, optical transmission and precision metrology. 
  • Proven ability to optimise optical performance and solve experimental challenges. 
  • Experience organising technical work and delivering project milestones. 
  • Experimental rigour, teamwork and professional English. French is not required. 

Important, but you can grow here: 

Technical & system integration 

  • Optical subsystem qualification and hardware integration. 
  • Python for experimental automation and data analysis. 
  • Semiconductor optics and quantum optical systems. 

Project & operational ownership 

  • Experimental planning, equipment and resource management. 
  • Coordination of multidisciplinary technical activities. 

Bonus: 

  • Experience transferring R&D setups into operational systems. 
  • Industrial qualification and reliability standards. 
  • Experience mentoring engineers or researchers. 
  • Exposure to quantum computing or advanced photonic hardware. 

Quantum computing experience is not required. What matters is your ability to understand complex optical systems, solve experimental challenges and deliver results. 

Benefits

Benefits 

Join a multidisciplinary team developing the optical systems for next-generation quantum processors, with substantial experimental ownership and opportunities for technical progression. 

  • Competitive compensation aligned with experience. 
  • Company savings plan and profit-sharing. 
  • 100% health coverage through Alan. 
  • Transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus. 
  • Swile meal vouchers. 
  • Gymlib and childcare support. 
  • Referral programme. 

Process 

  • Talent Acquisition interview (30–45 min) 
  • Hiring Manager interview (45–60 min) 
  • Technical discussion on previous experimental work 
  • Technical case study or presentation with the team 
  • Reference checks 
  • Team meeting 
  • Offer 

Beyond that: 

At Quandela, we value diverse scientific and engineering backgrounds, practical curiosity and the ability to learn from different fields. 

Whether your experience comes from an academic laboratory, industrial R&D or a different area of experimental optics, we'd love to hear from you if you enjoy tackling demanding technical challenges and turning experimental work into reliable results.

EggAI is the transformation partner on a core banking system replacement for a client to lay the foundations of operating Agentic Generative AI in production.

EggAI's role is to specify, set the standard and programme-manage. You will define what operational readiness means and prove it at each gate, working with the client's own teams and its managed service providers, as well as EggAI's platform engineers.

The platform is a mix of classical banking infrastructure and agentic AI workloads, so the reliability problem runs across both deterministic and probabilistic systems.

The Role

Own the definition of operational readiness for go-live: what "ready to run in production" means, how the bank proves it at each regulatory gate, and what has to change in the organisation for that proof to hold.

The bank's operations teams, processes and provider contracts were built to run classical banking infrastructure. Agentic AI workloads need a different operating model, and you will shape it: redraw responsibilities between the client's teams and its managed service providers, set the standards each party works to, and lead the people through the change — so that those who run the platform today are ready and willing to run what comes next.

This is a lead/principal position reporting to the Programme Plan and Execution Lead. It is remote, with regular London presence required for gate weeks and workshops.

Responsibilities

  • Reliability targets — set the SLO and error-budget framework alongside the client's existing structure, have the service owners adopt it, and commission the behavioural quality measures that do the same job for agentic workloads

  • Observability and detection — define what Tier-1 services and agentic workloads must emit, including trajectory logging; require an automated path from a firing alert to the affected services and their owners; and hold the operating teams to closing the logging gaps in what runs today

  • The incident and change path — set the runbook standard and its required coverage, extend incident classification and intervention mechanisms to agentic failure modes, and have rollback and change-failure rates measured and reported by those who own them

  • Capacity and performance — direct the headroom position through the parallel-run peak at cutover, sponsor the chaos and game-day programme for payment rails and the core ledger, and mandate that capacity modelling covers inference workloads

  • Gate evidence — own the technical content of the Operational Acceptance Report and Operational Readiness Certificate, the reliability section of each gate pack, and the reliability NFRs defended as ADRs through the client's Architecture Design Authority — written by the teams, reviewed and signed off by you

  • The operating organisation — decide how responsibilities sit between the client's teams and its managed service providers for the new platform, and lead the people concerned through that change

Expected experience

  • 10+ years in leading IT operations teams — You have operated L1, L2, and L3 support as SRE, platform reliability or infrastructure organisations, with the people and the providers reporting to you

  • Aligns operations with development, engineering and the business — has set operating goals that engineering teams and business stakeholders signed up to, and kept them focused on those goals through delivery

  • Has introduced SLOs and error budgets into an organisation that did not have them, and can build on the experienced success factors

  • Infrastructure in depth — has deep infrastructure knowledge, and what is required for smooth business operations: telemetry, redundancies, backups, etc.

  • Incident management, with post-incident reviews that led to real changes in the system and in the organisation

  • Regulated financial services, or another environment where an external body audits operational evidence.

  • Has worked through a managed service provider and can set standards they do not personally execute

  • Comfortable operating in a complex, multi-stakeholder programme where scope and ownership are still being established across parallel workstreams

Valuable, not required

  • LLM or agentic system operations: eval harnesses, drift detection, trajectory analysis, prompt and model versioning treated as change types

  • Core banking or payments exposure, particularly scheme gateway integration

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a platform architect. A separate role owns agentic platform design and build

  • Not an on-call engineer. You will not carry a client pager; out-of-hours operations are run by a third party

  • Not a service delivery manager. This is engineering judgement applied to readiness, not ITSM process administration

title: Systems & IT Engineer (w/m/d) 100%
description:
Please note that for this position, we'll only consider applications from people who are already living in Switzerland.

About Papers

Papers is a software engineering company founded on high-tech talent. We support the full lifecycle of innovative web3 products — from concept to software market fit — building secure, scalable futures for our clients and the internet at large.

With over a decade of experience and a reputation built on delivering for Fortune 500s and blockchain ecosystems, our teams combine deep technical know-how with a mission to enable meaningful, decentralized innovation.

As an engineering-driven team, we work with autonomy and purpose. Our culture is built on meritocracy, long-term thinking, and a commitment to quality over buzz. We aim to collaborate with people who love tech for its own sake and want to help shape the future by solving real-world challenges.

Tasks

Your Responsibilities

  • Manage and improve our self-hosted, Linux-based infrastructure (Ubuntu) running on a fleet of dedicated/bare-metal servers
  • Keep servers patched and up to date (OS/security updates, reboots) and maintain the various applications we self-host
  • Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI): build images, push to the GitLab Container Registry
  • Set up and optimize Docker and Docker Compose deployments
  • Automate infrastructure and host provisioning with Ansible
  • Define and enforce backup strategies and disaster-recovery processes.
  • Run our observability stack — Telegraf + InfluxDB + Grafana for metrics and alerting (alerts route to Teams/PagerDuty), Graylog for log aggregation — and write runbooks for the alerts
  • Administer Microsoft 365 / Entra ID (Azure AD) — identity & access management, MFA, Conditional Access, SSO, and email/collaboration security
  • Own and continuously improve our security posture: SSH/host hardening, firewalls, secrets management, least-privilege access, periodic access reviews, and incident response
  • Participate in on-call rotations to support critical services (incl. the Acurast blockchain/bridge infrastructure)
  • Collaborate with backend engineers to streamline integration and delivery
  • Continuously identify and automate repetitive tasks to reduce manual intervention

Tech Stack Overview

You'll be working with:

  • Linux (Ubuntu), bare-metal/dedicated hosts
  • GitLab CI, Docker, Docker Compose
  • Ansible (infrastructure-as-code)
  • Nginx, Let's Encrypt/certbot
  • Telegraf, InfluxDB, Grafana (metrics + alerting); Graylog (logs), PagerDuty
  • PostgreSQL, NATS, NetBird (mesh VPN)
  • Microsoft 365 / Entra ID (Azure AD) — identity, MFA, Conditional Access
  • Scripting: Bash, Python

Requirements

Your Profile

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in DevOps, SRE, or infrastructure roles
  • Proficient with Linux/Ubuntu system administration on self-managed servers
  • Comfortable with Docker / Docker Compose and CI/CD workflows (GitLab CI)
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Ansible especially)
  • Confident with Nginx, TLS, shell scripting, and practical networking (reverse proxies, firewalls, VPN/overlay networks)
  • Comfortable owning a metrics/alerting stack and responding to incidents
  • Solid grasp of security fundamentals: identity & access management (MFA/SSO, least privilege), host hardening, secrets handling, and patch management
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • Self-driven, self-organized, pragmatic, and comfortable working independently

Benefits

Bonus if you have:

  • Background in blockchain/web3 infrastructure (we run Acurast network and bridge services)
  • Microsoft 365 / Entra ID administration (Conditional Access, Intune, Defender)
  • Deeper security background: hardening, vulnerability/patch management, or a security certification
  • Experience operating a TIG stack (Telegraf/InfluxDB/Grafana) or other time-series monitoring
  • Managed-cloud experience (GCP/AWS/Azure) and Kubernetes/Helm
  • Terraform or other declarative IaC (transferable to our Ansible setup)
  • Contributions to open-source projects
  • Experience scaling infrastructure in startup or high-growth environments

Why join Papers?

  • 🧠 Work with cutting-edge web3 clients and technology.
  • 🏖️ 25 days paid vacation per year.
  • 💻 2 days of home office per week possible
  • 🤝 High ownership, low bureaucracy — your voice matters.
  • 🛠️ Influence the DevOps strategy from day one.
  • 🎉 Regular team events and retreats when possible.
  • 📚 Learning and development supported.

title: Computer Vision and Machine Learning Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Computer Vision and Machine Learning (CV/ML) Engineer to develop and deploy intelligent perception systems for our autonomous drone-in-a-box platform. You will work on challenging real-world computer vision problems, from real-time object detection and tracking on embedded devices to advanced scene understanding and cloud-based inference. As part of a small, technical team, you will own solutions across our software stack, taking algorithms and models from prototype to deployment. This position is for an on-site employee for our Zurich office.

Responsibilities

  • Design and develop a wide variety of computer vision and machine learning features for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications
  • Train, fine-tune and evaluate deep learning models for tasks such as object detection, instance segmentation, image retrieval/reidentification
  • Optimize algorithms and models for edge devices (NVIDIA Jetson and Qualcomm Dragonwing), and integrate them into our image and video processing pipelines
  • Monitor ML model performance in real-world deployments and set up workflows for continuous improvement (data collection, curation, labeling, retraining, evaluation)
  • Evaluate and integrate large/vision language models for scene understanding, situational awareness, and hazard analysis, including prompt design, performance benchmarking, and production deployment

Qualifications

  • Degree in Computer Science, Robotics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
  • Solid understanding of computer vision and machine learning fundamentals
  • Strong programming skills in Python and C++, with experience developing production-grade software that powers CV/ML systems
  • Experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow, ONNX, TensorRT, CUDA
  • Experience with end-to-end model development: from dataset curation, labeling strategies, active learning workflows to deployment and optimization for edge devices
  • Excellent oral and written skills in English
  • Work permit in Switzerland required

Bonus Points

  • Good understanding of 3D vision and robotics perception, along with hands-on experience with OpenCV and ROS/ROS2, is a strong plus
  • Experience with NVIDIA Jetson and Qualcomm edge devices, and their CV/ML SDKs
  • Experience with transformers, large/vision language models and prompt design for perception tasks
  • Experience with complex GStreamer pipelines and custom plugin development

description:

Join us, and together, we can power clean transportation!

Rocsys relies on your contribution to accelerating the adoption of electric mobility by building the software behind our autonomous charging technology. Our work enables reliable, scalable charging solutions that support cleaner transportation and a more sustainable energy ecosystem. 

You will be part of our small, dedicated cloud team, giving you real ownership and visibility over work vital to the success of our company. Together with your teammates, you shape the cloud platform and connectivity layer, while collaborating closely with a group of around ten developers across various domains and our operational teams. 

This is not just dashboard development: Your code runs both in the cloud and inside real-world robotic systems operating in the field supporting clean technology that makes a tangible difference. 

In this role you will

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Data Engineer

Shiftbase is building the self-driving assistant for shift-based businesses across Europe. Our customers range from independent restaurants in Amsterdam to multi-location retailers in München, and they spend hours every week on scheduling, time tracking, payroll prep, and HR admin. We want to take that work off their plate and eventually do it for them.

Underneath that product vision sits a data challenge. Insight, automation, and AI all depend on data people can trust, and the foundation for it doesn't exist yet.

You will build the foundation that fixes this.

What you'll do

  • Architect the warehouse. Design and own our BigQuery and Dataform warehouse from the ground up. Build a layered, well-modeled foundation, medallion staging through marts, not only the models that sit on top. Ask every day whether the whole company can trust and reuse it.

  • Make the data flow reliably. Build ELT and ETL with incremental, idempotent loads, orchestration, and retries, so pipelines run on time without anyone watching them. Ship monitored pipelines that hold up in production.

  • Take the transform layer. Own the Dataform model-building and transform layer, taking full responsibility for the transformation layer and freeing up capacity for semantic modeling and business definitions. This unblocks the whole team.

  • Build trust into the data. Make validation, freshness monitoring, alerting, and lineage the default. Diagnose failures at the root cause. leadscorev2 is the outcome this role exists to prevent.

  • Serve the whole company. Feed clean, governed datasets to Metabase, HubSpot, and the ML and AI work the product ML team owns. Push modeled data back into the tools business teams act on, including HubSpot and Customer.io.

  • Own the Platform handshake. Run the day-to-day collaboration with the Platform team on our GCP foundation, a bridge that only gets part-time attention today.

  • Treat the warehouse like a product. Keep documentation, lineage, and discoverability current so departments trust the data assets, and handle sensitive HR and workforce data to GDPR standards.

What success looks like in your first 3–6 months

  • The warehouse has a real foundation. The first vertical slice, our accounts model, ships with tests and monitoring.

  • You fully own the Dataform transform layer, creating capacity for semantic modeling and business-definition work

  • Pipelines run against a defined freshness SLA, and you catch breaks before stakeholders do.

  • Documentation and lineage cover what you own, and datasets that were stuck now flow to the teams that need them.


What we're looking for

You have built warehouse foundations yourself. You designed them rather than maintaining someone else's, with a track record in:

  • Designing layered warehouse architectures (medallion, bronze-silver-gold) and dimensional models (star and snowflake) that teams reuse

  • Advanced SQL as your daily working language

  • Hands-on BigQuery, since our stack is GCP

  • Building a SQL transform layer in Dataform, or strong dbt experience.

  • ELT and ETL with incremental, idempotent loads and real orchestration, scheduling, and dependency management

  • Data quality, testing, freshness monitoring, and lineage built in from the start

  • Python for pipeline code, scripting, automation, and API integration

  • Reviewable, repeatable change through Git and PR-based deployment

Nice to have, not required: another modern cloud warehouse such as Snowflake or Redshift; managed ingestion such as Airbyte; preparing data for ML, LLM, and agentic use cases; and familiarity with B2B SaaS metrics and HR or workforce data. English is our working language, and Dutch is not required.

This role isn't infrastructure engineering, ML or MLOps, or dashboard analysis. The Platform team owns infrastructure, the Product ML team owns ML, and the business teams own dashboards. It also isn't for someone who has only maintained a warehouse another person designed. You build the foundation properly, stay transparent about data quality and trade-offs, and treat the warehouse as a product for the whole company. You'll report to the Head of Operations and partner closely with the Platform team on the company's data architecture.

title: Frontend Engineer
description:
About Shiftbase

We build workforce software that helps people get work done. More than 10,000 companies use our platform every month to plan shifts and track time, with less admin in the way.

We work from our Zoetermeer office with over 80 people and we grow every year. The culture is open and informal. You can push back on an idea regardless of title, and we change how we work when someone makes the case in retro.

About the role

You build frontend features that customers use the day you release them. You sit in a product team with backend, QA, design and product, and you take a feature from a rough product idea to a screen a planner can use without a manual.

Your time is a balance between working on features, bugs and resolving technical debt.

Claude Code is how our engineers write software. Everyone here uses it daily, and whole features now go out with an agent doing most of the coding. You still own what you merge, so you read the diff, you know why it works, and you can defend it in review. The interesting part of the job is deciding what to hand to an agent, what to write yourself, and what context the agent needs to get it right the first time.

You ask what a planner is trying to do before you read what the ticket says. You automate the parts of your own process that don't need a human.

Year one, in order

First, ship. Deliver features in scheduling and time tracking. Start small, then take one full feature from the product conversation through to release.

Then, own an area. Pick up a product surface end to end and become the person the team asks about it, including what it should do next. That covers how AI fits your area, which patterns you document for the agent and which calls you keep for yourself.

Along the way, make what you build safe to change. Restructure and test the paths you build on while you build on them. Extend test coverage where it's lacking. We move fast and keep quality up by automating what a human doesn't need to do, including the checks that catch what an agent got wrong.

What you'll do

  • Design and build frontend features starting from rough product ideas

  • Deliver features with Claude Code, from the prompt through to the pull request, and review the output as closely as a colleague's

  • Write the patterns, conventions and project context our agents work from, so generated frontend code lands in the right shape

  • Turn tangled domain rules into screens people can use without a manual

  • Fix bugs in your own features and in code you've never seen

  • Improve the code you touch while you touch it, so the next feature in that area costs less

  • Write and maintain automated tests in Jest and Playwright

  • Ship in short cycles with your product team

  • Pair, review, and teach what you know

How we work

Frontend in Angular, backend in PHP, a web app and a mobile app in React Native. Tests in Jest and Playwright. We develop AI-assisted with Claude Code as the primary tool, and a growing share of our code starts there. Human review and engineers owning what they ship keep it safe. We ship in short cycles in product teams with mixed specialisations. We pair often, with each other and with an agent open. Every quarter you get time to build and ship one of your own ideas, and we run hackathons.




Must-haves

3+ years of professional experience with an SPA framework, Angular preferred. Depth in React or Vue works if you can show you'll carry it over.

You ship. You've delivered features to real users at a steady pace, and you can tell us what you cut to get them out.

You've shipped production code with an AI agent. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar. Tell us where you let it run, where you took the keyboard back, and what you changed about your own workflow after a month of it.

You automate your tests. Jest and Playwright, or equivalents, and you have an opinion about what deserves a test.

You simplify. Hand you a tangled domain problem and you produce a screen that hides the tangle.

You explain your choices. In review, in a design discussion, and to a product manager who doesn't read code.

You work as a peer. You pair, you review, and you make the people around you better without needing a title to be heard.

Nice-to-haves

  • Claude Code in particular, or agent setups you've tuned for a team rather than yourself

  • TypeScript at depth

  • Storybook or component library ownership

  • React

  • TDD

  • PHP, or enough backend to reason about the API you're consuming

  • Familiarity with a complex, regulated domain (ours covers scheduling, time tracking, leave, and labour law across countries)

This might be your dream job if…

✅ You want your work in front of customers within days

✅ You'd rather own a feature end to end than take a finished spec

✅ You want a say in how a team writes frontend code with agents while the answer is still open

✅ You improve the code you touch without being asked, and you stop before it turns into a six-week rewrite

✅ You like a domain that takes months to learn

This probably isn't your dream job if…

⛔️ You want the technical approach decided before the ticket reaches you

⛔️ You want a job where AI stays out of your editor

⛔️ You'd merge agent output you can't explain in review

⛔️ You'd stop shipping to finish a refactor

⛔️ You prefer pixel work and would rather leave tests and architecture to someone else

⛔️ You'd rather work alone than pair and review

What we offer

  • A laptop on Mac, Windows, or Linux

  • 32 or 40 hours workweek

  • Hybrid, from home or the Zoetermeer office

  • 25 vacation days based on a 40-hour contract

  • Pension plan

  • NS business card or travel expenses reimbursed.

  • Training budget for personal development

Please be aware that this is not a remote position and we are not taking applications in consideration outside of the Netherlands for this position.

title: Account Executive - NL Region
description:
Dit is Shiftbase

Meer dan 10.000 bedrijven. Ruim 250.000 gebruikers. Eén missie: personeelsplanning en tijdregistratie simpel maken. Ons platform is gebouwd om makkelijk, flexibel en schaalbaar te zijn, of je klant nu 15 of 2500 medewerkers heeft.

Vanuit ons hoofdkantoor in Zoetermeer en onze hub in Amsterdam werken 85+ collega's aan een product waar bedrijven blij van worden. De sfeer? Open, informeel en hands-on. Hier geen eindeloze vergadercycli. Wel korte lijnen, snelle beslissingen en ruimte om jezelf te zijn.


Wat ga je doen?

Als Account Executive voor de Nederlandse markt ben jij de persoon die kansen omzet in betalende klanten.

Je bedient de B2B-markt over de volle breedte: van horeca tot retail, van zorg tot transport. Bedrijven die vaak nog met Excel of een verouderd systeem werken en waarbij jij in één demo laat zien hoeveel tijd ze terugkrijgen. De use case is herkenbaar, de waarde is snel duidelijk en dat maakt je verkoopcycli lekker kort.

Het grootste deel van je pipeline is warm. Onze marketing levert continu leads aan van bedrijven die actief op zoek zijn, en dat gaat hard. Maar we willen niet afhankelijk zijn van alleen wat er binnenkomt. Je krijgt de ruimte, en de verwachting, om zelf ook kansen te creëren in accounts die je interessant vindt. Hoe we dat als team het beste aanpakken, bepalen we samen. Jouw ervaring in de praktijk weegt daarin mee.

Het volledige sales process is van jou, van discovery en demo tot onderhandeling en close. Na de close draag je het account over aan ons Customer Success-team. Jij focust volledig op new business. Je werkt met tempo en volume, en je weet wanneer een deal aandacht verdient en wanneer je hem moet laten gaan.

Je dag bestaat voor een groot deel uit bellen en demo's, want dit is een hands-on salesrol. Sporadisch ga je op pad naar een klant voor een persoonlijk gesprek.

Je bouwt mee aan een groeiend salesteam binnen een snelgroeiende organisatie, en dat vraagt energie, initiatief en doorzettingsvermogen. Je deelt wat voor jou werkt met het team, want we worden hier beter van elkaar.


Wie ben jij?

Een salesprofessional met een paar jaar ervaring die energie krijgt van tempo, van veel gesprekken en van scoren. Je hebt bewezen dat je kunt presteren in een snelle SaaS-salesomgeving en je wilt nu een volgende stap zetten in een team dat hard aan het opbouwen is. Je wacht niet tot de telefoon gaat: als je een account in gedachten hebt, vind je zelf een weg naar binnen.

Verder herkennen we je aan het volgende: je hebt minimaal 2 jaar ervaring in high-velocity software sales (SaaS), je bent commercieel scherp zonder je klant uit het oog te verliezen, je bent leergierig en staat open voor coaching, en je beheerst Nederlands uitstekend. Engels is een pre.

Profielen die ons aanspreken: je komt uit de SaaS-wereld en hebt ervaring met snelle funnels en hoge volumes. Denk aan omgevingen zoals Lightspeed, Zenchef of vergelijkbare SME-gerichte hospitality- of retailtech.

Of je hebt een leidinggevende achtergrond in de horeca, bent tech-savvy en hebt slimme techoplossingen geïmplementeerd in die rol, en je wilt nu de overstap maken naar software sales aan onder andere de horeca. In beide gevallen: je snapt de wereld van onze klanten als geen ander.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Een rol waarin je een SaaS-oplossing verkoopt die bedrijven écht vooruit helpt, in een omgeving waar resultaat en plezier hand in hand gaan.

Groei is hier geen loze belofte. We investeren serieus in je ontwikkeling vanaf dag één. Je start met een gedegen 30-60-90-dagen-onboardingprogramma met duidelijke milestones, zodat je precies weet waar je staat en waar je naartoe werkt. Je wordt daarnaast getraind en gecertificeerd via Winning by Design, hét toonaangevende salestrainingsprogramma voor SaaS, inclusief SPICED-certificering. Daarbovenop krijg je een persoonlijk ontwikkelbudget van €1.000 per jaar om te investeren in wat jou verder brengt: cursussen, conferenties, boeken of coaching. Jij kiest.

Verder bieden we een brutojaarsalaris van €55.000 tot €75.000 inclusief vakantiegeld op basis van 40 uur per week, afhankelijk van je ervaring. Daarnaast 25 vakantiedagen, een flexibele regeling voor thuis en op kantoor werken, een goede pensioenregeling en reiskostenvergoeding (NS Business Card of kilometervergoeding).

De werksfeer? Ontspannen, met gratis lunch, bootcamp op donderdag, vrijdagmiddagborrels en kwartaal-BBQ's.

Hoe werken we samen?

De eerste 3 maanden verwachten we een hogere aanwezigheid op kantoor in Zoetermeer. Logisch: je wilt het team, het product en de klant snel doorgronden, en dat gaat nu eenmaal sneller als je er bent. Na je onboarding werken we meer hybride.

Woon je op maximaal anderhalf uur reisafstand? Dan verwachten we je minimaal één keer per week op kantoor, op dinsdag of donderdag. In de praktijk gaan we hier flexibel mee om zodra het vertrouwen er is. Woon je dichterbij of heb je geen probleem met wat meer reistijd? Elke dag op kantoor is natuurlijk ook gewoon mogelijk. Daarnaast is er de hub in Amsterdam waar je terecht kunt.

Waarom Shiftbase?

Je verkoopt geen vaag platform dat niemand begrijpt. Shiftbase is marktleider in Nederland en groeit hard in Duitsland. Een product dat 10.000+ bedrijven dagelijks gebruiken omdat het hun werk simpelweg makkelijker maakt. We connect over 500’000 callers in 190 countries: that represents 36,000 calling corridors and over 100 million calling minutes. We work with various global suppliers optimising for call quality. It’s complex. Each calling corridor has its own quality quirks and legal and regulatory rules to work within. We want someone to own call quality and routing holistically across all of it: routing daily to optimize what's happening right now, while watching the data for the long-term trends that tell us where to fix things next.

A failed call is not a metric to us. It's someone not hearing their mother's voice or its an important business call that fails. We also have real ambitions to scale calling well beyond where we are today, so this complexity isn't going anywhere. It's only going to grow.

Talk360 has been profitable since 2025, expanding beyond our core calling app into embedded, B2B2C calling for partners. We are lean, around 30 people globally, spread across the Netherlands, South Africa, Nigeria, Suriname, Turkey, Egypt, Kenya, Ukraine, and beyond. That means this role has real scope from day one: no layers between you and the decisions that matter, and no shortage of things worth tackling.

This is a remote opportunity.

What You'll Do

  • Own call quality holistically: hold the full picture of call quality end to end, working with the team on both the daily grind and the long-term view, moving fluidly between quick fixes and structured experiments.

  • Manage zones, codes, and origins: own and continuously refine our zone, dialing code, and call origin management, keeping the underlying structure clean and accurate across all 900 zones.

  • Update routing continuously: change routing several times a day, from immediate fixes to longer-running tests of new suppliers.

  • Work cross-functionally by design: partner daily with Ozcan, who owns supplier account management and deal creation, and Mahmoud, who runs hourly monitoring and support-team escalations to suppliers. Work with Ewan on automating the processes behind routing, and with Product and CRM to improve the experience for our end users.

  • Move routing toward automation: work toward (semi) automated routing and pricing, reducing how much of this still runs on manual, single-person work.


What You'll Bring

  • Hands-on experience with international A-Z calling and telco routing: zones, codes, LCR, and SIP response codes, built at a telco, carrier, or comms platform with real cross-border calling experience.

  • NOC or technical support background: comfortable troubleshooting live voice traffic and reading call detail records and quality metrics like ASR and ACD.

  • Exposure to a routing/testing platform such as iTest or an equivalent tool. Familiarity with Digitalk Cloud Carrier (DCC), our current routing platform, is a plus.

  • Nice to have: working technical literacy in SIP signalling and SBC concepts

Who You Are

  • Process driven and meticulous: you build the audit trail as you go, not after something goes wrong. You are methodical and analytical by nature, and you would rather have a clean, repeatable process than a clever one-off fix.

title: Lead Analytics Engineer
description:
Do you love turning messy business questions into data people can trust? Can you connect the customer journey from the first marketing touch through sales conversion, revenue, retention, and product usage and explain the numbers equally clearly to an engineer, a CMO, and a CFO? AIHR is looking for a Lead Agentic Analytics Engineer to become the hands-on functional lead of our two-person Data & Analytics team. You will own the translation of cross-functional business questions into trusted metrics, governed semantic models, and decision-ready agentic analytics; set the analytical direction; and build the most critical models yourself. You are transforming raw data into governed products that drive decision-making for our business partners.

 

About AIHR

Founded in 2016 with the mission to future-proof HR, the Academy to Innovate HR (AIHR) has become the global market leader in online training for HR professionals. We support customers in more than 140 countries, including organizations such as Unilever, Reckitt, Goldman Sachs, Philips, Deloitte, Nike, Heineken, and UBS. Our goal is to continuously upskill and empower one million HR professionals.

Today, we are an international team of more than 100 people representing over 30 nationalities. We are driven by excellence, innovation, and a hunger to grow, while staying friendly, enthusiastic, and committed to helping each other succeed.

Working at AIHR means taking real responsibility, improving how we operate, and getting the freedom to develop in new areas and shape your role as the company grows.


Role and Responsibilities

AIHR's Data & Analytics team is part of Business Operations. You will work alongside Vahid, our Senior Data Engineer, and report to Leo, our VP of Business Operations. Our ingestion and warehouse foundation is largely established: data from systems such as HubSpot and our own LMS moves through ETL pipelines into Snowflake. Through special Projects, we are building governed semantic layers on top so the business can self-serve trusted analytics through Power BI, Metabase, and AI tools.

Your role owns the step that matters most: translating a business question into a clear definition, a well-designed model, and conversational/agentic analytics that your leadership trusts. You will set the analytical architecture, dbt standards, and roadmap, while Vahid focuses on ingestion, warehouse reliability, and engineering implementation. You will both build: you will personally deliver the most critical business models, review implementations, and ensure the outputs are usable by the business.

This role has no direct reports. Your colleague, Vahid, remains managed by the VP of Business Operations, while you have clear functional decision rights over metric definitions, semantic-model design, analytical quality, dbt standards, and technical priorities. It is designed for someone who wants to lead through expertise while remaining close to the work.

 

What You'll Own

  • Own and execute a rolling one-year Data & Analytics roadmap, balancing urgent business needs with foundational work. Guide Vahid through clear priorities, design reviews, code review, and reusable modeling patterns.

  • Lead discovery across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Finance to uncover the decision behind a request and translate it into agreed metric definitions, governed semantic layers, and data models that connect the full customer lifecycle.

  • Set the analytical architecture and dbt standards; design, build, test, and document the most critical governed models yourself using SQL and dbt.

  • Own the full-funnel measurement framework—from marketing reach, demand generation, attribution, and customer acquisition cost through lead and pipeline conversion, sales cycle, bookings, and revenue to onboarding, product adoption, expansion, renewal, churn, and customer lifetime value. Keep core recurring-revenue definitions finance-grade and reconciled while showing how upstream activity drives downstream customer outcomes.

  • Own the logic and quality behind executive dashboards and self-service analytics across Power BI, Metabase, and AI-enabled interfaces. Present the results to senior leaders, explain every assumption, and respond constructively to challenge.

  • Partner closely with Vahid on warehouse and pipeline requirements, resolve conflicting numbers at the source, and raise the technical quality of the team. Apply AI where it improves development speed or data access, while using sound judgment around privacy, governance, validation, and trust.

A Typical Week

This is a hands-on lead role. The exact balance will shift with business priorities, but you should expect roughly half your time to remain close to the data—building, reviewing, and investigating—and the rest to be split across discovery, functional leadership, and decision support.

  • Design or improve a dbt model that connects data across HubSpot, our LMS, billing, or other source systems; write the SQL, tests, documentation, and metric logic needed to put it into production.

  • Run discovery sessions with leaders in Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Product, or Finance to clarify the decision they need to make, challenge the requested metric, and agree on the definition.

  • Work side by side with Vahid on source-data requirements, architecture choices, and implementation; review code and unblock delivery without handing off all of the technical work.

  • Investigate a commercial or customer-lifecycle question, improve an executive or functional dashboard, and present the conclusion—including assumptions and limitations—to the relevant leadership team.

  • Reprioritize the Data & Analytics roadmap, resolve competing requests, and invest in the semantic layer, governance, and reusable modeling foundations that reduce future ad hoc work.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first three months, you have established a clear operating model with Vahid, mapped ownership of the most important metrics, agreed the Data & Analytics roadmap, and resolved at least one material conflicting-number problem.

Within six months, AIHR has a governed customer-lifecycle domain in dbt and an executive view connecting acquisition and pipeline to revenue, retention, and product usage, and has launched the first MVP of our agentic analytics platform to drive self-serve adoption. The underlying definitions are documented, reconciled where relevant, and trusted across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Finance.

Within twelve months, two or three priority business domains are governed end to end, leadership can trace performance from acquisition through lifetime value using consistent numbers, self-service adoption is growing, and Vahid can independently implement the modeling patterns and quality standards you established.

Throughout, you remain hands-on in SQL, dbt, Snowflake, and analytics while setting direction, coaching through the work, and earning leadership's trust in both the numbers and the roadmap.

We offer

  • A high-impact role as the functional lead of a small Data & Analytics team, with end-to-end ownership of the semantic layer behind company-wide decisions.

  • Competitive, benchmarked compensation.

  • Substantial autonomy to shape your day-to-day work, with regular growth conversations and support for your career goals.

  • Flexible working hours and work-from-home arrangements after onboarding.

  • 26 paid holidays per year, plus one extra day for each of your first five years at AIHR.

  • The option to exchange any two public holidays for two days of your choice.

  • A work-from-anywhere policy that lets you work abroad for up to 20 days per calendar year.

  • A pension plan, four Trust Days for ad hoc recovery, and access to the OpenUp mental health platform.

  • A personal development budget, training opportunities, and the books you need to keep learning.

  • All public-transport expenses covered through an NS Business Card, plus a MacBook and the equipment you need.

  • A beautiful office opposite Rotterdam Central Station, a satellite office in Amsterdam, daily chef-prepared lunch, regular drinks, team activities, and free access to the office gym.

Get a taste of working at AIHR in our AIHR Benefits Guide.

Apply for the Job

Are you excited to become our Lead Analytics Engineer? We would love to hear from you. We are aiming for a start date in December 2026 or January 2027.

P.S. If this role excites you but you do not meet every point, we still encourage you to apply. We care about the evidence behind your experience and your potential to grow—not a perfect checklist.


Who you are

title: Senior Sales Operations (SalesOps) Manager
description:
Do you like making it easier for a Sales team to do its best work? Do you enjoy owning the details that keep deals moving, while also spotting where the process could work better? And do you get satisfaction from turning repetitive work into a simpler, smarter way of working?

AIHR is looking for a Senior Sales Operations Manager to join our Revenue Operations team. You’ll help support more than €10 million in annual deal value, working closely with Sales leadership while owning the operational processes that move deals from opportunity to collected revenue.

 

About AIHR

Founded in 2016 with the mission to future-proof HR, the Academy to Innovate HR (AIHR) has become the world’s market leader in online training for human resources (HR) professionals. We are an international team of 90+ people, driven by excellence, innovation, and a hunger to grow in everything we do. As such, we strive to provide the world’s best courses and excellent support to our customers while continuously optimizing every aspect of our work. With over 30 nationalities, our team is diverse, yet we all share a few traits: we're friendly, enthusiastic, and great team players.

Being a fast-growing company, working at AIHR means taking on a lot of responsibility and getting countless opportunities to develop yourself in new areas and potential to craft your own role.


Role and Responsibilities

As our Senior Sales Operations Manager, your job is to make it easier for Sales to do great work. This is a hands-on role with a broad view of the commercial journey. You’ll work on how Sales operates, support leadership with better insight, and own processes such as the Deal Desk, vendor registration, invoicing, collections, and order-to-cash.

We see those responsibilities as connected. Being close to the day-to-day work gives you the context to see where time is being lost, where a process no longer works, and where the same problem keeps coming back. We want someone who is comfortable doing the work themselves, but who does not simply accept unnecessary manual work because “that’s how we do it.”

This role is a combination of keeping things moving today and making sure they work better tomorrow.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Improving how Sales works. You use data, feedback, and your understanding of the day-to-day work to identify where things can be better. That could mean redesigning a workflow, improving reporting, clarifying ownership, creating a better operating rhythm, or removing manual steps that no longer add value.

  • Helping Sales leadership improve performance. You look beyond individual requests and help spot patterns across the Sales organization. Where are deals slowing down? What does the data tell us about why? Are we missing information in HubSpot that would help Sales, Marketing, or leadership make better decisions? You turn those observations into practical recommendations and are comfortable challenging existing ways of working when the data points somewhere else.

  • Owning and improving the Deal Desk. When a deal needs something outside the standard process, you help move it forward. This can include approvals, documentation, commercial questions, vendor or supplier registration, procurement portals, questionnaires, and coordination across internal and external stakeholders. You take care of the immediate need, while also looking for patterns that could make the next request simpler.

  • Owning order-to-cash and collections. You take responsibility for turning booked revenue into collected cash. Collections is a meaningful and hands-on part of the role: monitoring outstanding invoices, following up with customers, picking up the phone when that is the best way to resolve an issue, and working with Sales, Finance, procurement teams, and other stakeholders to clear payment blockers. You also look at the process behind the work — reducing overdue balances, improving follow-up, and finding ways to make order-to-cash more effective over time.

  • Working AI-first. You actively use AI and automation where they can make the work more efficient or improve the quality of the outcome. That might mean analyzing patterns in Sales data, speeding up vendor registration, improving a recurring workflow, or removing repetitive administrative work. As part of RevOps, you are expected to try new approaches, keep what works, and share useful ways of working with the wider team.

  • Connecting the dots across teams. Many commercial processes cross Sales, Finance, Customer Experience, Marketing, Operations, and other parts of the business. You help create clarity around ownership, bring the right people together, and make sure decisions turn into action.

You’ll work with tools including HubSpot, Gong, Atlassian, QuotaPath, Zapier, Google Workspace, and a growing set of AI tools and internal AI workflows. We do not expect you to arrive as an expert in every system. We do expect you to be comfortable learning how they fit together and questioning whether we are using them in the best way.

Success in this role is not simply an empty queue or a dashboard that looks good. It is reliable day-to-day execution combined with steady improvement in how Sales operates.

 

On a typical day

On Monday morning, you start by getting a view of the commercial week ahead. You check active deals in HubSpot, outstanding operational requests, the payments inbox, and anything else that needs attention.

During the RevOps stand-up with the RevOps team, you talk through priorities. An Account Executive is working on an enterprise opportunity where the customer's procurement team needs AIHR registered as a vendor. Several invoices need follow-up. You have also noticed a group of deals spending longer than expected in one stage of the pipeline.

The vendor registration comes first. You use one of our existing AI workflows to help complete the documentation, gather any missing information internally, and get the process moving. While doing that, you notice that part of the information the workflow relies on is out of date. Rather than working around it, you fix the source and make sure the next registration is easier.

Later, you turn to the stalled opportunities. You dig into the data, speak with the Sales team, and find that Account Executives are not consistently recording meeting outcomes. That makes it difficult to understand why certain MQLs progress while others do not.

The answer may not be “Sales needs to update HubSpot more.” You look at why the information is not being captured in the first place and whether the workflow can be made easier for reps while still giving Marketing and leadership the information they need. You believe it’s easier to change a process than to change human behaviors.

After lunch with colleagues in the office, you spend time on collections. Some invoices need a straightforward reminder. Others need more persistence. You follow up with customers, get on the phone where needed, and work through issues involving purchase orders, invoicing details, procurement processes, or internal ownership.

This work is part of the role, not something sitting outside it. And because you are doing it yourself, you see first-hand which issues are one-offs and which ones point to something we should fix.

On another day, you sit down with Sales leadership to look at commercial performance. You are not there simply to report what happened. You help interpret what is behind the numbers and what we might do differently.

You also regularly connect with Neal, Head of CX & Operations, and colleagues across Business Operations. Some weeks you will spend more time on live operational work; other weeks give you more room to improve reporting, build an automation in Zapier, clean up a process in HubSpot, or work on a broader RevOps project.

That balance is part of the role.

By Friday, a good week means the work got done: customers were followed up, deals moved forward, Sales had the support they needed, and something in the way we operate is now a little clearer or easier than it was before.

title: Data Engineer
description:
De wereld om ons heen verandert razendsnel. Wat vandaag nieuw is, kan morgen alweer achterhaald zijn. Bij PuurData krijg je de kans om samen met collega’s te werken aan slimme oplossingen voor onze klanten. Zo kun je bijvoorbeeld bedrijven helpen met het inzichtelijk maken van hun data of meedenken over hoe ze veiliger met hun data om kunnen gaan. Je helpt onze klanten vooruit door ze mee te nemen in nieuwe technologieën en te laten zien waar bijvoorbeeld AI daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegt. Op deze manier kun je zowel kleine, maar ook grote en veeleisende bedrijven helpen met oplossingen die kritisch zijn voor hun bedrijfsvoering.  

Tenslotte zorgen wij er samen voor dat jij continu blijft groeien en op de hoogte bent van de nieuwste ontwikkelingen. 

 

Wat ga je doen?  

Als Data Engineer bij PuurData ben je meer dan een technicus. Je bent een consultant die klanten helpt om meer waarde uit hun data te halen. PuurData werkt met platformen zoals Elastic en AWS, en bedient klanten op het gebied van zoektechnologie, observability, security en AI. Jij bent degene die die oplossingen tot leven brengt.

Je start bij de klant. Je inventariseert de vraag: wat willen ze met hun data? Gaat het om betere zoekfunctionaliteit, real-time inzicht in systemen, of security en threat detection? Klanten weten vaak dat er iets niet klopt. Data is traag, er is geen inzicht, of er zijn performance problemen. Maar ze weten niet altijd hoe ze het moeten oplossen. Jij helpt dat helder te maken.

Geen probleem. Als je leergierig bent en en affiniteit hebt met data, komen we graag met je in contact.

title: Medior C++ Software Engineer
description:
About Vitestro

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™). This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement.

As a Medior C++ Engineer, you will take ownership of software components within our hardware-integrated systems. You will design, implement, and improve robust C++ software that interacts with multiple subsystems, and real-time environments. You will collaborate closely with hardware engineers, systems engineers, and other software developers to ensure system reliability, maintainability, and performance.

First months at Vitestro

In your first months, you get to know Vitestro's software architecture, hardware-integrated systems, and development processes. You build an understanding of how our software interacts with different subsystems and start contributing to the design, implementation, and improvement of software components in modern C++ (C++17/20).

Working closely with hardware engineers, systems engineers, and other software developers, you become familiar with our state-machine-based logic, DDS communication protocols, and Linux and real-time environments. You contribute to debugging, automated testing, and code reviews while building the knowledge needed to take ownership of software components.

After your first month you will be able to contribute to the velocity of the team by working on new features in the scope of the motion team. You will be able to solve complex integration issues coming from production and the field.

This is what success looks like

After 12 months, you have taken ownership of software components within our hardware-integrated systems. You confidently design, implement, and maintain robust C++ software that interacts with multiple subsystems and real-time environments.

You actively contribute to improving the existing software architecture, ensuring maintainability, scalability, and performance. You design and maintain structured state-machine-based logic, integrate evolving hardware components into the software stack, and contribute to system-level design discussions and technical decisions.

You work effectively with hardware engineers, systems engineers, and other software developers to debug complex issues across software and hardware boundaries. You have contributed to improving testability and automated verification strategies, actively participate in code reviews, and help raise software quality standards.

After your first year, you will own significant nontrivial features and parts of the code-base of the team. You will be a key knowledge holder of the implementation of the motion software unit as well as accuracy calibrations and verifications. You actively engage in building the roadmap for the coming years together with other engineers.


What You'll Bring:

  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • 4–7 years of experience developing C++ software in a professional environment.

  • Proven experience designing and maintaining production-level software systems.

  • Strong proficiency in modern C++ (C++17/20).

  • Experience structuring code for maintainability and scalability.

title: Senior Quality Systems Officer
description:
About Vitestro

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™). This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

 

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

 

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement.

As our Senior QS officer, you focus on the continuous improvement of our quality systems and support the company through the change control process. You review existing quality processes, identify where they can be improved or made more compliant, and help develop practical solutions to make those improvements happen. 

You also guide colleagues through change control. Rather than executing every change yourself, you ensure people understand and follow the process, ask the right questions, consider the relevant implications, obtain the necessary approvals, and ensure that changes are completed Correctly and on time. 

This role requires a strong analytical and systematic mindset combined with a pragmatic approach to quality. You should be comfortable identifying problems, but more importantly, finding workable solutions and alternatives. You understand the requirements of working in a regulated environment without approaching quality as simply enforcing rules. You are able to adapt, think creatively and help the organisation find compliant ways forward.

First months at Vitestro

In your first months, you get to know Vitestro’s quality systems, processes, and the teams working with them. You build a thorough understanding of our Change Control process and start supporting colleagues through changes, helping them consider the right questions and ensuring changes are complete, appropriately approved, and progressing on time. As you become familiar with how we work, you identify opportunities to improve the compliance and efficiency of the Change Control process and develop a clear plan for implementing those improvements.

This is what success looks like:

After 12 months, you are a trusted partner for colleagues working with our quality systems and Change Control process. You confidently support the organization in executing changes, ensuring they are well considered, appropriately approved, and completed on time. You have improved the Change Control process to strengthen both compliance and efficiency, and have identified and implemented improvements across other areas of the QMS. You combine strong analytical thinking with a pragmatic and creative approach. You don’t just identify where something could be improved; you translate those insights into practical solutions and, when one approach doesn’t work, find alternative ways forward.


What You’ll Bring:

  • Strong analytical thinking and the ability to assess existing processes, identify where issues occur and determine how they can be improved.

  • Experience working in a regulated environment.

  • Relevant professional experience that provides an understanding of how quality systems and processes work.

  • A systematic, process-oriented way of working.

  • The ability to identify and develop solutions to quality and process problems.

  • A pragmatic and adaptable mindset, with the ability to think beyond rigid or established approaches while respecting regulatory requirements.

  • The ability to guide colleagues through processes by asking questions, highlighting considerations and ensuring required steps are completed.

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in engineering, applied sciences, biomedical engineering, or similar technical field

  • Minimum 3 to 5 years experience in Quality Assurance / Quality Systems for medical devices.

Nice to have:

  • Experience across multiple organisations or environments, providing exposure to different ways of working.

  • Medical-device experience can be relevant but is not required.

  • Experience with MDSAP

How We Work

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

  • We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

  • We focus on execution and delivering results.

  • We proactively remove blockers and help each other succeed.

  • We challenge ideas, not people.

  • We continuously learn, improve, and raise the bar.

  • We celebrate team success over individual heroics.

We move fast, but we do so thoughtfully. We care deeply about quality because the technology we build ultimately impacts patients and healthcare professionals.

If you are looking for an environment where you can make a significant contribution, take ownership of meaningful work, and be surrounded by highly motivated colleagues, we'd love to meet you.

What we offer 

  • Competitive salary including pension plan 

  • 25 days of annual leave based on a full-time position 

  • Hybrid work model 

  • Working together in a high-skilled team with our home base in Utrecht 

  • Frequent out-of-work activities with our team, and annual company weekend away.

  • Training budget 

  • Opportunity to be key shaper of a new global industry niche: autonomous medical robotics 

We’re big fans of working from the office – this is where team spirit comes alive. At the same time, we offer flexibility, allowing up to two (out of 5) days of working from home for those who prefer it. 

Are you excited? 

We totally understand that and so are we! By joining us, you can play an active role in changing the future of health care. Excited to join our revolution? Then we’d love to hear from you! 

If you think you've got what it takes, but you don't meet all the requirements - we still recommend you apply. title: wo-stage economie: Nowcasting Model voor BBP
description:
wo-praktijkstage,

start in overleg

Krijg jij energie van het bouwen van slimme datamodellen die economische groei voorspellen nog voordat alle cijfers binnen zijn? Duik jij graag in data, ontdek je nieuwe databronnen en wil je met jouw analyses échte impact maken op officiële bbp-ramingen?
Dan is deze stage in nowcasting en econometrie precies wat je zoekt.

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Bij het ramen van de kwartaalcijfers van het bbp (economische groei) gebruiken we voor een aantal bedrijfstakken momenteel een relatief eenvoudige methode: de ontwikkeling van het aantal banen dient als benadering voor de economische activiteit. Dit gebeurt omdat directe en tijdige broninformatie ontbreekt. Een belangrijk gevolg hiervan is dat we de eerste ramingen later vaak moeten bijstellen wanneer er meer volledige data beschikbaar komt bij de definitieve raming (ongeveer anderhalf jaar later).

Het is aan jou om deze methodiek te verbeteren.

Je gaat een geavanceerder model ontwikkelen waarmee we de economische activiteit van deze bedrijfstakken kort na afloop van de verslagperiode nauwkeuriger kunnen inschatten. Dit wordt ook wel “nowcasting” genoemd. Het doel is om dichter bij de uiteindelijke realisatie te zitten en daarmee het aantal en de omvang van latere bijstellingen te verkleinen.

Een belangrijk onderdeel van jouw opdracht is om te onderzoeken welke databronnen tijdig beschikbaar zijn en we kunnen gebruiken als input voor dit model. Vervolgens ga je met behulp van historische data eerdere verslagperiodes simuleren. Zo kun je analyseren of jouw voorgestelde methode daadwerkelijk beter presteert dan de huidige aanpak, bijvoorbeeld door te kijken naar kleinere bijstellingen.

Tot slot ontwikkel je een werkende productiestraat in R, zodat de nieuwe methode praktisch toepasbaar wordt binnen het ramingproces.

Dit is jouw stageplek,

bij CBS Den Haag

We verwelkomen je binnen de sector Nationale Rekeningen, bij het team Aanbod- en gebruiktabellen, dat bestaat uit ruim 25 mensen. Het team maakt de kwartaal- en jaarramingen van het bruto binnenlands product (bbp), en de economische groei. We zijn gedreven onderzoekers en producenten van cruciale informatie, waaronder de economische groei, en continu op zoek naar verbeteringen.

De nationale rekeningen vormen de officiële overzichtsstatistiek van de nationale economie. Het nationaal inkomen, de economische groei, het overheidstekort en het beschikbaar inkomen van huishoudens zijn enkele belangrijke macro-economische indicatoren die aan de hand van de nationale rekeningen worden vastgesteld.

Binnen ons team heerst een open, betrokken en collegiale sfeer. 

Twee ervaren teamleden zullen je begeleiden bij deze stageopdracht.

Dit breng jij mee

  • Je volgt een economische wo-opleiding met een duidelijke kwantitatieve component.

  • Je hebt kennis van – en bij voorkeur al enige ervaring met – softwareontwikkeling en programmeren in R.

  • Je werkt nauwkeurig en gestructureerd, zowel met data als met code en documentatie.

  • Je bent analytisch sterk en weet complexe vraagstukken te doorgronden en data kritisch te interpreteren.

  • Je denkt proactief mee over het verbeteren van bestaande methoden en staat open voor het verkennen van nieuwe ideeën en technieken.

  • Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor je eigen werk: je plant, organiseert en bewaakt je voortgang gedurende de stage.

Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk.

Dit kun je van ons verwachten

Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je:

  • Jouw programmeer- en analysevaardigheden inzet in een praktijkgerichte omgeving;

  • Jouw vakkennis vergroot door samen te werken met ervaren collega's;

  • Jouw kennis over econometrische en statistische modellen o.b.v. economische indicatoren in de praktijk gaat toepassen;

  • Waardevolle werkervaring opdoet voor een toekomstige carrière in data analyse of onderzoek.

Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week).

Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken.

Dit zijn onze voorwaarden

Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken. Deze stageopdracht is bedoeld voor studenten die momenteel staan ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling; afgestudeerden komen niet in aanmerking.

title: wo-stage statistiek: data-analyse en weegmethoden
description:
wo-afstudeerstage, start in overleg

Op zoek naar een statistiekstage?
Analyseer bij het CBS weegmethoden en non-respons met R en draag bij aan betere statistieken voor Nederland.

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het CBS trekt steekproeven onder de Nederlandse bevolking om diverse statistieken te maken. Hierbij is sprake van selectieve non-respons. Om voor deze non-respons te corrigeren, voeren we een zogenaamde weging uit, waarbij personen een gewicht krijgen op basis van hun onder- of oververtegenwoordiging in de respons. Personen met achtergrondkenmerken die ondervertegenwoordigd zijn in de respons, krijgen dan een groter gewicht dan personen met achtergrondkenmerken die oververtegenwoordigd zijn. Zie bijvoorbeeld [1] voor algemene informatie over wegen.

Bij het uitvoeren van een weging zijn er diverse zaken om rekening mee te houden. Zo kan niet voor alle achtergrondkenmerken worden gecorrigeerd voor scheefheid, omdat de gewichten dan te extreem zouden worden. Daarnaast is het vaak verstandig om überhaupt niet voor te veel achtergrondkenmerken te corrigeren, omdat dit een negatieve invloed heeft op de marges van de schattingen voor de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek. Ook is er een relatie met de doelvariabelen in het onderzoek: op het moment dat er een samenhang is tussen een achtergrondkenmerk en de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek, is het wenselijk om wél voor dat achtergrondkenmerk te corrigeren als dat kenmerk scheef in de respons zit. Het is daarom vaak verstandig om toch zo veel mogelijk te corrigeren voor scheefheid in achtergrondkenmerken.

Het CBS heeft een reguliere werkwijze voor het opstellen en uitvoeren van wegingen voor reguliere onderzoeken. Een optie die nog niet wordt gebruikt, maar wel interessant lijkt, is het uitvoeren van een zogenaamde voorweging. Hierbij wordt de weging min of meer in twee stappen uitgevoerd, waardoor er mogelijk voor meer en/of andere achtergrondkenmerken gecorrigeerd kan worden. Wellicht is het mogelijk om eerst een correctie uit te voeren voor non-respons en vervolgens een verdere weging uit te voeren die meer focust op de doelvariabelen van het onderzoek en de achtergrondkenmerken die daarmee correleren. Dit soort vragen speelt zowel bij de reguliere steekproeven die bij het CBS worden uitgevoerd als bij potentiële nieuwe toepassingen. In deze stage ga je aan de slag om verschillende opties voor de weging te analyseren, te kijken naar de verschillen tussen deze opties en te bepalen welke keuze de voorkeur heeft.

Afhankelijk van de resultaten zouden weegmethoden aangepast kunnen worden, met directe impact op de statistieken van het CBS.

[1] https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/onze-diensten/methoden/statistische-methoden/throughput/throughput/wegen-als-correctie-voor-non-respons 

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Heerlen

Binnen het team waar je komt te werken, worden nagenoeg alle steekproeven voor het CBS getrokken. Hiermee staan we aan de kern van het waarneemproces en komen er allerlei statistieken langs bij het team. Daarnaast zijn we betrokken bij het maken van schattingen: hoe kunnen we de respondenten op zo’n manier mee laten tellen dat er zinnige resultaten uit onze onderzoeken komen die ook daadwerkelijk iets zeggen over de gehele populatie?

We zijn een team met hoogopgeleide professionals die hoge kwaliteit nastreven. Als onze methoden verbeterd of uitgebreid kunnen worden, zodat we beter uit de voeten kunnen met de data die het CBS verzamelt, dan worden wij daar heel blij van. In deze stage ga je kijken of zulke mogelijkheden er zijn. Afhankelijk van de resultaten zullen we bestaande methoden opnieuw bekijken en kunnen onze methoden misschien worden toegepast op datasets waar dat nu (nog) niet mogelijk is.

Dit breng jij mee

Je volgt een bèta-opleiding op wo-niveau met als studierichting statistiek.

Je hebt kennis van en wellicht ervaring met:

  • data-analyse;

  • diverse onderzoeksmethoden en -technieken;

Kernwoorden die jou omschrijven zijn proactief, analytisch, communicatief sterk en kritisch.

description:

Ben jij die nieuwsgierige statistiekstudent die energie krijgt van data-analyse en complexe vraagstukken? Tijdens deze afstudeerstage bij het CBS duik je in echte data, werk je met R en draag je bij aan betere statistieken voor Nederland.

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het CBS trekt steekproeven onder de Nederlandse bevolking om diverse statistieken te maken. Hierbij is sprake van selectieve nonrespons. We ondernemen diverse pogingen om de respons zo gelijkmatig mogelijk te laten zijn (naar diverse achtergrondkenmerken van personen). We proberen daarbij zo veel mogelijk respons binnen te krijgen, maar kijken tegelijkertijd ook naar de samenstelling van de respons. In het bijzonder kijken we daar bij diverse onderzoeken naar in de vorm van doelgroepgericht benaderen [1].

Omdat het verzenden van brieven steeds duurder wordt, wordt de afweging tussen kwaliteit en kosten ook voor onderzoeken die alleen via internetwaarneming plaatsvinden steeds relevanter. Bij dit soort onderzoeken worden meerdere brieven verstuurd als personen niet direct de vragenlijst invullen. Omdat deze brieven steeds duurder worden, lijkt het voor de hand te liggen om geen herinneringen te sturen naar personen die nog niet gerespondeerd hebben, maar tegelijkertijd ook tot groepen behoren die al voldoende gerespondeerd hebben. In zekere zin zou dit ook een doelgroepgerichte benadering zijn.

In deze stage ga jij aan de slag met een van de kernprocessen binnen het CBS: het trekken en uitbaten van de steekproef.
Dit raakt de kern van onze processen: zonder data van goede kwaliteit kunnen we geen hoogwaardige statistieken maken.
Jij gaat kijken naar de gevolgen voor onze statistieken van diverse keuzes die we bij het design kunnen maken. Zijn er verschuivingen in de samenstelling van de respons en zo ja, kunnen we begrijpen waarom die verschuivingen er zijn? En, misschien nog wel belangrijker, is er nog iets te merken van eventuele verschuivingen bij het maken van de statistieken? Wat gebeurt er als je bepaalde groepen weglaat uit de respons? 

Afhankelijk van de uitkomsten is het wellicht handig en wenselijk om een soort doelgroepenbenadering in te voeren bij onderzoeken met alleen CAWI-waarneming. Gezien de stijgende kosten van het versturen van brieven, zou het zomaar kunnen dat we dit daadwerkelijk in gaan voeren.
