title: Apporteur d’affaires indépendant (H/F)
description:
🚀 Apporteur d’affaires indépendant — Développez votre réseau avec PropertyOS

100 % à distance · Organisation libre · Commission sur les ventes issues de vos recommandations

Vous aimez créer des contacts, repérer des opportunités et mettre les bonnes personnes en relation ?

Avec PropertyOS, vous identifiez des propriétaires, bailleurs ou petites agences intéressés par une gestion immobilière plus simple. Vous organisez le rendez-vous : le fondateur assure la démonstration et le closing.

🏡 PropertyOS, c’est quoi ?

PropertyOS est une plateforme SaaS qui centralise les biens immobiliers, les locataires, les finances, les documents et les tâches dans un même espace.

Notre ambition : permettre aux propriétaires et gestionnaires de gagner du temps et de garder une vision claire de leur activité immobilière.

La plateforme est accessible directement en ligne. Nous développons également un réseau de partenaires indépendants pour la faire découvrir à de nouveaux clients grâce à une approche plus personnelle.

🎯 Votre mission : créer des opportunités qualifiées

Votre rôle consiste à :

  • Identifier des propriétaires bailleurs, investisseurs et petites agences susceptibles d’être intéressés.

  • Entrer en contact avec eux et comprendre leur organisation actuelle.

  • Présenter simplement PropertyOS et son intérêt.

  • Vérifier leur intérêt pour une démonstration et pour le budget proposé.

  • Organiser un rendez-vous avec le fondateur.

  • Enregistrer les informations utiles dans PropertyOS Advisor pour préparer l’échange.

Vous vous concentrez sur la prospection et la mise en relation. Le fondateur prend ensuite le relais pour la démonstration détaillée, les questions commerciales, la négociation et la conclusion de l’abonnement.

Vous ne négociez pas les conditions et ne signez pas de contrat au nom de PropertyOS.

⚡ PropertyOS Advisor : votre application partenaire

Vous disposez de PropertyOS Advisor, notre application dédiée aux apporteurs d’affaires.

Pensée pour fluidifier votre activité, elle vous permet de centraliser les informations de vos prospects, suivre vos mises en relation et transmettre le contexte nécessaire à la préparation des rendez-vous.

L’objectif : une prospection organisée et un passage de relais simple, pour donner à chaque opportunité les meilleures chances d’aboutir.

💸 Une rémunération liée aux clients apportés

L’offre mise en avant dans ce partenariat est l’abonnement annuel PropertyOS à 990 €.

Vous percevez une commission pour chaque nouveau client qui souscrit et règle cet abonnement à la suite de votre mise en relation, selon les conditions prévues au contrat.

  • Rémunération à la commission uniquement.

  • Aucun salaire fixe ni revenu garanti.

  • Le montant de la commission et le calendrier de versement sont communiqués avant tout engagement.

  • Les règles d’attribution des prospects, de traitement des doublons et d’annulation sont précisées au contrat.

  • Un rendez-vous seul ne déclenche pas de commission : celle-ci dépend de la souscription et de l’encaissement correspondants.

👋 À qui s’adresse cette opportunité ?

À des personnes autonomes, à l’aise dans les échanges et capables de créer un premier contact de qualité.

Vous pouvez avoir une expérience commerciale, un réseau dans l’immobilier ou simplement une vraie capacité à prospecter avec méthode.

Nous recherchons surtout :

  • De l’écoute, pour repérer un besoin réel.

  • De la clarté, pour expliquer la solution sans faire de promesses excessives.

  • De la régularité, pour développer votre activité.

  • De la rigueur, pour transmettre des informations fiables.

  • Un bon relationnel, pour représenter PropertyOS avec professionnalisme.

Une expérience en prospection, en immobilier ou dans le SaaS est un atout. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être un expert du logiciel ni un closer confirmé.

🌴 Notre culture : détendue, directe et orientée résultats

Chez PropertyOS, on apprécie les échanges simples, les idées utiles et les personnes qui prennent des initiatives.

Vous organisez librement votre activité : pas d’horaires imposés ni de volume hebdomadaire obligatoire. Cette collaboration peut compléter d’autres activités professionnelles.

Notre façon d’avancer : partager les retours du terrain, améliorer les approches et privilégier des mises en relation pertinentes.

Une ambiance chill, des engagements tenus et des opportunités concrètes.

🤝 Pour bien démarrer

La prise en main comprend :

  • Une présentation de PropertyOS et de ses principaux cas d’usage.

  • La découverte de PropertyOS Advisor.

  • Des repères pour identifier les profils de clients recherchés.

  • Des supports pour présenter la solution.

  • Une explication du processus de mise en relation et de rémunération.

Vous avez un interlocuteur direct pour transmettre vos questions et vos retours.

📋 Cadre de la collaboration

Nature : partenariat indépendant d’apport d’affaires, sans contrat de travail.
Lieu : à distance, depuis la France.
Organisation : libre, sans exclusivité.
Démarrage : à convenir ensemble.

Vous devez disposer d’une activité indépendante déclarée et d’un SIRET pour exercer depuis la France. La micro-entreprise est une possibilité.

Vous pouvez candidater avant d’avoir créé votre activité, mais les formalités nécessaires devront être réalisées pour démarrer la collaboration.

Un contrat écrit définit les missions, les commissions et les conditions du partenariat.

🚀 Intéressé ? Présentez-vous simplement.

Envoyez-nous quelques lignes sur :

  • Votre parcours et votre éventuelle expérience en prospection.

  • Les types de prospects que vous pourriez contacter.

  • Votre statut actuel et vos disponibilités pour démarrer.

Vous créez le contact. Nous prenons le relais pour transformer l’intérêt en abonnement.

title: Customer Success Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Angefangen hat alles vor sieben Jahren als ambitionierte Idee. Heute sind wir Marktführer für Abschlusszeitungen in Deutschland. Jedes Jahr nutzen mehr als zwei Drittel aller deutschen Abschlussjahrgänge die nuggit App, um ihre Abschlusszeitung und ihre Abschlusstextilien zu gestalten und sich damit eine Erinnerung an eine gemeinsame Zeit zu schaffen, die bleibt.

Unsere Mission: Durch digitale Innovation und persönlichen Kundenkontakt sind wir für SchülerInnen der verlässliche Partner bei ihrem allerersten großen Projekt. Dafür hinterfragen wir permanent den Status Quo und entwickeln neue, kreative Lösungen.

Wir sind ein kleines Team mit sehr großer Reichweite. Als Customer Success Manager (m/w/d) bist du die persönliche Ansprechperson für unsere Abschlussjahrgänge, von der Angebotsannahme bis zur Lieferung. Standardfragen beantworten bei uns Chatbot und Helpcenter, das Onboarding läuft über Videos und Formulare. Du kümmerst dich um das, was Automatisierung nicht kann: echte Beziehungen zu den Jahrgängen aufbauen und dafür sorgen, dass jedes Projekt sicher ins Ziel kommt. Das heißt kurze Wege, direkte Wirkung und viel Verantwortung. Es heißt aber auch, dass du eigenständig arbeiten und priorisieren musst.

Aufgaben

  • Betreuung: Du betreust unsere Jahrgänge per Videocall, Chat und Telefon und bist für alles da, was über Chatbot und Helpcenter hinausgeht.

  • Projektbegleitung: Du begleitest jeden Jahrgang von der Angebotsannahme bis zur Lieferung, behältst Fristen und Freigaben im Blick und fasst nach, wenn ein Projekt hängt. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unserem Operations-Team zusammen, das Produktion und Lieferung steuert.

  • Pipeline: Du hast deine Kunden eigenständig im Griff: Status, nächste Schritte, Risiken. Wo es eng wird, merkst du es vor dem Kunden.

  • Video-Sprechstunden: Wir bauen buchbare Video-Calls auf, in denen SchülerInnen intensive Begleitung bei ihrem Projekt bekommen. Du gestaltest das Format mit und führst die Calls.

  • Self-Service: Du erkennst, welche Fragen immer wiederkommen, und sorgst dafür, dass Chatbot und Helpcenter sie künftig beantworten.

  • Wachstum: Wenn du Lust hast, wächst du in Upselling und Referral hinein: Textilien für Jahrbuch-Kunden, Jahrbuch für Textil-Kunden, Schulshops und Empfehlungen an andere Jahrgänge und Schulen.

So arbeiten wir

  • Persönlich ist unser Unterschied. Unsere Kunden sind 17, 18 oder 19 Jahre alt und stemmen oft ihr erstes großes Projekt. Sie brauchen jemanden, der erreichbar ist, mitdenkt und ehrlich sagt, wenn es eng wird.

  • Automatisierung entlastet dich, sie ersetzt dich nicht. Chatbot, Helpcenter und Onboarding-Videos nehmen dir die Standardfragen ab, damit du Zeit für die Gespräche hast, die wirklich zählen.

  • Eigeninitiative ist Pflicht, nicht Bonus. Du bekommst Ziele und Kontext, den Weg gestaltest du selbst. Niemand treibt dich an, aber alle verlassen sich auf dich.

  • Hybrid, ehrlich gemeint. Unser neues Office liegt im Mindspace in der Uhlandstraße 32, direkt am Kudamm und bestens angebunden, mit allen Annehmlichkeiten eines Coworking Space. Alle weiteren Mindspace Standorte kannst du temporär mitnutzen. Homeoffice und mobiles Arbeiten sind selbstverständlich möglich, solange das Ergebnis stimmt.

Qualifikation

  • Du hast bereits Erfahrung im Kundenservice, Support oder Customer Success gesammelt. Wie lange, interessiert uns weniger als das, was du daraus mitnimmst.

  • Du kannst mit jungen Menschen: locker im Ton, verbindlich in der Sache.

  • Telefon und Kamera schrecken dich nicht ab, im Gegenteil.

  • Du organisierst dich selbst und behältst auch bei vielen parallelen Projekten den Überblick.

  • Du lieferst zuverlässig, auch wenn viel gleichzeitig läuft. Unsere Saison hat klare Peaks.

  • Du arbeitest sicher mit CRM-Tools und digitalen Kanälen.

  • Du erkennst, wenn ein Kunde mehr braucht, und sprichst es an. Vertriebserfahrung ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss.

  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch. Das ist bei uns Voraussetzung, weil unsere Kunden deutschsprachig sind.

  • Du hast eine proaktive Haltung und arbeitest gerne eng mit anderen Teams zusammen.

Benefits

Unser Angebot

  • Du begleitest jedes Jahr Abschlussjahrgänge aus ganz Deutschland bei ihrem allerersten großen Projekt

  • Eine Rolle mit Perspektive: vom Support hin zu echtem Customer Success mit Upselling und Referral

  • Ein kleines Team, in dem deine Arbeit direkt sichtbar ist

  • Kurze Wege und offene Ohren: Ideen landen bei uns direkt beim Entscheider, ohne Zwischenebenen

  • 30 Urlaubstage, Firmenlaptop, Sachgutscheine sowie D-Ticket oder JobRad

Die perfekte Bewerberin oder den perfekten Bewerber gibt es nicht. Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung, auch wenn du die Anforderungen (noch) nicht zu 100 % erfüllst, du aber die Motivation mitbringst, dir die nötigen Fähigkeiten anzueignen. Wir begrüßen BewerberInnen verschiedenster Hintergründe, ungeachtet ihrer Geschlechtsidentität, Religion, Ethnizität, nationaler Herkunft, sexuellen Orientierung, Migrationsgeschichte, Alter oder Einschränkungen.

title: Business Development Representative (m/w/d) - AI Agent Platform
description:
Ninox ist eine Berliner Low-Code-Plattform, mit der Teams genau die Geschäftsanwendungen bauen, die sie brauchen. Rund 80 Mitarbeitende, tausende Kundinnen und Kunden in ganz Europa, vom kleinen Team bis zum Großunternehmen. Ein Produkt, an dem Menschen wirklich hängen. Wir sind seit 12 Jahren am Markt, etabliert, wachsen und sind solide mit Wagniskapital finanziert.

Worum es geht

Du machst Outbound. Zu 100 %, und vor allem am Telefon.

Du bekommst Zielaccounts aus Branchen, die wir vorab festlegen, findest dort die Menschen, die das Problem tatsächlich haben, rufst sie an — und buchst qualifizierte Erstgespräche für unsere Account Executives. Nach dem Handover übernimmt der AE. Dein Ergebnis ist das stattgefundene, qualifizierte Gespräch, nicht der Abschluss und nicht der Kalendereintrag.

Der größte Teil unseres Geschäfts sind kleine und mittlere Unternehmen, dazu kommt ein solider Anteil Mid-Market. Innerhalb der Verticals, die für uns nachweislich funktionieren, gehen wir gelegentlich auch in größere Organisationen. Damit es keine Missverständnisse gibt: „Enterprise" heißt bei uns Unternehmen mit einigen hundert bis wenigen tausend Mitarbeitenden — nicht DAX-Konzern mit zweijährigem Beschaffungsprozess und Rahmenvertragsverhandlung.

Du arbeitest auf Deutsch und auf Englisch, jeden Tag. Deutschland und Großbritannien sind unsere Kernmärkte, weitere europäische Länder kommen situativ dazu.

Dein Umfeld, ehrlich beschrieben: Unser Vertrieb arbeitet heute Full-Funnel. Die Account Executives machen neben allem anderen rund eine Stunde Outbound pro Tag. Dazu kommt eine Kollegin bzw. ein Kollege mit ebenfalls reinem Outbound-Fokus, allerdings auf Kooperationen, Webinare und Partner. Du bist damit die erste Person bei uns, die ausschließlich und direkt auf Neukunden-Erstgespräche geht. Das heißt: Es gibt Erfahrung im Haus, an die du andocken kannst, und ein Playbook, das gerade entsteht. Welche Branchen wir angehen und mit welchen Kampagnen, verantworten unser Head of Sales und unser CRO. Dein Part ist das Gespräch, und was du dort hörst, fließt direkt in die nächste Runde ein.

Aufgaben

  • Telefon ist dein Hauptkanal. Cold Calling ist der Kern der Rolle, nicht ein Kanal unter mehreren. E-Mail und LinkedIn ergänzen die Ansprache

  • Ziellisten aus den Verticals abarbeiten, die Head of Sales und CRO festlegen. Die Listen kommen aufgebaut aus Clay und Cognism. Du priorisierst innerhalb der Liste und bereitest jeden Account kurz vor, bevor du anrufst

  • Kampagnen und Sequenzen in Lemlist setzen Head of Sales und CRO auf. Du führst sie aus und passt deinen Gesprächseinstieg im Call an dein Gegenüber an. Lemlist ist dein täglicher Arbeitsplatz, Clay und Cognism füttern ihn

  • Erstgespräche buchen, sauber vorbereiten und mit belastbarem Kontext an die Account Executives übergeben

  • Zurückspielen, was du im Markt hörst: welche Branche reagiert, welche Botschaft funktioniert, welche Einwände wiederkehren. Marketing und Sales-Leitung brauchen das

  • HubSpot sauber und aktuell halten — nicht als Selbstzweck, sondern weil Pipeline-Bewertung und Forecast darauf beruhen.

  • Enge Abstimmung mit Marketing und den AEs zu Kampagnen und Übergabekriterien

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens 1,5 Jahre Outbound-Erfahrung im B2B, idealerweise SaaS oder erklärungsbedürftige IT-Lösungen. Du musst nicht alles gesehen haben, aber du solltest den Job kennen und nicht bei null anfangen — ein spürbarer Teil dieser Zeit sollte am Telefon stattgefunden haben und nicht nur in Sequenzen. Das ist keine Einstiegsposition.

  • Deutsch verhandlungssicher auf muttersprachnahem Niveau (C2), Englisch mindestens C1. Beides täglich. Der Maßstab ist das Telefonat: Du führst auf Englisch ein Kaltgespräch, reagierst auf Einwände und hältst den Small Talk davor und danach aus, ohne dass die Sprache zum Thema wird. Wir hören uns das im Prozess an.

  • Du kannst nachvollziehbar erklären, warum deine Ansprache funktioniert hat — mit Zahlen und mit einer Begründung, nicht mit Bauchgefühl.

  • Du kommst mit Geschäftsführerinnen und Inhabern zurecht. Im Mittelstand hast du häufig direkt die Person am Telefon, die entscheidet — und die dir drei Minuten gibt, bevor sie wieder in den Betrieb muss. Erst in größeren Häusern sprichst du mit Fachbereichsleitungen und gelegentlich mit der IT.

  • Recherchefähigkeit: Du findest heraus, wer in einem Unternehmen ein Problem hat, bevor du zum Hörer greifst.

  • Selbstorganisation: Du strukturierst deine Woche selbst und brauchst keine tägliche Ansage, um in die Aktivität zu kommen.

  • Ein realistisches Verhältnis zu Ablehnung. Der größte Teil deiner Versuche führt zu nichts. Das ist normal und sollte dich weder überraschen noch aus der Ruhe bringen.

  • Sicherer Umgang mit CRM und Sales-Engagement-Tools. Unser Stack ist HubSpot, Lemlist, Clay und Cognism — genau diese Tools musst du nicht kennen, vergleichbare schon.

  • Du arbeitest selbstverständlich mit KI-Tools. Recherche verdichten, Textvarianten durchspielen, ein Unternehmen vor dem Call in fünf Minuten verstehen — das geht heute schneller, wenn man weiß wie. Wir erwarten keine Zertifikate, aber auch niemanden, der ChatGPT einmal ausprobiert und wieder weggelegt hat.

  • Von Vorteil: Du hast schon aktiv nach Großbritannien akquiriert und kennst den Unterschied im Gesprächseinstieg. Ebenfalls hilfreich: Erfahrung mit Low-Code/No-Code-, ERP-, CRM- oder Datenbankthemen.

Formale Abschlüsse sind uns weniger wichtig als belastbare Outbound-Praxis. Wenn du das kannst, interessiert uns dein Studienfach nicht.

Benefits

Was wir bieten

  • 60.000 – 70.000 € Zieljahresgehalt (OTE) bei einem Split von 70 % Fixum und 30 % variabel. Der variable Anteil hängt an Kriterien, die du beeinflussen kannst, und ist erreichbar geplant. Den Plan legen wir vor Vertragsunterschrift offen.

  • Strukturierter Einstieg: Produkt, ICP, Einwände und Gesprächsleitfäden in den ersten Wochen — plus regelmäßige 1:1s und Call-Reviews statt Zurufmanagement.

  • Kurze Wege. Du berichtest an Tim Genkinger, unseren Head of Sales, und hast direkten Zugang zu den Menschen, die über Produkt und Go-to-Market entscheiden.

  • 30 Urlaubstage, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, BVG-Ticket und weitere Benefits.

  • Hybrides Arbeiten in unserem Büro am Monbijouplatz in Berlin-Mitte.

  • Ein Stack, der die Arbeit tatsächlich trägt: HubSpot als CRM, Lemlist für Sequenzen, Clay für Listenaufbau und Anreicherung, Cognism für belastbare Telefonnummern. Dazu KI-Assistenz als fester Teil des Arbeitsalltags, bei uns Claude, für Recherche, Textvarianten und Call-Vorbereitung. Du verbringst deine Zeit mit Gesprächen und nicht mit der Suche nach Durchwahlen. Fehlt im Stack etwas, reden wir darüber.

  • Ein Unternehmen, klein genug, dass deine Ergebnisse sichtbar sind, und groß genug, dass sie etwas bewegen.

Was diese Rolle nicht ist

  • Kein Inbound. Anfragen aus Produkt und Marketing laufen an anderer Stelle. Es gibt keine eingehenden Leads und keine Messelisten zum Nachfassen.

  • Kein Closing. Angebot, Verhandlung und Abschluss liegen bei den AEs. Die Stelle ist als Outbound-Rolle ausgeschrieben, nicht als Durchgangsstation — wohin es danach geht, entscheidet sich über Ergebnisse und nicht über eine Zusage im Bewerbungsgespräch.

  • Keine Führungsrolle. Du baust kein Team auf und führst niemanden.

  • Keine reine Remote-Rolle. Wir hätten dich gern etwa zwei Tage pro Woche im Büro, im Haus sind das meist Dienstag bis Donnerstag. Mehr ist willkommen, weniger im Einzelfall auch machbar. Berlin als Lebensmittelpunkt setzen wir voraus.

  • Kein Produkt, das sich von selbst erklärt. Ninox ist keine Wissenschaft — in einer Demo versteht fast jeder, was es tut. Der Aufhänger liegt trotzdem nie im Produkt, sondern beim Gegenüber: das Excel-Konstrukt, das niemand mehr pflegen kann, die Standardsoftware, die nicht passt. Darauf musst du Lust haben.

Bewerbung

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein paar Sätze zu einer Ansprache, die funktioniert hat: wen du angesprochen hast, warum genau so, was dabei herauskam und was du daraus für den nächsten Versuch mitgenommen hast. Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht.

Unser Prozess besteht aus drei Terminen:

  1. Erstgespräch mit Tim Genkinger, Head of Sales und Hiring Manager dieser Rolle.

  2. Case Study. Du bekommst vorab eine Aufgabe und stellst sie Tim und Michael Blazek, unserem CRO, vor. Teile davon führen wir auf Englisch.

  3. Meet the Team. Du lernst die Kolleginnen und Kollegen kennen, mit denen du täglich arbeiten wirst.

Danach entscheiden wir. Wir halten den Prozess bewusst kurz und melden uns bei jeder Bewerbung zurück, auch bei einer Absage.

Ninox steht für ein Arbeitsumfeld ohne Diskriminierung. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen unabhängig von Herkunft, Geschlecht, Alter, Religion, Behinderung oder sexueller Identität.

You will own features end-to-end at a massive scale, ultimately empowering fraud analysts to uncover and investigate suspicious transactions faster than ever before.

Translate complexity to usability: Build out complex technical systems into intuitive, user-friendly interfaces.

Build fraud-fighting tools: Develop and optimize advanced graph systems to visualize fraud rings, and build performant search tools that help analysts rapidly identify suspicious transactions.

Collaborate cross-functionally: Work tightly with Design, Data, Product, and Account Management teams to align engineering output with business and user needs.

Ensure system health: Proactively diagnose, triage, and resolve bugs while writing highly efficient and performant code.

Core technical stack: Extensive experience writing efficient, production-ready code in TypeScript, Node.js, React, Go and other server programming languages.

Scale and data expertise: Proven experience working with data-intensive applications, complex workflows, and big data at scale.

Pipeline proficiency: Deep background in technical data modeling and building robust production data pipelines.

High-growth adaptability: The ability to thrive, execute, and deliver consistently in a fast-paced, high-growth startup environment.

Independent execution: A proven track record of taking extreme ownership of ambiguous problems and independently turning them into polished, scalable features.

  • Deep knowledge of the Java Virtual Machine, especially its memory model and performance characteristics in highly concurrent, data‑intensive workloads.

title: Deployment Lead - ERP Solutions
description:
What We Do

Rillet serves accounting and finance teams, the financial brains of their companies. Our job is to help them run the numbers with impossible speed, accuracy, and insight.

Rillet is the Agentic ERP built for modern finance teams. We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 600 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG.

We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.

Who We Are

Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.

The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.

Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan.

Rillet is built on deep accounting expertise, and it takes people from many disciplines to build a category-defining company. You do not need to be an accountant to thrive here. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Together, we combine the precision of accounting with the speed, creativity, and ambition of AI-native software to power the financial core of the world’s fastest-growing companies while redefining what finance teams should expect from their software.

Who We Need

We are building industry-defining accounting and finance software. We are looking for an experienced Deployment Lead to guide complex customer implementations and help finance teams successfully transition onto Rillet.

This role is ideal for someone who has led ERP implementations and understands how to turn complex accounting and operational requirements into practical systems solutions. You may come from an ERP implementation firm, Big 4 finance transformation practice, systems consulting team, or a SaaS company serving finance organizations. You are comfortable owning multiple workstreams, advising senior stakeholders, and navigating the details of configuration, data migration, integrations, testing, and go-live.

You will combine strong implementation judgment with a customer-first mindset—bringing structure to ambiguity, identifying risks early, and keeping customers and internal teams moving toward a successful launch.

We’re primarily looking for teammates who are based near our New York City or San Francisco offices, or open to relocating. For this role, we’re also open to remote candidates based anywhere in the United States. Our hybrid schedule brings office-based team members together in person on Tuesdays and Thursdays, plus one additional flexible day each week. Some roles may spend more time in the office depending on the needs of the team.

What You'll Do

  • Lead key parts of customer onboarding and deployment, helping ensure a smooth and timely implementation experience

  • Partner with internal teams across Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to execute implementation plans and solve customer problems quickly

  • Learn and analyze client accounting and finance workflows, then translate those needs into clear requirements and practical solutions

  • Guide customers through onboarding, training, change management, and adoption

  • Support data migration, reconciliations, systems setup, and integration coordination

  • Track milestones, drive follow-through, and keep internal and external stakeholders aligned throughout the onboarding process

  • Identify risks early, escalate issues quickly, and help keep customer launches on track

  • Build trust with customers by being responsive, thoughtful, and solutions-oriented

  • Maintain clear documentation and provide regular status updates to customers and internal stakeholders

Who We're Looking For

  • 4–7 years in ERP implementation, systems consulting, or finance transformation (e.g., Big 4 or implementation firms)

  • Background in SaaS, high-growth technology companies, or implementation/consulting environments is strongly preferred

  • Hands-on ERP experience (NetSuite, SAP, Workday, etc.), including requirements, configuration, data migration, and go-live

  • Strong understanding of core accounting workflows (close, reconciliations, ASC 606) and how they translate into systems

  • Customer-facing with strong communication and stakeholder management skills

  • Systems-minded with solid project management skills; able to run multiple workstreams

  • Comfortable in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and highly detail-oriented

  • Experience working cross-functionally with technical and non-technical teams

Tier A: $100,000 – $150,000

Tier C: $100,000 – $130,000

Life at Rillet

We are looking for a RAMS Engineer to strengthen our safety and compliance team, with a particular emphasis on safety engineering for our vehicles, propulsion systems, ground infrastructure, and operations.

RAMS covers Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, and Safety. Although the role sits within safety and compliance rather than systems engineering, you will need a strong systems-engineering background and experience working with high-reliability, high-safety, or mission-critical systems.

About us

We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications.

We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket.

We are working hard to build something truly spectacular.

To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

Key responsibilities

  • Establish and develop RAMS and safety-engineering processes across vehicles, propulsion systems, ground systems, facilities, and operations.

  • Define, manage, and verify reliability, availability, maintainability, and safety requirements throughout the system lifecycle.

  • Lead hazard identification, risk assessments, failure-mode analysis, fault-tree analysis, and other structured safety assessments.

  • Develop and maintain safety cases, hazard logs, RAMS plans, safety assessments, compliance evidence, and technical justifications.

  • Work with systems, propulsion, avionics, test, manufacturing, operations, and suppliers to identify hazards and implement effective risk controls.

  • Support design reviews, test-readiness reviews, operational-readiness activities, incident investigations, change control, and corrective actions.

What we are looking for

  • Proven experience in RAMS, safety engineering, reliability engineering, or systems engineering for high-reliability, high-safety, or mission-critical systems.

  • Experience analysing complex hardware and operational systems, including interfaces, failure modes, hazards, and system-level risks.

  • Strong understanding of safety-engineering methods and the ability to turn analysis into practical design and operational controls.

  • Experience producing clear technical documentation, safety arguments, risk assessments, compliance evidence, and engineering reports.

  • Strong communication skills, with the confidence to challenge technical decisions and work effectively with specialist engineering and operational teams.

  • A degree in systems engineering, safety engineering, aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related discipline; equivalent practical experience may also be relevant.

Desirable experience

  • RAMS or safety engineering within aerospace, space, defence, rocketry, missile systems, nuclear, rail, energy, automotive, or another high-consequence industry.

  • Experience with FMEA, FMECA, fault-tree analysis, hazard analysis, HAZOP, STPA, bow-tie analysis, or similar techniques.

  • Safety cases, functional-safety assessments, reliability predictions, maintainability analysis, or probabilistic risk assessment.

  • Propulsion systems, solid rocket motors, hazardous materials, explosives, test stands, launch operations, or high-energy systems.

  • Experience supporting verification and validation, qualification, acceptance testing, configuration control, and engineering change processes.

  • Familiarity with applicable aerospace, defence, functional-safety, quality, or hazardous-operations standards and regulatory frameworks.

title: UAV Software and Controls Engineer
description:
🚀 Join SE3 Labs as UAV Software and Controls Engineer

Lead the autonomy stack of our systems. Starting from custom firmware all the way to GCS plugins.

About SE3

SE3 Labs is building Spatial AI by combining 3D computer vision with large language models (LLMs). We believe the ability to reason about and act within physical space is foundational to unlocking the next generation of automation, from construction to smart infrastructure, and ultimately, defence.

Now, we’re building the physical platform to bring Spatial AI to life. That means high-performance, real-world robotic systems (starting with UAVs), and we’re looking for a skilled, hands-on engineer who’s ready to bring these machines into the real world.

About the Role

As Drone Software and Controls Engineer, you will be working on the full-stack avionics development of our UAV fleet. From selecting the components to tuning and configuring the UAV, all the way to GCS development and autonomy orchestration. You will be the brain behind the fleet.

You will be in the middle of the software and hardware team, mastering the integration of the two fields and bringing the final product to life.

What You’ll Work On

  • Architecture & Plan: Define and develop schematics for communication and integration of the software stack across all our systems. How does UAV A get a position from UGV B? How does Payload 1 inform UAV C that it needs to land?

  • Prototype & Iterate: Build, rework, and test hardware with speed and precision, both in simulation and in flight. Develop better simulations and tools for faster iteration.

  • Optimize & Troubleshoot: Analyse the full flow of information via simulation and real-world testing, including UAV to UAV, UAV to GCS or UAV to payload.

  • Document with Purpose: Keep clear records of requirements, tradeoffs, test results, tuning procedures, and implementation rationale

  • Validate in the Loop: Support hardware-in-the-loop and environmental validation workflows to ensure rugged, reliable implementations.

Your Profile

  • You hold a B.Sc. or higher in Aerospace Engineering or a related discipline

  • You bring 3+ years of hands-on experience in avionics development, from component selection and firmware design to full system integration

  • You’re confident with lab equipment (multimeters, scopes, spectrum analyzers, near-field probes) and use them to diagnose and debug with purpose

  • You have a deep understanding of Autonomy principles and know how to develop and deal with low level issues in a UAV fleet.

  • You’ve worked with PX4 and ArduPilot and know where to go in the code to get what you need.

  • You’re experienced with QGC and know how to customise it to your will.

  • You’re familiar with hardware-in-the-loop and environmental testing, and understand how designs fail in the wild

  • You speak fluent English; German is a strong plus

  • Most importantly, you’re structured, fast-moving, and mission-driven. You don’t wait for perfection. You iterate until it works. You love building things that last and love making them fly majestically..

Especially Valued Bonus Skills

  • Architecture and software development skills.

  • ArduPilot, PX4, or QGC open source contributor.

  • Flying License A1-A3

  • Experience with multi-vehicle coordination.

Perks & Benefits

  • Real Ownership: Get equity early, real stock options to participate directly in SE3’s growth

  • Work Environment to Excel at: Find a high-quality and modern toolset, flat hierarchy and a skilled, driven team which will push the limits together with you

  • 31 Paid Days Off: 30 vacation days plus your birthday off

  • Well-being Access: Free membership to gyms, yoga, and wellness through EGYM Wellpass

  • Team Offsites: We go on 2 company retreats per year, our last ones were in Italy and Greece

  • Mentorship: Work closely with experienced engineers and get paired with a professional mentor to support your growth

Our Process

  1. Intro Call (30 min): Let’s get to know each other

  2. Technical Interview (45 min): (We will deep diver into your experience and the role)

  3. Coding Interview(1 hr): (with our external coding partners)

  4. One site trial/case (1.5h): let’s build and test a system together with our hardware team

  5. Team Dinner / Lunch: Meet the team and see whether it is a strong fit on both sides.

You set the priorities, assign the owners, and drive each issue to resolution.

We expect our PBPs to lead with high agency, and this role carries that expectation further than any other. You'll set the regional People agenda, make the calls, and drive outcomes the way a regional Chief People Officer would, with specialist partners at HQ to pull in when you need them.

Location: Munich, Germany

  • Be the senior People leader and business strategist for EMEA. Understand where the regional business is going and bring leaders a clear point of view, with the tradeoffs of each option laid out. Translate business goals into talent decisions: org design, workforce planning, leveling, and succession. Use data to spot attrition risk, capability gaps, and structural problems before the business feels them, and treat your leaders as customers whose success is your measure.

  • Lead end-to-end People programs for the region. Know what has to stay consistent worldwide and what should flex by country, and bring HQ recommendations with the tradeoffs laid out, not just concerns. Treat each country in the region as its own environment, not as one market.

  • Lead the region through growth and change. Support expansion into new countries and entities, reorganizations, and leadership transitions with a clear plan, narrative, and follow-through with managers and teams.

  • Increase talent density. Lead calibration, promotion, and talent review for the region. Identify and develop top talent, coach managers to raise the bar on their teams, and handle performance and employee relations issues with judgment, discretion, and dignity. Move fast and move safe.

  • Strong judgment. You know when to move fast, when to slow down an irreversible decision, and when to bring in partners, and leaders trust your read on sensitive, ambiguous situations.

  • A record of influencing in both directions. You've advocated for a region with headquarters and challenged regional leaders when needed, and you can tell the difference between a legal requirement, a business need, and a preference.

  • A record of leading change, not just supporting it, including implementing global programs locally and guiding teams through growth or reorganization.

  • Fluency with data and clear, concise, direct communication, and the discipline to prioritize ruthlessly when everything feels urgent.

  • Business-level fluency in the local language is a plus. Comfort working across time zones with a People team based in California.

  • Experience building People programs from scratch in a high-growth company.

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. title: Market Product Lead
description:
About Us

Basecamp Research is building frontier AI for therapeutic design. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how.

Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData, the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development.

In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. We have offices and labs in London and Boston, we partner with biopharma companies and academic institutions worldwide, and our work has been recognised by Fast Company's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Biotech, the FT-backed Sifted AI100 list of Europe's leading AI startups as well as Barclays Eagle Labs Ones to watch, AI100.

At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The role

You will own the peptide and protein platform as a commercial product: the market analysis behind it, the target product profiles it is judged against, the decisions about what we build and license first, the go to market strategy and the positioning that partners hear. You will sit between our model and science teams and our business development function, and you will be accountable for the peptide portfolio having a defined buyer, a defensible claim and a credible price.

Key responsibilities

Market and competitive intelligence

  • Build and maintain a rigorous view of the peptide/protein therapeutics landscape by segment, indication and modality, mechanism trends and delivery technologies.

  • Track and interpret competitor activity across AI-enabled discovery platforms, peptide/protein-focused biotechs, screening technology providers, and internal pharmaceutical capability, and translate it into implications for our product road map and and go to market execution.

  • Maintain a live map of deal structures, comparables and valuation benchmarks in platform licensing and co-development, and advise on where our agreements should sit.

  • Bring the outside in: run structured voice-of-customer work with pharmaceutical R&D leaders, and turn it into prioritised, written requirements rather than anecdotes.

Target product profiles and programme definition

  • Author and defend target product profiles for internal programmes, specifying which properties are differentiated in the market and define evidence needs.

  • Translate partner-supplied target product profiles into feasible research plans in collaboration with scientific leadership, including honest assessments of what our platform can and cannot address today.

  • Define stage gates and go or no-go criteria for peptide programmes, and make the recommendation when a programme should stop.

Productization and roadmap

  • Decide, on evidence, which platform capabilities become licensable products and in what sequence, balancing near-term revenue against durable differentiation.

  • Own the peptide/product product roadmap end to end, agreeing priorities with model, data and science teams and holding the line on scope.

  • Define packaging and commercial models for each offering, including access arrangements, bespoke model fine-tuning on partner data, co-development structures and asset-level licensing.

  • Specify the data we need from partners in order to improve, and turn broad offers of collaboration into precise, written requests.

Positioning, evidence and partner engagement

  • Responsible for partner engagement and revenue generation in collaboration with the Business Development team.

  • Build the peptide narrative and the materials behind it: capability maps, benchmark summaries, validation packages and competitive comparisons that hold up under scrutiny from senior pharmaceutical scientists.

  • Set and enforce the standard for external claims, ensuring that what we say about validation, benchmarks and limitations is accurate, consistent across documents, and appropriately caveated.

  • Support business development through partner meetings, scientific exchanges, conferences and diligence processes, acting as the credible bridge between technical and commercial conversations.

  • Work with scientific and legal colleagues on intellectual property strategy, freedom-to-operate considerations and novelty positioning for designed molecules.

Essential experience and skills

  • Ten or more years in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, with substantial exposure to peptide, protein or biologics therapeutics in discovery, development, product strategy or business development.

  • Demonstrable command of what makes peptides difficult as drugs: proteolytic stability, oral and systemic exposure, receptor selectivity and off-target risk, immunogenicity, formulation and manufacturability, and the trade-offs between them.

  • A track record of shaping and closing commercial partnerships, licensing agreements or platform deals with pharmaceutical companies, or of owning commercial strategy for a platform sold into pharmaceutical R&D.

  • Proven ability to author target product profiles, competitive assessments and commercial cases that senior stakeholders act on.

  • Credibility in both directions: able to hold a substantive technical discussion with computational and experimental scientists, and a commercial discussion with a vice-president of platform technologies, without over-claiming in either.

  • Comfort operating with incomplete evidence, and the discipline to distinguish clearly between what is validated, what is promising and what is aspiration.

  • Excellent written English. A great deal of this role is producing documents that must be right.

  • Travel including to represent Basecamp Research at clients and industry meetings

Desirable experience

  • Experience in metabolic disease, immunology, anti-infectives or another therapeutic area with an active peptide pipeline.

  • Familiarity with macrocyclic peptides, peptidomimetics, non-canonical amino acids, conjugation strategies or oral delivery technologies.

  • Direct experience of AI-enabled drug discovery platforms, from either the platform side or the pharmaceutical side of a partnership.

  • A postgraduate degree in a life science, chemistry or a related business areas, or equivalent depth acquired in industry

Compensation and benefits

  • Collaborative Culture: You'll be surrounded by world-class engineers, scientists, and researchers who care deeply about their work and about each other. With offices in London and Boston, we've built a flexible, cross-functional environment where personal development and real ownership aren't just talking points.

  • High Growth: We truly believe in investing our people we make coaching available to team members during steep growth journeys and we have twice yearly promotion opportunities. People who are really successful here own it and go directly to solve problems at pace and we ensure reward increases with impact.

  • Comprehensive Benefits: We've built a benefits package people value. That means competitive salary, equity, and private healthcare with no medical history exclusions so strong that means most employees' family members opt into our plan over their own. title: Special Projects Lead - Category Expansion
description:
Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain?

The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise items with just a photo. Turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. We're backed by some of the world's best investors, including a16z, Y Combinator and HV Capital, alongside world-class angels who helped build Depop, Shopify, and Postmates.

Today, we serve thousands of resellers and retailers across the UK, Europe and the US. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

We're looking for people who want to build something that matters and move fast doing it. Sounds good? Keep reading.

About the Role

We're hiring a Special Projects Lead to take Fleek's new category bets from thesis to proven economics. Each is a new business line that could add £5M+ in GMV, opening a new supply category or a new sourcing geography for the marketplace. Here's what makes these bets unusually winnable. Fleek already owns the demand. Most of the live bets sell to buyers who transact on Fleek today, so they're a supply-first test rather than a two-sided cold start. Your job on a new bet is to find and onboard the supply, sell it into demand that already exists and read the economics fast.

Every bet runs through the same gates. If a bet misses its gates, you kill it with evidence and move to the next one. If it works and you're running it well, you don't have to hand it off. You scale into owning the category, with supply, acquisition and ops building out under you. Think of this seat as a venture builder inside Fleek.

One thing this is not. We're not building a sales team or a sales culture, and this is not an AE or account manager role with a new title. You'll work directly with the founders and our commercial lead, close to the centre of the company.

What You'll Do

  • Run bets through the gates: take each bet from market research to first suppliers to first GMV to a feasible-or-not call, with win metrics and kill metrics defined before you start.

  • Go where the supply is: get on planes. You'll visit suppliers, graders and rag houses in the markets your bets open up, because this trade is built face to face and the best stock never gets listed anywhere.

  • Sell supply into live demand: onboard brands, brokers, graders and wholesalers, then get Fleek's existing buyers transacting on the new inventory. The sell is fast, informal and relationship-led, over WhatsApp and Instagram as often as in a boardroom.

  • Make the kill calls: hold a clear view of unit economics and the competitive landscape on every bet. Double down or cut on evidence, not attachment.

  • Be the ops function, for now: work out importer-of-record structures, duties, freight cost and last mile for each new flow.

  • Ride the AI infrastructure: our acquisition team has spent months building the agentic outreach and enrichment engine. You'll plug your bets into it and extend it, rather than building from a blank page or adding headcount.

  • Learn the actual trade: how stock is graded, routed and priced across markets, and who's sitting on good inventory that nobody has approached. You'll get deep in it fast.

What You Bring

  • Zero-to-one is your natural habitat. You've built something from nothing as a founder, an early employee or the person who started a new line inside an existing company. You've operated without a playbook and you didn't wait for one.

  • Operator and commercial in one person. You build the machine and you carry the number. You're not pure strategy and you're not pure sales, and you're comfortable being measured on GMV within your first quarter.

  • AI fluency. You work with agents and automations daily and you'd rather build a workflow than repeat a task.

Strong signals on top of that:

  • An instinct for physical goods. You understand inventory, margins and trading relationships, or you've worked around fashion, resale or marketplaces.

  • Deals you structured yourself, at any size, that didn't exist before you wrote them.

  • Exposure to cross-border trade, logistics or supply chain operations.

Nice to Have

  • Direct experience in resale, surplus or secondary-market inventory

  • Experience launching a new market, geography or product line from scratch

  • Established networks in international sourcing markets

What You'll Get

  • Generous equity: being on Fleek means you'll own a part of it

  • Comprehensive healthcare coverage

  • A collaborative team in a lovely office in the heart of East London

  • Access to founders. We're a small team and they're heavily involved (and good fun!)

  • Exclusive employee discounts to buy on Fleek

  • Access to borrow any item from our collection of vintage and reworks in the office

  • A disproportionate level of responsibility and the opportunity to drive massive impact

How We Work

Fleek is an in-office company. We're based at Commercial Street, E1 (Liverpool Street / Aldgate East). We operate a fully in-person culture at our office in Shoreditch, with trust-based flexibility. We hire adults and trust them to perform.

The Practicalities

  • Location: London HQ, Commercial Street, E1 (Liverpool Street / Aldgate East)

  • Stage: Post-Series B, hyper-growth

  • Team: 200 across three geographies

  • Culture: High ownership, non-hierarchical, fast-moving. Founder-led with strong opinions loosely held.

Our Values

Five values shape how we work at Fleek:

  • Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself: Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach.

  • Absolute Ownership: The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done.

  • Curiosity Leads the Way: Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate.

  • Talk to the Customer: Deeply understand their challenges, motivations, and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre.

  • Embrace Diversity: A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter.

Ready to build the infrastructure for the world's fastest-growing fashion economy? If you want to work on genuinely hard problems, with a world-class team, at a company that's tripling annually, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Talent Director
description:
About OLIX

AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The industry is still leaning on a ten-year-old hardware blueprint that has reached its limit. A new paradigm that is faster and more efficient will be the biggest economic opportunity of the next century and create the most important company of the next decade. The OLIX Decode Accelerator 1 (DX-1) is the first accelerator architected specifically for decode. Rack-scale co-design of logic, data movement, packaging, optics and interconnect enables a step change in system level performance.

 

The Role

The Talent Director owns how OLIX finds, wins and hires the people who will build it. You will take a talent function built for around 200 people and make it one that carries us confidently to 1,000, across London, Bristol, Austin, San Francisco and Toronto, without lowering the bar on a single hire.

This is a hands on leadership role. You will personally lead our most senior and executive searches, and close people who are not looking. Many of the people we need exist in pools of a few dozen worldwide: III-V device engineers, advanced packaging architects, optical interconnect specialists, AI software engineers, silicon leaders who have taken a chip to production. Hiring them is a precision problem, not a volume one. You will build a team of recruiters as sharp as the engineers they hire, and set an AI strategy for recruiting that changes how we decide, not just how fast we work. The best argument wins here, and we expect you to make it, welcome challenges to it, and change your mind when the evidence says so.

 

Responsibilities

  • Build and scale the talent function from around 200 to 1,000 people: org design, hiring, priorities and operating rhythm, in place before the headcount arrives

  • Lead senior and executive searches directly, including the hires that signal the calibre of people joining OLIX

  • Attract, hire and develop top Recruiters and Sourcers, and hold them to the same bar as our engineers

  • Own the hiring bar: what great looks like for each role family, and how consistently every interviewer applies it

  • Build the playbook for extremely scarce talent: mapping the market, building relationships early, and closing passive candidates

  • Set OLIX's AI strategy for recruiting, deciding where AI improves our judgement and where people need to stay in the loop

  • Own hiring systems, data and metrics, and partner with the exec team on workforce planning, including saying when a plan is not hireable as written

  • Build OLIX's talent brand so the best people in photonics, silicon and AI know who we are

 

Skills & Experience

  • Has built and led a talent function through hyper-growth, from a few hundred people toward 1,000 or beyond, while keeping quality high. This is non-negotiable

  • Has attracted and developed top recruiters, and can name the people who would come with you

  • Has worked where talent density is top 1% (a frontier AI lab, a leading semiconductor or hardware company, or an elite deep tech scale-up) and knows what that bar looks and feels like

  • Has personally led senior and executive searches into niche, extremely limited talent pools

  • A clear point of view on AI in recruiting that goes beyond efficiency, with evidence of putting it into practice

  • Either versed in deep tech already, or curious enough to go deep on product and technology and hold your own with engineers

  • Influences through evidence and clear reasoning, not title, and is comfortable disagreeing directly in a founder-led environment

 

Nice to Have

  • Talent leadership at an AI lab, AI hardware company or semiconductor business

  • Direct experience hiring in photonics, optoelectronics, advanced packaging, silicon or AI software

  • Experience hiring across the UK and US and running a multi-site function

 

Compensation & Equity

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience, skills, and location

  • Equity & Ownership: Meaningful stock options. You’re not just joining the mission; you’re owning a piece of it

  • Proximity Bonus: We value your time. To minimise your commute and maximise your life, we offer an annual Living-Local Bonus if your residence is within 20 minutes of the office

  • Retirement Benefits: Employer-contributed retirement plans to help you build long-term financial security

Due to U.S. export control regulations, candidates’ eligibility to work at OLIX depends on their most recent citizenship or permanent residency status. We are generally unable to consider applicants whose most recent citizenship or permanent residence is in certain restricted countries (currently including Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Russia, Belarus, China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Venezuela). Applicants who have subsequently obtained citizenship or permanent residency in another country not subject to these restrictions may still be eligible.

About us

Motorway is the first and largest car-selling marketplace in the UK, connecting private sellers directly with over 8,000 verified dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve market leading prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want to grow their businesses profitably.

Founded in 2017, Motorway's technology-led approach has transformed the car-selling experience. We now facilitate hundreds of thousands of car sales each year, with 2,500 cars in our daily auction. We employ 400+ people across the UK. Valued at over $1bn and backed by leading global technology investors, including Index and Iconiq. Motorway is now entering a critical phase focused on scale, growth and profitability. This is a rare opportunity to join a high-growth scale-up at a pivotal moment and help shape the services that sit around every car sold on Motorway.

About the job

As Commercial Director of Dealer Solutions, you will own what happens after Motorway's daily auction closes: inspecting and transporting the car, making sure everyone gets paid, and helping dealers fund the stock they buy. Transport, Payments and Dealer Finance are central to Motorway's next phase of growth. They shape how dealers experience Motorway, how much of each transaction we serve, and how we grow revenue beyond the core marketplace. There is significant work to do across all three, with scope to add new dealer solutions over time.

This is a senior commercial leadership role. You will set the strategy, own the P&L for these services and lead experienced specialist teams, bringing commercial clarity, pace and ambition. You will be as comfortable framing an investment case for the executive team as you are working through an operational problem with your team.

You will work closely with Sales, Marketing, Operations, Product and Engineering, as well as a network of external partners that support the delivery of Dealer Solutions. Our dealer base and partnerships are growing, and our Dealer Solutions need to scale ahead of that demand while staying simple and reliable for dealers and sellers.

The Commercial Director reports directly to the Chief Operating Officer, James Wilson, and is part of Motorway's senior leadership team.

Responsibilities

This role is responsible for turning Motorway's Dealer Solutions into a scaled, profitable part of the business. You will set clear priorities, make explicit trade-offs and move between strategy and detail as the situation needs.

Strategy & Commercial Leadership

  • Set the vision, strategy and goals for Transport, Payments and Dealer Finance, with clear priorities across short and long-term horizons

  • Own the P&L for Dealer Solutions, making explicit trade-offs between growth, margin and customer experience

  • Build and present investment cases to the executive team and contribute to Motorway's wider strategy

Transport & Fulfilment

  • Lead the strategy and performance of Motorway's vehicle transport proposition, making sure capacity keeps pace with demand

  • Build and manage a scalable network of logistics partners, with strong commercial terms and clear performance management

  • Improve reliability, speed and cost so dealers and sellers get a fast, predictable experience

Payments

  • Own the commercial performance of Motorway's dealer payment products, driving adoption and a smooth, secure payment experience

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to launch and scale improvements, using phased rollouts and clear success measures

Dealer Finance

  • Shape and grow Motorway's dealer finance proposition, including stock funding, working with internal teams and external partners

  • Develop the commercial model, partnerships and go-to-market approach needed to scale it

Performance & Operating Rhythm

  • Set clear metrics for each service and a regular operating cadence, using data to find root causes and drive improvement

  • Make sure operations can absorb growth and seasonal peaks without the customer experience suffering

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Lead and develop experienced specialist teams, adding commercial framing and clear priorities while giving experts room to lead

  • Build strong working relationships with Sales, Marketing, Operations, Product and Engineering teams

  • Manage key partners and suppliers, getting full value from existing relationships and identifying and onboarding new partners as required

  • Role-model Motorway's values as part of the senior leadership team

Requirements

This role requires a senior commercial leader who combines strategic thinking with operational delivery. You should be comfortable in a fast-moving environment, able to set direction at an executive level and get into the detail with your team when it matters.

  • Strategy: Ability to set and communicate a clear commercial strategy, translating growth plans and constraints into a prioritised roadmap over multiple horizons

  • Commercial: Proven experience owning a P&L or major commercial line in a high-growth, technology-led business, ideally a marketplace.

  • Situational leadership: Experience leading senior specialists, knowing when to step into the detail and when to step back

  • Judgement: A pragmatic, outcome-driven mindset with strong ownership and high business judgement

  • Composure: Calm and decisive when operations are under pressure, and focused on fixing root causes afterwards

  • Communication: Explains complex commercial and operational trade-offs clearly, adjusting the message for audiences from the executive team to front-line colleagues

Il possède également des compétences en développement de capteurs et d’instrumentation.

Les technologies de captage et stockage du CO2 sont des technologies clés pour la décarbonation du secteur industriel. Les stockages offshores ont déjà démontré leur faisabilité, mais les stockages onshores semblent nécessaires pour augmenter les capacités de stockage tout en réduisant le transport de CO2. Or, la proximité de ces sites avec les populations rend leurs déploiements incertains et soulève des questions relatives à l’acceptabilité sociale.

La surveillance à long terme des sites de stockage de CO2, exigée par la directive européenne CCS, constitue une opportunité pour renforcer la transparence et l’acceptation locale du stockage en engageant les parties prenantes dans l’acquisition et l’interprétation des données. Cependant, les systèmes actuels de surveillance ne permettent pas à la fois de réaliser des mesures in-situ, simulations numériques et visualisation interactive pour une approche du suivi intégrée des sites de stockage. Le projet CO2MET vise à développer et faire progresser des unités ou éléments clés pour préparer un futur système intégré de surveillance numérique à long terme améliorant la fiabilité et l’acceptabilité du stockage géologique de CO2.

Pour atteindre ces objectifs, le consortium CO2MET a été constitué et est composé de l'IFPEN, du BRGM, de Mines Saint-Etienne et de Cerema.

La surveillance à long terme nécessite des outils fiables et performants, notamment dans le domaine des capteurs environnementaux, ce qui soulève la question de la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives pour traiter le signal, ainsi que celle de l'influence des variations à long terme des paramètres externes sur la réponse des capteurs (et de l'impact du changement climatique). Étant donné que les signaux de concentration en CO₂ peuvent, à eux seuls, ne pas être suffisamment discriminants (les concentrations biologiques dans les sols pouvant dépasser 10 % vol.), compte tenu de leurs origines diverses (sources profondes, provenant du stockage ou de l’interaction gaz-roche ; processus de respiration ; oxydation du méthane), la prévention des faux positifs dans la surveillance des sites de stockage doit s'appuyer sur des capteurs de CO₂ (NDIR ou photoacoustiques) et sur d'autres capteurs (par exemple, un capteur chimique d'O₂), ainsi que sur des capteurs environnementaux (humidité, pression, température) afin de permettre une attribution correcte de la source de CO2.

Parmi les missions qui lui seront attribuées, le doctorant devra :

· Sélectionner des capteurs existants répondants aux spécifications afin de mettre au point une plateforme de détection 

· Etudier, en conditions de laboratoire, la sélectivité des capteurs vis-à-vis des espèces gazeuses interférentes, à l’aide d’une analyse multivariée

· Définir des algorithmes de prédiction tenant compte de la reproductibilité, de la dérive, de la linéarité et de la variabilité dans des mélanges gazeux complexes et des conditions environnementales variables (température, pression et humidité relative)

· Etudier l'influence du vieillissement des capteurs sur leur réponse et sur les prévisions établies, afin de proposer un algorithme de compensation

·  Enfin, mener des études de cas concrets sur le site de Sainte-Marguerite (Puy-de-Dôme), avec des niveaux d'émissions de CO₂ variables, afin de tester et de valider les plateformes de capteurs développées.

Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer enseignement, recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Vous êtes titulaire d’un :

· Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent

Et idéalement :

· Titulaire d’un de master 2 dans les domaines suivants : Mesure / Instrumentation / Métrologie ; Acquisition, traitement et analyse de la donnée

· Avec une expérience de stage ou professionnelle dans la recherche (goût prononcé pour la partie expérimentale)

title: Post-doctorant.e : "Elaboration et caractérisation de matériaux inorganiques à partir d’une mine urbaine" - CDD 18 mois
description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !

Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant que post-doctorant.e, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affectées au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS). Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal, « en décortiquant » la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils d’élaboration et de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nous déployons le concept de «Material by design» : concevoir au mieux les matériaux de demain répondant aux enjeux de transition.

Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

 

Ce post-doctorat s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet VARIMA (VAlorisation des Résidus d’Incinération en Matériaux Avancés) du dispositif Partenariats d'innovation Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes - volet Preuves de Concept. L’incinération des déchets ménagers produit, en plus de l'énergie, des résidus contenant des métaux et des minéraux. Des entreprises récupèrent et recyclent les différents métaux. Cependant, des milliers de tonnes de poussières minérales sont générées et sont généralement envoyées en décharge faute de solution de valorisation.

Ce post-doctorat, d’une durée de 18 mois vise à étudier la valorisation des poussières d’incinération par deux voies d’élaboration : voie géopolymères et voie métallurgie des poudres. Les matériaux obtenus seront ensuite caractérisés au niveau microstructural mais aussi au niveau des propriétés d’usage (propriétés mécanique et thermique ainsi que la tenue à la lixiviation). Le post-doctorant.e contribuera durant la deuxième année de ce CDD à une étude d’impact relative au procédés développés.

· Vous faites preuve d'une grande autonomie dans la conduite de vos travaux expérimentaux tout en montrant une rigueur scientifique exemplaire

· Vous rendez compte des résultats à vos encadrants et à l’entreprise partenaire du projet

· Vous participez aux réunions de suivi de projet et à la rédaction des livrables

Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir.

🚀 Missions

Ø  Caractérisation physico-chimique et bifurcation des flux de poussières.

  • Mise en œuvre des outils de la plateforme (DRX, FRX, ICP-MS, ATG/DSC, granulométrie laser, etc.

  • Validation et application du protocole de bifurcation technique pour orienter chaque lot vers la voie optimale.

Ø  Développement et optimisation des matrices liantes.

Pilotage des formulations expérimentales en laboratoire pour les deux voies de valorisation afin de lever les verrous scientifiques majeurs (gestion du soufre et des inhibiteurs de prise comme le ZnO).

  • Conception et optimisation des formulations de géopolymères.

  • Optimisation des programmes de frittage des céramiques denses.

Ø  Évaluation de la durabilité, de la conformité réglementaire et lixiviation.

Assurer la qualification technique et environnementale des matériaux développés pour garantir leur transférabilité vers le marché de la construction.

  • Réaliser les tests de performance mécanique et de durabilité (stabilité face à l'expansion sulfatique).

  • Conduire les tests de lixiviation normalisés (NF EN 12457-2) pour démontrer la conformité réglementaire vis-à-vis des seuils de stockage (ISDI) et participer à la rédaction technique de la proposition d’une fiche matière GAMAA et d’un dossier technique d’application.

Ø  Analyse de Cycle de Vie et de soutenabilité.

  • Collecte des données d'inventaire

  • Participation à la modélisation pour quantifier les bénéfices (réduction du CO2) et à l’évaluation des dimensions socio-économiques locales.

Ø  Gestion de projet, animation du partenariat et valorisation scientifique.

Assurer le suivi opérationnel quotidien du projet VARIMA et la diffusion des connaissances au sein de l'écosystème concerné.

  • Participation à l’encadrement des stagiaires associés aux travaux et maintien d’un lien technique étroit avec le partenaire industriel pour le partage des résultats.

  • Rédaction des rapports d'avancement du projet.

  • Valorisation des résultats à travers la rédaction d'articles scientifiques internationaux à comité de lecture, participation à des congrès, et contribution à la détection d'opportunités de brevets.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Vous êtes titulaire d’un :

  • Doctorat (PhD) ou équivalent en Chimie des matériaux, Sciences et Génie des matériaux ou des procédés, Génie civil.

Et idéalement :

  • Avec une expérience sur l’élaboration et la caractérisation de matériaux inorganiques.

  • Une appétence pour les travaux expérimentaux.

  • Une maîtrise de l’anglais (niveau C1) et, idéalement, une expérience internationale

Vos atouts supplémentaires :

  • Capacité à travailler en équipe

  • Capacité à dialoguer avec des interlocuteurs académiques et industriels

Sa stratégie 2023-2027 vise à accompagner les transitions écologique, numérique et générationnelle, tout en contribuant à la souveraineté nationale et européenne en microélectronique et numérique.

Le campus Aix-Marseille-Provence, situé à Gardanne, regroupe le Centre Microélectronique de Provence (CMP), des formations d’ingénieurs et de masters, un incubateur technologique et des plateformes de prototypage. Il accueille environ 400 étudiants et 200 personnels de Mines Saint-Étienne et d’entreprises partenaires.

Le CMP dispose d’une salle blanche de 700 m², équipée d’une centaine d’équipements scientifiques répartis en zones de classes 100, 1 000 et 10 000. Cette plateforme est utilisée par les équipes de recherche, les membres académiques et industriels de l’association Micro-PackS, ainsi que pour les formations initiales et continues.

Ses activités couvrent notamment les procédés de couches minces, la photolithographie, la chimie, la caractérisation physique et électrique des matériaux et dispositifs, le micropackaging, l’électronique imprimée et la préparation d’échantillons.

La formation se concentrera sur la réalisation de transistor NMOS.

Le Centre de Microélectronique de Provence recrute un ingénieur pour mettre en place et dispenser ces formations, gérer les opérations nécessaires au bon déroulement de celles-ci.
