Als OT Network Engineer sorgst du dafür, dass die Netzwerke und Infrastruktur unserer Batteriespeicheranlagen zuverlässig und sicher funktionieren. Gemeinsam mit unserem OT-Team betreibst du die technische Infrastruktur, sicherst die Kommunikation zwischen den Systemen und unterstützt die Anbindung neuer Anlagen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du betreibst und wartest unsere OT-nahen Infrastrukturkomponenten – von Netzwerken und Servern bis zu Endgeräten und Backup-Systemen.
  • Beim Aufbau und der Weiterentwicklung unserer OT-Netzwerke gestaltest du die Architektur, setzt Netzwerksegmentierung und DMZ-Konzepte um und sorgst für sichere Schnittstellen zwischen IT und OT.
  • Firewalls und Remote-Access-Lösungen administrierst du so, dass Fernzugriffe kontrolliert erfolgen und die Sicherheitsgrenzen unserer Systeme eingehalten werden.
  • Die sichere Anbindung von Edge- und IoT-Komponenten sowie das Endpoint Management im OT-Umfeld liegen ebenfalls in deinem Aufgabenbereich.
  • Gemeinsam mit unserem Cyber-Security-Team setzt du technische Standards, Systemhärtungen und ein abgestimmtes Patch-Management um.
  • Bei Störungen in Netzwerk, SCADA oder Energiemanagementsystemen analysierst du die Ursachen und koordinierst die Behebung in enger Abstimmung mit dem Digital OT Lead und dem OT-Team.
  • Neue Standorte und Anlagen begleitest du beim Infrastruktur-Rollout und unterstützt ihre Einbindung in unsere bestehende OT-Landschaft.
  • Durch eine nachvollziehbare Dokumentation und einheitliche Konfigurationen schaffst du die Grundlage für einen verlässlichen Betrieb und die weitere Standardisierung unserer Infrastruktur.
  • Mit unseren Managed-Services-Partnern und dem Cyber-Security-Team arbeitest du bei Monitoring und Incident Response eng zusammen.

Dein Profil

  • Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung oder ein Studium im IT-/OT-Umfeld bildet die Grundlage deiner Qualifikation.
  • Im Betrieb von Netzwerk-, Server- und OT-Infrastruktur hast du bereits mehrjährige praktische Erfahrung gesammelt.
  • OT-Netzwerke, Netzwerksegmentierung und die sichere Integration von IT und OT gehören zu deinen fachlichen Stärken.
  • Mit der Administration von Firewalls und Remote-Access-Lösungen bist du vertraut.
  • Kenntnisse im Endpoint Management mit Microsoft Intune sowie im Microsoft-365-Umfeld sind von Vorteil.
  • Technische Probleme gehst du strukturiert und lösungsorientiert an; dabei behältst du die Verfügbarkeit und Sicherheit der Systeme im Blick.
  • Für Rollouts und technische Einsätze bringst du die Bereitschaft mit, zu unseren Anlagenstandorten zu reisen.
  • Für die enge Zusammenarbeit mit unserem Team bist du regelmäßig für zwei bis drei Tage vor Ort in unserem Büro in Aschheim bei München.
  • Auf Deutsch(mindestens C2) und Englisch kannst du dich im Arbeitsalltag und zu technischen Themen gut verständigen.

Warum wir?

  • Verantwortung im Anlagenbetrieb: Deine Arbeit trägt unmittelbar zur sicheren Kommunikation und zuverlässigen Verfügbarkeit unserer Batteriespeicher bei.
  • Technischer Gestaltungsspielraum: Du entwickelst unsere OT-Infrastruktur weiter und bringst eigene Lösungen für Standards, Sicherheit und Betrieb ein.

title: Signal Processing & Data Engineer
description:
Who We Are

Limatica measures what batteries whisper. We turn the tiny voltage noise of battery cells into a quality verdict, far faster than conventional tests, and help cell manufacturers cut scrap.

We are a team of twelve in Chemnitz and Munich, spanning data, ML, HPC, hardware and industrialization. Early adopters across Europe and Asia already use our technology. In 2026 we move from pilots to production lines, and our data grows faster than our team.

What You'll Do

Our measurement stations produce several hundred GB of high-resolution voltage data per hour. You own the step from raw signal to reliable answer.

  • Work with novel cell noise data: Derive features from raw time series that make physical sense that hold up in production
  • Build for streaming: Design feature computations that work in streaming mode, at a throughput of up to 10,000 measurements per hour.
  • Make throughput a design decision: Build modular, parameterizable nodes for our distributed processing pipeline and help bring them into our Rust-based production environment.
  • Ship modules, not scripts: Automate evaluations end to end, from raw data to reports for our engineering team and our customers.
  • Own customer projects technically: Assess requirements, communicate interim results and findings, and turn feedback into improvements.

What You Bring

  • Measurement experience: A degree in electrical engineering (or comparable) and 3+ years with real-world measurement data. Sampling, noise, filtering and artifacts you know from practice, not just lectures.
  • Physical intuition: You can explain why a feature makes sense, and you prefer a simple, well-understood method over a model nobody can explain.
  • Data at scale: You think in throughput: data formats, intermediate results, distributed and cached processing.
  • Clean engineering: Python, Git, tests and CI/CD as a matter of course. No Rust expertise needed, but the will to learn it.
  • Customer confidence: Fluent German and English, written and spoken. You explain results clearly to engineers and managers alike.

Why Limatica

  • Real ownership: Your own part of the pipeline and your first customer project within months. As we grow, this role can grow into technical lead.
  • Learn what few get to learn: Electrochemistry, Rust in production and data engineering at scale, with real cells and international manufacturers.
  • Share the upside: Salary package including virtual stock options.
  • Invest in yourself: Additional holiday for personal learning
  • Flexibility & wellbeing: Flexible hours, hybrid work, further benefits via Guud Card and free beverages

What it's like here: You get a lot of trust and a lot of room to shape things. We look for people who stay with a problem until it's solved and who enjoy the moments when a customer launch needs the whole team. Those are the moments where people here grow fastest. This role is intentionally a towards-senior position. You will take on increasing responsibility for pipeline modules and customer projects. Those who help shape the architecture and lead projects independently grow into a senior role with us.

Ready to find the signal in the noise? Let's build the future of battery diagnostics together. ⚡

About Flow

Flow Engineering is an AI-native requirements platform for modern engineering organizations, enabling hardware teams to collaborate with AI agents to design, validate, and evolve complex systems with speed and rigor.

About the role

Flow is seeking software engineers to build AI-powered capabilities that help teams author, review, and manage requirements more effectively. You will work on agentic systems engineer and agentic domain engineer workflows—bringing AI into the center of how teams reason about their systems.​

This role sits at the intersection of AI, product, and full-stack engineering: you will take ideas from prototype all the way to stable, observable features in production.​

What you’ll do

  • Design and ship AI-powered features such as assisted requirement drafting, consistency checks, impact analysis, and intelligent suggestions for systems and domain engineers.

  • Build agentic workflows that help “agentic systems engineers” and “agentic domain engineers” explore designs, simulate changes, and validate requirements.​

  • Evaluate and integrate language models and related tooling, optimizing for reliability, latency, cost, and debuggability in production.

  • Build and maintain the surrounding infrastructure: data pipelines, evaluation harnesses, prompt and model management, observability, and safety/guardrails.

  • Work across the stack—from backend integrations and APIs to simple UI hooks—to deliver complete AI features, not just model endpoints.

  • Partner with product and customers to identify high-value workflows, run experiments, and iterate quickly based on usage.

About you

  • 5+ years developing production software, including designing, testing, and operating services at scale in a cloud environment.

  • Hands-on experience with modern LLM providers and tooling (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, vector stores, RAG patterns).

description:
At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

Research questions you could initially work on

  • Learning dynamics from operational data. How can we identify useful models of a plant from noisy, partially observed data collected during closed-loop control?

  • Optimising under uncertainty. How can Bayesian optimisation improve plant performance when experiments are expensive, samples are noisy, and operating constraints must be respected?

  • Learning while controlling. How can we use dual control and active learning to choose actions that improve performance while gathering information about uncertain dynamics?

  • Learning across plants. Which parts of a model or control strategy can transfer between plants, and how can we adapt them efficiently to a new site?

These are meant as examples rather than an exhaustive list. We’re looking for someone who can bring depth to a relevant area, identify promising connections, and help us decide which problems to tackle next.

Your main responsibilities

As a Research Scientist, you’ll:

  • Help shape our research and development agenda, turning challenges from live plants into well-defined research problems.

  • Develop and implement methods for modelling, identification, optimisation and control of complex physical systems.

  • Design rigorous experiments, establish strong baselines and understand when and why a method works.

  • Work with process engineers to incorporate plant physics, operating knowledge and constraints into models and algorithms.

  • Work with machine learning and deployment engineers to evaluate promising methods and bring them into production.

  • Follow deployed performance, investigate failures, and use what you learn to guide further research.

  • Communicate your findings clearly and contribute to the team’s scientific understanding.

What a great fit looks like

  • A PhD in control, machine learning, applied mathematics, engineering, physics or a related field, or equivalent research experience.

  • A strong research background in one or more of control theory, data-driven control, system identification, Bayesian optimisation, probabilistic modelling, physics-informed machine learning, imitation learning or model-based reinforcement learning.

  • Evidence that you can formulate a research question, develop a method and evaluate it carefully, through publications, open-source work or applied research.

  • Strong Python skills and experience implementing machine learning models using tools such as Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch.

  • An interest in working closely with engineers and taking responsibility for how your methods perform in practice.

  • Practical experience deploying machine learning and control algorithms.

  • A strong interest in climate mitigation.

You don’t need to know about cement. You do need to get excited about the physics, willing to learn from operators and process engineers, and keen to understand why a plant behaves the way it does.

We don’t expect you to tick every box. If you bring depth in a relevant area and these problems excite you, we’d like to hear from you.

In return for your hard work, we’ll give you

📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside.

🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team.

🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge

🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one.

Our Operating Principles

↗️ Go Gig or Go Home: High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires.

🏭 Concrete Honesty: Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture.

🦾 Autonomous Ownership: High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it.

😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun: Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still limited. We want to enjoy the ride. To see these in full, go to Gigaton’s Operating Principles Notion page.

description:
Mission

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

Every Neko clinic brings together members, advanced medical equipment, a clinical team and, before opening, an active construction site. The Global Health & Safety Lead ensures that all of this is safe and legally compliant in every country where we operate, and that safety is embedded in how we select, build, open and run our clinics.

This is a build role. With hundreds of new locations planned across global markets, you will establish the standards, checks and processes that make every opening safe and legally compliant, and build the global standards and operating systems that oversee day-to-day health and safety, adapted to each market’s legislation and needs.

You will own Neko’s day-to-day health and safety management so that our members and staff are in a safe environment, select and implement the systems to run it at scale, and put in place the training, audits and people needed to sustain high standards as we grow.



What You’ll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

Clinic Openings

  • A repeatable opening process, with the health and safety standards, checks and sign-offs every new clinic must pass before it opens, built to work across hundreds of locations in different markets.

  • Map the health and safety legal requirements in each Neko market and establish global standards with local additions where required.

  • Health and safety due diligence for every new site and new market, with a clear view of the residual market risks.

  • Safety integrated into clinic design and construction, in partnership with the real estate and construction teams: contractor requirements and pre-qualification, site audits, and complete safety briefings at handover.

  • Emergency and evacuation plans agreed with the Global Security Lead.

Risk Management and Infrastructure

  • A global health and safety management system, adapted locally for each market, that oversees day-to-day safety across every clinic and office.

  • Risk assessments for every clinic, office and build site, covering fire safety, first aid, manual handling and the use of medical equipment.

  • Controls for clinic-specific hazards, including clinical waste and the safe operation of medical equipment, aligned with local regulation and quality management systems.

  • A risk-based audit programme and a set of performance measures reported regularly to the COO.

Day to Day Operations

  • Ownership of Neko’s day-to-day health and safety management, so our members and staff are in a safe environment in every clinic.

  • Routine maintenance and compliance checks that control building risks including fire, water hygiene, electrical safety and lifts, in collaboration with Facilities.

  • Robust reporting, investigation and corrective action processes for incidents and near misses, including statutory reporting to regulators.

  • Induction and ongoing training for clinic teams, including fire wardens and first aiders who can lead effectively in an emergency.

Tech Forward

  • Selection and implementation of the systems used to manage health and safety globally.



Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in health and safety, including responsibility across more than one country.

  • A recognised professional qualification, such as the NEBOSH Diploma, Chartered membership of IOSH (CMIOSH) or equivalent.

  • Experience building or running a health and safety management system, ideally certified to ISO 45001.

  • Hands-on experience of construction or fit-out safety for new commercial sites.

  • A track record of leading incident investigations and driving corrective actions through completion.

  • Ability to influence operations, construction, and senior leadership teams without direct authority.

  • Ability to travel regularly between markets.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background in multi-site, public-facing businesses such as healthcare, fitness, wellness, co-working, tech, retail or hospitality.

  • Experience in a regulated environment involving medical equipment or a quality management system.

  • Experience managing contractor safety on new builds.

  • ISO 45001 lead auditor training or equivalent.

  • Knowledge of health and safety regulations in Neko’s global markets.

  • Experience building a health and safety function as a business scales from a few sites to many.

  • Experience selecting and implementing systems to manage health and safety at scale

description:

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are seeking a TPRM Senior Associate with 4+ years of relevant experience to serve as a key operational member of the London TPRM team. This role is the primary operational bridge between the London leadership, the Offshore TPRM Operations Team, and critical onshore functions (Procurement, Business Owners, Risk SMEs). The Senior Associate is responsible for coordinating the execution workflow, managing the quality assurance of medium-risk third parties, and driving the logistics for the critical Supplier Performance Review process.

Responsibilities

This role is centred on execution quality, operational leadership, and cross-functional coordination within the London TPRM team structure:

  • Offshore Operations Liaison & Quality Control:

    • Act as the primary daily point of contact and operational supervisor for the Offshore TPRM Operations Team, ensuring the accurate and timely execution of all third-party risk assessments and due diligence activities.

    • Lead the Quality Control (QC) process for all assessments delivered by the offshore team, ensuring outputs are consistent, align with established methodologies, and are fully audit-ready.

    • Monitor the operational performance of the offshore team against defined Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

    • Be ready to conduct third-party assessments to support the team, where required.

  • Stakeholder Coordination & Assessment Oversight:

    • Coordinate Assessment Initiation by working closely with Procurement and Business Owners to ensure third-party risk assessments are initiated at the correct phase of the third-party lifecycle.

    • Manage the crucial triage and review process by coordinating with Internal Risk SMEs (e.g., InfoSec, Data Privacy, BCP) to ensure high-risk assessments receive appropriate specialized review and sign-off prior to completion.

    • Serve as the operational point of contact for these onshore internal risk teams regarding third-party-specific findings and remediation requirements.

  • Supplier Performance Monitoring & Reporting:

    • Oversee the governance and standardization of ongoing supplier performance monitoring activities executed by the offshore team.

    • Coordinate with Business Owners and Procurement to collect and review performance data (e.g., SLA adherence, operational metrics) and integrate significant performance failures or deficiencies into the overall third-party risk profile.

    • Ensure any critical performance issues are appropriately flagged for risk review and incorporated into continuous monitoring plans.

  • Escalation and Remediation Management:

    • Serve as the primary escalation point for all high-risk findings, process bottlenecks, and third-party non-compliance issues reported by the Offshore TPRM Operations Team.

    • Work with Business Owners and Procurement to define, drive, and track third-party remediation plans, ensuring mitigation steps are completed within established timelines.

  • 2nd Line of Defense Liaison & Governance Support:

    • Act as the key operational liaison for the 2nd Line of Defense (Risk Oversight), compiling and delivering required operational data, metrics, and commentary on the coverage and control effectiveness of the TPRM program.

    • Support the TPRM team in the preparation of reports and presentations on TPRM metrics, trends, and program effectiveness for leadership and Risk Committees.

  • Program & Tool Support:

    • Assist the TPRM team in the implementation, configuration, and ongoing maintenance of the TPRM system/tool, ensuring data integrity across the platform.

Qualifications

  • Experience: 4+ years of dedicated experience in Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM), risk management, compliance, or a related operational control function.

  • Consulting Background: Prior experience working at a Big 4 (e.g., Deloitte, EY, PwC, KPMG) or a similar major consulting firm is highly desirable.

  • Operational Control: Proven experience acting as a process gatekeeper or reviewer, with specific experience in Quality Assurance (QA) for risk or compliance deliverables.

  • Stakeholder Management: Strong organizational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to manage expectations and articulate complex operational risks clearly.

  • TPRM/GRC Knowledge: Solid understanding of TPRM principles, risk domains (InfoSec, BCP, ABAC, etc.), and prior experience supporting the administration or maintenance of a GRC/TPRM platform is highly desirable.

title: Senior eCommerce Content Strategist
description:
About Us
Since 2003, Luzern eCommerce has been helping leading global brands grow their online business. We partner with brands including Panasonic, Reebok, Stokke, KIKO, Next, Twining's, Canon, Bondi Sands and Philips, helping them accelerate growth and deliver exceptional customer experiences across major marketplaces including Amazon and Zalando, branded webstores and social platforms.

Backed by significant investment, Luzern is an international, technology-led eCommerce business with anambitious growth strategy. Our AI-enabled Channel Optimizer platform, combined with our eCommerce expertise, helps brands manage and grow their presence across increasingly complex digital channels.
As we continue to grow and evolve, we are looking for talented people who enjoy working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and want to play an active role in the next stage of Luzern's development.

The Senior eCommerce Content Strategist owns content strategy and execution across Amazon and the wider commerce ecosystem for Luzern's enterprise brand clients. Amazon is the primary focus — listings, A+/Premium A+ Content, Brand Store and related content — but the role is deliberately platform-agnostic in outlook, extending strategy and content guidance to other marketplaces, retailer sites (e.g. Tesco, Zalando,Otto) and D2C.

The role is audit-led: content strategy is built from a structured read of customer and platform signals — reviews, search terms, AI-generated summaries, and the queries customers put to AI assistants and platform agents — combined with a quality assessment of current content (using a framework such as IDQ or equivalent) against Best-in-Class competitors and audience requirements. Strategy, messaging and content requirements follow from that evidence base, rather than from assumption.

A defining part of the role is thinking beyond traditional platform search: strategies must consider how content needs to be structured and prepared to be discovered and surfaced by generative AI assistants (e.g ChatGPT) and in-platform shopping agents (e.g. Amazon's Rufus), alongside conventional marketplace and retailer search algorithms.

The role sits as the senior content specialist within a small delivery pod, working alongside an SEO Executive and Designers. It carries direct client-facing responsibility: estimating, briefing, managing feedback and contributing to proposals and is responsible for reviewing the pod's output before it reaches the client. It does not carry resourcing, project management or formal line management responsibility.

Tasks

What You’ll Be Doing

Content Audits & Quality Assessment
● Signal analysis: analyse customer reviews, search terms, AI-generated summaries, and the queries customers and AI agents put to platforms (e.g. Rufus prompts), to understand what content needs to do and where current content falls short.
● Quality benchmarking — review current platform content and score it against a content quality framework (e.g. IDQ or equivalent), benchmarking against Best-in-Class competitors and audience requirements.
● Findings to action — translate audit findings into a clear, prioritised view of content requirements that feeds directly into strategy.

Content Strategy Development
● Amazon content ownership- develop and own content strategy and execution for listings, A+/Premium A+ Content, Brand Store and related Amazon content, as the role's primary focus.
● Cross-platform extension — extend strategy and content recommendations to other marketplaces,retailer sites (e.g. Tesco, Zalando, Otto) and D2C storefronts, adapting to each platform's content rules, algorithm and customer behaviour.
● Strategic framework - from audit findings, develop comms objectives, key messages and a messaging hierarchy for each client or category.
● Content requirements - define the content requirements, imagery and copy needed to deliverthe strategy, and the frameworks/guidelines the team and client can act on.
● Wireframes & mock-ups - develop A+ and Brand Store wireframes and mock-ups in collaborationwith the Designer, turning strategy into an executable creative direction.

AI & Agentic Discoverability
● AI-ready content — build content strategies that account for how product and brand content is read, ranked and surfaced by generative AI assistants (e.g. ChatGPT) and in-platform shopping agents (e.g Rufus), alongside traditional search.
● Point of view — keep Luzern's thinking on AI/agentic discoverability current, and translate emerging platform and LLM behaviour into practical, sellable content recommendations.
● Alignment with SEO — partner with the SEO Executive so keyword and search strategy and content structure are aligned across traditional and AI-mediated discovery.

Testing & Performance Monitoring
● A/B testing — recommend and run A/B tests (e.g. on A+ Content, Brand Store, imagery and messaging) to determine the most effective executional approach, rather than relying on opinion or precedent.
● Monitoring set-up - set up monitoring using Compass (or equivalent) to measure content effectiveness and implementation.
● Reporting on impact — track and report on content performance against strategy objectives, feeding learnings back into future audits and strategy.

Creative Briefing & Review
● Strategic foundation - develop the strategy and messaging that underpins paid social, display and
marketplace advertising content.
● Creative briefs - write and own briefs for Designers producing static and video ad assets, translating strategy into clear creative direction.
● Creative review - review creative output against the brief, brand guidelines and platform requirements before client delivery.

Client Management
● Client-facing delivery - present content strategy, recommendations and audit findings directly to client stakeholders.
● Estimates & scoping - prepare estimates and scopes of work for content workstreams.
● Briefs — shape and write content and creative briefs in response to client requirements.
● Feedback management — manage client feedback through to resolution, balancing client expectations against strategy and platform best practice.
● Proposals — contribute to and help prepare proposals and pitch content for new and existing client business.

Quality & Output Review
● Senior review — review the SEO Executive's and Designers' work before it is sent to the client, checking it against strategy, brand guidelines and platform requirements.
● Direction — give feedback and direction to keep output consistent and on-strategy.

AI-Enabled Working
● AI as a working method — use AI tools proficiently for content and competitive audits, for generating recommendations, and for producing or accelerating creative and written content — not only as a subject of strategy.
● Continuous improvement — identify and recommend where AI tools can improve the speed or quality of content production and audit work across the team.

Requirements

What You Bring to the Role

● Proven experience in Amazon content strategy and execution (listings, A+/Premium A+ Content, Brand Store, Amazon Posts), ideally within an agency or managed services environment.

● Working knowledge of content requirements across at least one other marketplace or major retailer platform (e.g. Tesco, Zalando, Otto) and D2C.

● Experience running content audits — analysing reviews, search terms, AI-generated summaries and customer/AI-agent queries — and scoring content quality (e.g. IDQ or equivalent) against best-in-Class standards.

● Experience translating audit findings into content strategy: comms objectives, key messaging, messaging hierarchy, and content requirements for imagery and copy.

● Experience developing or briefing A+ and Brand Store wireframes and mock-ups, working closely with designers.

● Experience designing and running A/B tests to determine the most effective executional approach, and setting up performance monitoring (e.g. Amazon Compass or equivalent) to track results.

● Strong understanding of how AI assistants and platform shopping agents (e.g. ChatGPT, Rufus)surface and rank product content, and how content should be structured to support this.

● Confident, credible client-facing communicator — comfortable presenting strategy, leading feedback conversations, and owning estimates and proposals.

● Experience briefing creative teams for paid social/display advertising, across both static and video formats.

● Demonstrable, hands-on use of AI tools for research, auditing and content production, not just familiarity in principle.

● Strong copywriting and content editing skills, with a close eye for brand and platform compliance.

● Comfortable reviewing and giving constructive feedback on the work of SEO and design peers.

Desirable

● Experience across multiple international marketplaces or retail media platforms.

● Familiarity with SEO fundamentals, to collaborate effectively with the SEO Executive.

● Experience contributing to new business pitches or proposals.

● Category experience relevant to Luzern's enterprise brand client base.

Benefits

What We Offer
● Competitive salary and benefits
● Hybrid Working Model
● Great working environment with a passionate, collaborative team
● Continuous learning & career development
● The opportunity to work with some of the world's leading brands across the most exciting marketplaces

We are committed to equal opportunities and welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates. If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.

About DFYNE:

A picture paints a thousand words… and we’re sure you don’t want to be sat here reading an essay of corporate “about us” spiel…. Seriously, how’re you able to really get under the skin of what we’re about from a few words on a screen. So why don’t you have a look and see what we’re all about for yourself - www.dfyne.com.

About the role - DFYNE Your Career:

First off, it's best I introduce myself (person behind the keyboard here). It’s not the norm on a job advert, but I think it’s important you get introduced to who you might be working with for a long time early on.

I'm Luca, Chief Financial Officer at DFYNE, and I'm looking for someone who can help us continue building a world-class finance function as we scale globally.

This isn't a traditional management accountant role where you'll only focus on month-end reporting from a distance. We're looking for someone who takes ownership of accurate and timely management accounts while remaining hands-on across accounts payable, fixed asset management, lease accounting, financial controls, and commercial analysis.

You'll be responsible for ensuring financial information is reliable, insightful, and delivered on time, whilst maintaining strong processes that keep the day-to-day finance operation running smoothly. You'll partner with teams across the business, challenge costs where appropriate, identify risks and opportunities, and support the continued growth of DFYNE through sound financial management.

Attitude:

  • Ownership mentality
  • Detail obsessed
  • Commercially curious
  • Problem solver
  • Calm under pressure
  • Continuous improvement mindset


Key Responsibilities

1. Management Accounts & Month-End Reporting:

  • Prepare monthly management accounts, including profit and loss, balance sheet, and supporting schedules, to agreed deadlines.
  • Post and review accruals, prepayments, depreciation, amortisation, and other month-end journals; maintain clear supporting working papers.
  • Complete and review balance sheet reconciliations, investigate differences, and resolve outstanding items.
  • Analyse actual results against budget, forecast, and prior periods, explaining material variances and cost trends to management.
  • Support budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, and improvements to management reporting.
  • Ensure accurate cut-off, allocation of costs to departments and cost centres, and completeness of month-end liabilities.
  • Work with the Finance Team Lead on audit preparation, financial controls, and process improvements.


2. Fixed Assets & Right-of-Use (ROU) Asset Accounting:

  • Maintain and reconcile the Fixed Asset Register (FAR), ensuring accurate accounting for capital expenditure (CapEx), additions, disposals, and depreciation calculations.
  • Manage Right-of-Use (ROU) asset schedules and lease liabilities in accordance with relevant accounting standards (IFRS 16 / FRS 102), ensuring monthly lease interest and depreciation journals are accurately posted.
  • Review purchase invoices and CapEx requests to ensure correct capitalisation treatment versus operational expense (OpEx).
  • Perform periodic physical asset verifications/audits and reconcile asset register balances to general ledger control accounts.
  • Prepare lease schedules, impairment reviews, and disclosures for month-end and year-end statutory audit reporting.


3. Daily Finance Inbox & Invoice Control:

  • Manage and clear the finance inbox daily, with visible Processed/Actioned and pending categories to support seamless handovers.
  • Register 100% of incoming invoices in NetSuite within two working days and maintain visibility of future payment liabilities.
  • Verify supplier invoice details, dates, values, and UK VAT treatment; accurately code invoices to general ledger accounts and cost centres.
  • Assess expenditure for value for money; query unexpected charges with department heads and place unresolved invoices on hold.


4. Reconciliations & Financial Control:

  • Regularly review and cleanse the accounts payable ledger, resolving aged balances, unapplied payments, and debit notes.
  • Reconcile supplier statements, the AP sub-ledger, fixed asset registers, lease schedules, and the general ledger before month-end close.
  • Keep AP postings aligned with bank payment schedules and investigate discrepancies promptly.
  • Maintain accurate, audit-ready records and comply with applicable HMRC VAT and record-keeping requirements.


5. Specialist Logistics Accounting:

  • Process outbound shipping invoices weekly, clearing relevant inbox items before posting; post matching journals on the same day for accurate cost-centre reporting.
  • Register returns logistics invoices on receipt, complete checks using the available checker, and post required journals.


Experience Needed:

  • AAT-qualified, part-qualified ACCA/CIMA, or qualified by experience with substantial relevant responsibility.
  • Demonstrable hands-on experience preparing monthly management accounts and completing month-end close.
  • Practical experience in maintaining fixed asset registers, calculating depreciation, and managing capital expenditure accounting.
  • Strong practical accounts payable experience, including high-volume invoices, supplier reconciliations, and payment runs.
  • Experience with NetSuite or a comparable cloud ERP; sound Excel skills for reconciliations and reporting.


Skills:

  • Understanding of lease accounting principles and Right-of-Use (ROU) asset management under IFRS 16 or FRS 102.
  • Confident with journals, accruals, prepayments, balance sheet reconciliations, and variance analysis.
  • Good understanding of UK VAT, HMRC documentation requirements, general ledger coding, and financial controls.
  • Organised, accurate, and commercially aware; comfortable challenging costs and working independently to deadlines.
  • Able to communicate effectively with department heads, suppliers, and senior finance colleagues.


So, what’s in it for you?:

If you’ve made it this far down without being put off, brilliant, I’d love to hear from you. Besides a work family and a great place to work, you’ll have an opportunity to grow with the company, be a part of the journey, and have a vital input into helping continue the crazy growth we’ve already seen.

You’ll be part of a high challenge, high reward culture.

tem is rebuilding the energy transaction - transparent, fair and built on trust. Behind that mission is a company growing fast, and a Performance team that's already lean and stretched. Core People operations needs more firepower as we scale, and there's a direct commercial angle too: a strong People Operations function is what lets new joiners ramp up and become productive faster once they arrive.

This is a multi-disciplinary People Operations role at the centre of the employee lifecycle - equal parts operational delivery, automation and continuous improvement. You'll be the reliable hands keeping People processes running as we scale, from multi-country payroll to onboarding, employee changes and offboarding. You'll also build the tools, automations and lightweight AI workflows that connect our systems (Rippling, Notion, Linear, Slack, Ashby, n8n and Google Workspace), so the function doesn't need to double in size every time headcount does.

In your first 12 months, you might:

  • Take ownership of payroll across our UK and employer-of-record employees, keeping every cycle accurate and on time as pay schedules and countries multiply.

  • Become the trusted point of contact for employees and managers, owning their queries through to resolution.

  • Build the automations and AI-enabled workflows that remove repetitive manual work from the employee lifecycle.

  • Turn recurring pain points into better processes, tools or self-service, and measure whether they actually worked.

  • Move across People disciplines as priorities shift - reward and benchmarking, pensions and options administration, performance cycles, engagement and people data.

🛠️ Responsibilities

  • Run payroll end to end: own monthly payroll across UK and employer-of-record employees - changes, corrections, off-cycle and ex-gratia payments, contractor payroll and invoicing, and country-specific items - keeping it accurate and on time as we add pay schedules and countries.

  • Keep the lifecycle running: deliver core People operations across onboarding, employee changes, contracts and documentation, leave, mobility (visas and international moves), EOR and contractor setup, and offboarding, flexing into whatever the business needs most.

  • Be the trusted point of contact: own employee and manager queries through to resolution with a clear response standard, rather than passing them between functions.

  • Keep the foundations accurate: maintain employee data, documentation and systems so that everything else can depend on them.

  • Automate the repeatable: build and maintain automations and lightweight AI-enabled tools, workflows and agents that connect Rippling, Notion, Linear, Slack, Ashby, n8n, Google Workspace and similar, and remove repetitive manual work - with controls so speed never costs accuracy, privacy or employee trust.

  • Own the People tech stack: evolve our People technology ecosystem - evaluate emerging tools, consolidate where we can, and simplify the architecture.

  • Improve continuously: turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service, measure whether they worked, and give foundational People processes a named owner and a runbook someone else could follow cold.

  • Design to delight and to scale: we treat our people like top athletes and aim to delight at every step of the employee journey, and what works at today's size shouldn't need twice the People team when headcount doubles - default to eliminating or automating work rather than administering it.

  • Partner across the business: work with Finance, Legal, Talent, Performance Partners and functional specialists to turn People initiatives into scalable services, and build dashboards and lightweight analysis that help the team and the business make better decisions.

✅ Requirements

Must-Haves

  • You've worked in People Operations, People Services, HR Operations or another operational People role - generalists welcome - and you hold a high bar on accuracy and confidentiality.

  • You've run payroll cycles end to end, ideally multi-country, in-house or through an employer of record. UK fundamentals (PAYE, RTI, pension auto-enrolment, statutory payments) are familiar, or clearly learnable fast if your payroll experience comes from another market.

  • You're highly comfortable with technology: AI is part of how you work, you actively experiment with new tools and capabilities, and you can build automations through no-code or low-code tools, integrations and AI workflows.

  • You think in systems and workflows rather than individual tasks, with a strong instinct for simplification ("why are we doing this manually?"), and you're comfortable using data to diagnose problems and make decisions.

  • You operate effectively in ambiguity, without waiting for a perfectly defined process or remit, and you balance efficiency with empathy - People Operations is about people, not just workflows.

  • Strong ownership instincts: when something's broken, unclear or inefficient, your instinct is to fix it, and you're willing to move across People disciplines depending on where the organisation needs you.

Desirable

  • Breadth across the People remit beyond Operations - reward and benchmarking, pensions, benefits, or performance and engagement. This role is deliberately multi-disciplinary.

  • Familiarity with the basics of UK and EU employment law, and experience administering equity or share options (for example EMI or unapproved schemes, and cap-table tools such as Vestd).

  • Experience supporting international employment through employers of record, and setting up or managing contractors (including off-payroll and IR35 awareness).

  • Experience in a fast-scaling startup or scale-up, especially through a period of doubling headcount or entering new countries.

🎁 Benefits & Perks

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

  • Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,400 per year for your remote setup.

  • Up to GBP150 or EUR170 per month for wellbeing.
